stories.title: 11 teams selected for National Children's Science Congress:Senior team scores 94, junior team 90; to participate in state-level competition in November
stories.summary: Eleven teams from Varanasi have been selected for the state-level event in the district-level competition of the National Children's Science Congress 2026. The competition was held on 28 October at Sant Atulanand Convent School in Koirajpur. Around 300 child scientists and 150 guide teachers participated in the event. This year's main theme was 'Science and Innovation for Sustainable Development'. The sub-themes included waste management, energy, water conservation, food, agriculture and health, and the use of Indian knowledge traditions for sustainable development. In the senior category, the team from Subhash English School, Bhagwanpur, scored 94 points, while two teams in the junior category scored 90 points each. Focus on five topics, from waste management to water conservation This year, the main theme of the National Children's Science Congress was 'Science and Innovation for Sustainable Development'. Participants had to prepare projects on five topics. Reducing and reusing waste, saving energy and finding new methods; water harvesting and conservation; improving food, farming and health; and finding new avenues for development by using traditional Indian knowledge. Six teams selected in the junior category Six teams were selected in the junior category. The teams from International Hindu School and St Atulanand Convent School, Koirajpur, scored 90 points each. They will participate in the state-level competition in November The selected teams will participate in the state-level National Children's Science Congress, to be held on 27, 28 and 29 November. The chief guest at the programme was DIET Principal and Deputy Education Director (Secondary) Umesh Kumar Shukla. School secretary Rahul Singh chaired the event. It was organised under the leadership of district coordinator Girish Kumar Singh, with the support of programme in-charge Sankatha Prasad Asthana. Projects were evaluated by BHU district academic coordinator Professor PC Abhilash and his team, along with judges from UP College. The organisers wished the selected students success in the state-level competition.

stories.title: Akash Anand changes stance after return:Calls Rahul ‘confused leader’ after earlier addressing him as ‘uncle’; why hold all 3 rallies in western UP?
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) national coordinator Akash Anand struck a more assertive note in Bulandshahr on August 28, launching sharp attacks on the BJP, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. He made it clear that he would not hesitate to target any political party. At a rally in Sadabad, Hathras, Anand had referred to Akhilesh and Rahul as “uncles”. This time, he described Rahul Gandhi as a “confused leader”. BSP seeks to establish itself as an independent political force Akash Anand’s more aggressive tone after his return to the party sends two clear signals. First, the BSP does not want to position itself solely as an anti-BJP force in the next Assembly elections. Second, it wants to present itself as an independent political alternative, distinct from both the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress. Jatav voters remain central to BSP’s strategy in western UP Anand has held all three public meetings in western Uttar Pradesh. He understands that if the BSP’s Jatav voters unite again, they could help the party regain some of its lost political strength. Dalits account for 21% of Uttar Pradesh’s population, of whom Jatavs make up 12%. In several constituencies in western UP, Jatav voters account for 25% to 30% of the electorate. Three key political messages in Akash Anand’s speeches Three clear messages emerged from Anand’s speeches: Akash Anand seeks to clear confusion among BSP workers Akash Anand pledged to make sacrifices for the Bahujan movement, saying he would not rest until the Bahujan community secured a share in political power. He also recalled asking Mayawati about the reason for his expulsion from the party. According to Anand, he assured Mayawati that he was ready to fight for the Bahujan mission until his last breath. Senior journalist Syed Qasim said Anand’s statement was an attempt to clear up confusion among party workers. His expulsion had triggered a strong reaction from workers this time. By referring to the reason for his expulsion, Anand also tried to explain to party workers that the episode should be seen as a test of his patience and restraint. Why Akash Anand called Rahul Gandhi ‘uncle’ in Sadabad and a ‘confused leader’ in Bulandshahr On August 10, Akash Anand launched the BSP’s election campaign for Mission 2027 in Sadabad, Hathras. He delivered a speech lasting around 57 minutes. His strategy in Sadabad appeared to have two parts. First, he raised issues concerning young people and students to target the BJP government. Second, by referring to Akhilesh Yadav and Rahul Gandhi as “uncles”, he turned the generational gap into a political message. Through this approach, Anand appeared to be trying to establish himself not merely as a young leader from Mayawati’s family, but as a voice of the younger generation. In Bulandshahr, Anand went a step further by attacking the Congress and Rahul Gandhi. He alleged that despite being in power for a long time, the Congress was now raising questions about public issues. He called Rahul Gandhi a “confused leader” and accused him of not being sufficiently active in movements related to reservation and the rights of disadvantaged communities. Anand also took a dig at Rahul Gandhi for carrying a copy of the Constitution. He said that merely talking about the Constitution and reservation was not enough; leaders must also take to the streets in support of these issues when necessary. According to senior journalist Ratanlal Mani, Anand knows that a large section of Dalit voters backed the SP-Congress alliance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The BSP’s challenge ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections is to bring its core voters back into its fold. By attacking Akhilesh Yadav and Rahul Gandhi together, Anand has attempted to sharpen the BSP’s political agenda and distinguish the party from both the NDA and the Opposition alliance. BJP government faces the sharpest criticism in Bulandshahr At a rally in Bulandshahr on October 28, Akash Anand launched a sharp attack on the BJP government. In his roughly 40-minute speech, he devoted around 20 minutes to criticising the BJP. He linked issues such as education, employment and security to the government’s advertising expenditure. He alleged that the government had spent around Rs 7,000 crore on s over the past 10 years to improve its image, while claiming it had no money to fill vacant government posts. Raising the issue of youth unemployment, Anand claimed that 1.3 million government posts were vacant in Uttar Pradesh. He also questioned the state of education, the condition of government schools, paper leaks, women’s safety and hospital facilities. He cited the deaths of children in a hospital fire in Jhansi. Anand also questioned the quality of expressways and roads, referring to projects where potholes appeared soon after inauguration. In contrast, he cited the Agra-Noida Expressway, built during Mayawati’s government. Through these examples, Anand sought to argue that development should not be judged by s and inaugurations alone, but by construction quality and how well projects stand the test of time. What does Anand’s attack on the SP’s PDA slogan signify? One key shift in Anand’s Bulandshahr speech was his attempt to portray the Samajwadi Party (SP) not merely as an Opposition party challenging the BJP, but also as a political rival competing for Dalit votes. He questioned Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA slogan, which stands for Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak (backward classes, Dalits and minorities). He alleged that the SP uses its political messaging to bring different social groups together. Anand referred to the “chavanni” (25 paise coin) jibe directed at Jayant Chaudhary. Citing Chaudhary Charan Singh and Mulayam Singh Yadav, he questioned the SP’s politics of social justice. He also raised the issue of district names being changed during the SP government’s tenure. His central argument was that the past decisions and political conduct of a party that speaks of respecting Dalits, backward classes and other communities should also be scrutinised. In this way, Anand sought to strengthen the BSP’s political base among social groups that have been drawn towards the SP through its PDA campaign. Akash cites Mayawati government’s achievements to position BSP as a contender for power The rally held on August 25 in the Jewar area of Gautam Buddha Nagar was also significant for the BSP’s strategy. After the SP and BJP held show-of-strength events in Dadri, the BSP organised a workers’ conference in Dankaur, Jewar. At the event, Akash Anand announced Satvir Gurjar as the party’s candidate for the Jewar Assembly seat. Anand’s speech focused on rebuilding the party’s organisation and public support in the region. The announcement of a candidate from the Gurjar community was also seen as part of this strategy. In Bulandshahr, Anand devoted around 15 minutes of his roughly 40-minute speech to highlighting the work carried out during Mayawati’s four terms as chief minister. Referring to the Savitribai Phule Education Scheme, he claimed that more than 700,000 girls had benefited from it, with over Rs 600 crore spent on the initiative. He also mentioned the construction of universities, ITIs, schools and colleges, as well as engineering, homeopathy, polytechnic and paramedical institutions. Anand also presented figures relating to schemes for Scheduled Castes and backward classes, Ambedkar villages, land allotments to landless families, teacher recruitment, sanitation workers’ appointments, police recruitment and government employment. Through these figures, he sought to show that the BSP government had taken steps to improve education, social dignity and employment opportunities. According to senior journalist Syed Qasim, Anand is using the achievements of Mayawati’s government to encourage voters to compare the BSP’s record with the performance of SP and BJP governments. He is seeking to once again position the BSP as a strong contender for power and restore confidence among party workers.

stories.title: Hospitals sealed after deaths, unsealed after bribe:ACMO demands ₹3 lakh to reopen closed hospital in UP
stories.summary: Patients die because of wrong treatment, while cases of rape and murder have also been reported inside hospitals. Health department officials seal such facilities, but within days, some of these tainted hospitals reopen under new names after payments are made. This amounts to officials putting patients’ lives at risk for money. To expose this alleged racket, the Dainik Bhaskar team conducted an investigation in Lucknow, Kanpur and Unnao in Uttar Pradesh. Bhaskar reporters posed as hospital operators and approached officials. A responsible officer and a clerk allegedly negotiated a deal to reopen sealed hospitals in exchange for bribes. They also explained how the sealed facilities could obtain a clean chit and resume operations. Undercover reporter approaches Unnao health official to negotiate reopening of sealed hospital The Dainik Bhaskar investigation team received information about Uttam Hospital in Unnao. The hospital’s operator, Devkant Uttam, was accused of kidnapping, abortion and murder in the case of a 22-year-old student. In July 2026, the district administration and health department sealed the hospital. To negotiate a deal to reopen the sealed hospital under a different name, a Bhaskar undercover reporter met Additional Chief Medical Officer (ACMO) Dr Narendra with the hospital’s documents. Posing as the hospital operator, the reporter discussed the deal with officials and staff, from a clerk to the ACMO. Reporter: “A hospital has been sealed, and we want to run it.” Dr Narendra: “What is the name of the hospital?” Reporter: “Uttam Hospital… Has the lease been finalised?” Dr Narendra: “Under what name will you run it?” Reporter: “We will change the name and run it as you suggest.” Dr Narendra: “All right, write down on paper what you will pay.” Reporter: “How much should we write?” Reporter: (Writing Rs 2.5 lakh on a piece of paper) “Sir, this is the amount I was told here.” Dr Narendra: “What name will you give the hospital?” Reporter: “I have thought of a few names… It will be done for Rs 2.5 lakh, right?” Dr Narendra: “Let’s see. We’ll speak to the CMO.” Reporter: “Sir, it won’t cost more than Rs 2.5 lakh, will it?” Dr Narendra: “I’ll speak to them. We’ll have to increase it a little.” Reporter: “How much more will we have to pay?” Dr Narendra: “You’ll have to make it at least one lakh more.” Reporter: “So, it will be done for Rs 3.5 lakh?” Dr Narendra: “Yes. Write down the name and give it to me.” Reporter: “I was considering Shagun or RPM.” Dr Narendra: “The CMO has gone to Bombay. We can’t discuss all this over the phone. Once he returns, the work will be done. By the way, what is your relationship with the hospital operator?” Reporter: “I’m not related to him. I’m taking over the entire hospital, including its equipment, on rent. Sir, please make sure everything is handled properly so that the hospital is not sealed again.” Dr Narendra: “Just do what you’ve been told. If you manage things properly, everything will be fine.” During the conversation, Unnao ACMO Dr Narendra said that local people would have to be managed so that no one interfered in the matter. When asked whether the hospital could operate under its old registration, he said a new registration would be required. He also suggested ways to pay off complainants to keep them quiet. During the investigation, the team received information about IPS Hospital in Chinhat, Lucknow. The Chief Medical Officer (CMO) sealed the hospital in May 2026 after a 22-year-old woman died following allegedly improper treatment. A Bhaskar reporter took the sealed hospital’s documents to the CMO’s office in Lucknow, where he met ACMO Dr Akhand Pratap Singh, who oversees private hospitals. Dr Singh discussed reopening the hospital under a different name. Reporter: “A hospital has been sealed, and we want to reopen it.” Dr AP Singh: “A new one?” Reporter: “Yes, we’ll add something new to it and operate it.” Dr AP Singh: “What do you do?” Reporter: “I deal in medicines and property.” Dr AP Singh: “What is the hospital called?” Reporter: “IPS Hospital.” Dr AP Singh: “Oh, the one in Chinhat, right?” Reporter: “Yes. We’re taking it over after changing its name.” Dr AP Singh: “But the location will remain the same, won’t it?” Reporter: “That’s not a problem. Please arrange the registration.” Dr AP Singh: “There will be a problem, won’t there? Look, it’s sealed, so there will be some difficulties.” Reporter: “We’ll change the name completely.” Dr AP Singh: “All right. Meet Sanjeev Babu. Go ahead; I’ll let him know.” The clerk said, “Reach a settlement with the husband of the woman who died.” After the conversation, Lucknow ACMO Dr AP Singh sent the reporter to a clerk named Sanjeev. He also called Sanjeev to brief him about the matter. When the investigation team reached Room No. 13 at the CMO’s office, they met Sanjeev, who discussed the full deal to reopen the sealed hospital building under a new name. Reporter: “Dr AP Singh must have called you just now.” Sanjeev: “Yes. Tell me, what do you need?” Reporter: “A hospital has been sealed, and we want to reopen it under a different name.” Sanjeev: “Which hospital is it?” Reporter: “IPS Hospital.” Sanjeev: “IPS is closed.” Reporter: “Yes. Another hospital next to it was also closed, but it is now operating under a different name.” Reporter: “We’ll manage everything else.” Sanjeev: “Don’t reopen it immediately. His lawyer is pursuing the matter, and another letter has arrived.” Reporter: “If I manage the lawyer, will it be possible?” Sanjeev: “Reach a settlement with the complainant, Sanjay Yadav.” Reporter: “I’ll take care of that. Don’t worry about it.” Sanjeev: “Manage that first, and then proceed with this.” Reporter: “I’m taking the hospital on lease.” Sanjeev: “Get all the paperwork done and manage everything. Your work will be completed.” Reporter: “Fifty per cent of the paperwork is done. You just manage things here.” Sanjeev: “Yes, you manage that. Otherwise, he’ll start getting reports published in the newspapers.” ACMO says, “Get a lease agreement prepared” After speaking to clerk Sanjeev, the reporter returned to ACMO Dr AP Singh. Dr Singh asked him to get a lease agreement prepared. He said the entire process would be carried out afresh and the hospital’s name would also be changed. He added, “Run it in your own name; his name should not appear.” When the reporter asked about the expenses, Dr AP Singh said— Reporter: “Sir, I’ve spoken to him. He said he would get the work done for a lower amount.” Dr AP Singh: “All right, you see to it.” Reporter: “So, should I deal directly with him?” Dr AP Singh: “Yes, go ahead. There’s no problem.” Reporter: “But, sir, I won’t be able to pay more than Rs 2 lakh because the rent is also high.” Dr AP Singh: “How much is the rent?” Reporter: “Rs 1.5 lakh.” Dr AP Singh: “But the problem is that the hospital is sealed.” Reporter: “Sir, please get it done. I’ll take care of the rest.” Dr AP Singh: “All right.” Reporter: “Please give me your number. We’ll talk on WhatsApp.” Dr AP Singh: “Write it down: 941545XXXX. You can contact me on this number.” Reporter: “All right, sir. I’ll call you on WhatsApp.” Clerk negotiates the payment After the conversation with ACMO Dr AP Singh, Sanjeev met the reporter again. The reporter said an agent had earlier demanded Rs 4 lakh for the same work. Sanjeev replied that he could get it done for considerably less. He asked the reporter to get the lease documents prepared. Reporter: “I’ll handle the outside work myself. You tell me what needs to be done here.” Sanjeev: “Don’t speak to anyone else now. Bring the documents, and then I’ll tell you.” Reporter: “If you could give me some details, I could prepare accordingly.” Sanjeev: “We’ll stand by you. There won’t be much trouble.” Sanjeev: “Don’t call, boss. The situation is very sensitive right now.” Reporter: “All right. We’ll meet and discuss it.” Reporter: “I’m getting the lease papers prepared.” Sanjeev: “They had asked for Rs 4 lakh. We’ll get it done for 50% less.” ACMO asks reporter to visit office over WhatsApp call to discuss payment A day later, the reporter called ACMO Dr AP Singh on WhatsApp and said, “Sir, I have to pay Sanjeev Babu. I’ve discussed everything with him. At your suggestion, he has agreed to Rs 2 lakh.” Dr AP Singh then told the reporter to come to his office and meet him instead of paying Sanjeev directly. Chandra Hospital in Kanpur is now operating under the name Veda Hospital A Chandra Hospital previously operated on Shivli Road in Kanpur but is now running under the name Veda Hospital. During the investigation, we found a notice issued by the Chief Medical Officer (CMO), Kanpur, on January 31, 2024, directing that the hospital be sealed. The investigation found that treatment continued at the hospital despite the sealing order. On June 10, 2025, Ramdas, a resident of Rasoolabad, lodged an FIR against the hospital and its operators, alleging that his son died because of improper treatment at the sealed facility. The complaint also alleged that the hospital was operating an ICU and an operation theatre (OT) without the health department’s permission. A case was registered under the SC/ST Act and Sections 351(3), 352, 115(2) and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Doctors Mohit, Shivam and Mukesh were named as accused. After the matter came to light, the hospital shut down once again. However, about a month later, Veda Hospital began operating in the same building, replacing Chandra Hospital. To contact Mukesh, a reporter visited the hospital on the pretext of obtaining an estimate for a kidney stone operation. Reporter: Will you examine the patient yourself, or will someone else do it? Mukesh: No, we won’t examine the patient. The urology doctor will. This is our hospital. Reporter: Was it previously known as Chandra Hospital? Mukesh: Yes, it was called Chandra Hospital earlier, but our Ayushman application was rejected three times. In such cases, we have to apply again under a new name. That is why the name was changed. Reporter: What do you charge for delivery? Mukesh: If you get it done here, the charges are very reasonable. A caesarean delivery costs just Rs 14,000 at our hospital. A normal delivery costs Rs 8,000. Reporter: Are you a doctor too? Mukesh: Yes, I’m also a doctor, but I’m a plain MBBS graduate. FIR was filed against the hospital in 2025 Questions also arise over Mukesh’s claim that he is a doctor. A notice issued to the hospital in 2024 alleged that it did not have qualified doctors. In the FIR filed in 2025, three people were named as accused, but the title “Dr” appeared only before Mohit’s name. Neither Shivam nor Mukesh was identified as a doctor. The FIR was filed just a year ago. Modern Life Hospital sealed three times and renamed four times in two years We received information about a hospital in Kalyanpur, Kanpur, that had been sealed three times and renamed four times within two years. The Chief Medical Officer’s (CMO) office revealed that the same building housed New Life Hospital in 2024. It was run by Neeraj and Raju Rathore. The hospital was sealed because it did not have a registration. It was then renamed Grace Hospital, but Raju Rathore continued to operate it. After running for a few months, Grace Hospital was also sealed, and its name was changed to KPS Hospital. It was operated by Imtiyaz Ahmed and Prince Dwivedi. Imtiyaz Ahmed was accused of raping a nurse who worked at the hospital. The hospital was subsequently sealed. It has now been renamed Modern Life Hospital. Following this lead, the Bhaskar investigation team visited Modern Life Hospital. To get an estimate for an appendix operation, the team spoke to Pradeep, who claimed to be a doctor. Reporter: Is this KPS Hospital? Receptionist: (Looking towards the operator) Sir… Operator: What do you need to discuss? Reporter: Actually, a man had a kidney stone operation here earlier. Now he needs an appendix operation. He told me this was the hospital in the area. He had met someone named Prince here. Operator: We are running it now. Reporter: Oh, so Prince is no longer here? Operator: Prince is still here, but he visits occasionally. I’m here most of the time, though Prince keeps coming. Reporter: Can I get an estimate for the operation? Operator: Yes… The operator then took the reporter inside. Operator: Who sent you here? Reporter: He lives in Swaroop Nagar. Operator: All right. Did he get treatment here, or is he a doctor? Reporter: He received treatment here. Operator: He said he used to visit this building earlier. He told you that people recover after getting treatment here. Operator: How old is the patient? Reporter: Around 46. Operator: All right. We’ll conduct the tests first. The approximate cost will be Rs 20,000–22,000. Sealing hospitals accused of serious violations appears to be little more than a paperwork exercise The Dainik Bhaskar investigation found that officials in the health department appeared to place little value on patients’ lives. Sealing hospitals following cases involving murder, rape and deaths has seemingly become little more than a paperwork exercise, with some facilities allegedly resuming operations under different names. When those responsible for protecting the public are accused of striking deals with such hospitals, public safety is left at risk. It remains to be seen whether action will be taken against the officials responsible following these revelations, or whether the familiar cycle of investigations will continue.

stories.title: Akash Anand returns to political arena:Holds rally in Bulandshahr, says he asked Mayawati why she keeps expelling him from the party
stories.summary: After returning to the BSP for the fourth time, Mayawati's nephew Akash Anand held a public rally in Bulandshahr for the first time. The rally took place on Wednesday afternoon at 1:45 pm in Khalor, Anupshahr. On stage, Block Pramukh Manoj Pradhan presented Akash Anand with a golden crown. Manoj has joined the BSP after leaving the BJP. Akash Anand said, “Rahul Gandhi is ahead in taking credit. The Congress and the BJP are two sides of the same coin. Akhilesh uncle is older in age. His PDA changes colour like a chameleon.” During this, Akash declared Manoj Pradhan as the candidate from Anupshahr, and former block pramukh Mukesh Pandit, who joined the BSP after leaving the RLD, as the candidate from Shikarpur. Prior to this, Akash had held a public rally in Jewar on 25th August. Now read the key takeaways from Akash's statements 1- Behanji said how can I hand over the reins without a test Behanji had punished me. She told me to sit at home now. I asked her why she tests me every time. She asked whether Baba Saheb and Kanshi Ram Ji were tested until their last breath or not. I said, yes Behanji. Then Behanji said how can I hand over the reins to you without a test? Hearing this, tears came to my eyes. I said that I am ready to take the test until my last breath. I am ready to renounce my family to make society my family. I assure Behanji that I consider only the Bahujan society as my family. Bowing my head, I thank Behanji. 2- BJP government is spending only on s Behanji keeps giving messages to you all through tweets. I have come to warn you about the reality of the BJP government that has been running for the last 10 years. The BJP government praised itself falsely through s and spent Rs 7,000 crore. A safe and educated UP is shown in s. But the reality is that there is no money to fill the 13 lakh vacant posts in government departments. They do not have money to stop paper leaks. 10 children died in a fire at a government hospital in Jhansi. They do not have money to improve arrangements there. 3- Congress-SP have nothing to show Baba Saheb had said that the SP and Congress are alike. One is Nagnath, the other is Sampnath. In the last elections, these people came together. Showing the book of the Constitution, they said we will do this, we will do that. These people have nothing to show you. Rahul Gandhi is so confused that when the agitation took place in Delhi, he jumped into it. Instead of guiding the youth, he himself joined the agitation. The ally parties also jumped in along with the Congress. The poor youth suffered the lathi charges. Under the rule of the government of the very party that took credit for that agitation, a similar attitude was adopted towards youth in another state. 4- SP changes colour like a chameleon Akhilesh uncle is older than us in age. We will joke about it later. When the SP was in government, these people did such work that exposed their double standards. Behanji has said that just as a chameleon changes colour, the SP also changes colour. Sometimes the letter 'P' in PDA stands for Pandit, and sometimes it becomes Pichhda. Akhilesh used abusive language for a leader of the Jat community. Will they insult and forget Chaudhary Charan Singh, owing to whom Mulayam Singh became Chief Minister for the first time? Upon coming to power, Akhilesh Yadav changed the name of Kanshi Ram Nagar to Kasganj, Mahamaya Nagar to Hathras, and Ramabai Nagar to Kanpur Dehat. 5- People from BJP will come to ask for votes again, but do not give them People from the BJP will come to you again and say give us your vote. We will work for your community. But do not vote for them. People still remember the law and order during Behanji's tenure. During Behanji's tenure, no riot ever took place. At that time, no one dared to harass any sister or daughter. 6- Three thousand murders occurring every year under BJP rule Akash said—There is jungle raj in UP under the BJP's rule. Annually, three thousand cases of murder come to light. More than 65 thousand cases of atrocities against women and daughters are registered. Annually, over 10 thousand cases of robbery and extortion are registered. Is this the safe Uttar Pradesh? Is this the safe India? 7- They make a spectacle by asking rapists to limp The BJP government has run a narrative that it is a government that conducts encounters. When a rape accused is caught, he is brought before the media as a spectacle. Whispering in his ear, he is told to limp as the media is in front. If a crime like rape is a joke to them, does such a government have the right to remain in power? 8- BJP government closed down 25 thousand schools Over the last 10 years, I searched extensively, but I could not find any new school. Contrarily, these people closed down 25 thousand schools in 10 years. They do not have money to fill 1.5 lakh vacant posts for teachers. More than 2 crore youth are roaming unemployed. If the government wishes, it can fill the 13 lakh vacant posts tomorrow itself. They want to keep our children illiterate and unemployed. 9- BJP has neither intention nor intellect People in the BJP are ahead in cutting ribbons. Whether a road is built or a hospital, they remain ahead in performing inaugurations. They will say that we built the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway, which caved in at more than 80 places in 18 days. Sinkholes deeper than 15 feet appeared on the Purvanchal Expressway. The Bundelkhand Expressway caved in just 5 days after its inauguration. The Ganga Expressway was inaugurated in April. In August, that too caved in at several places. The Agra-Noida Expressway built during Behanji's tenure stands as it was even today. The BJP government has neither the intention nor the intellect to do anything for our society. In 2014, they gave the slogan—Enough of the inflation hit, this time BJP government. Their slogan should be—Inflation hitting the public, the responsible BJP government. Akash listed Mayawati's achievements Akash said that Behanji had run the Savitribai Phule Education Scheme. Under this, Rs 600 crore was spent to provide free education to 7 lakh children. She established 6 engineering institutes, 2 homoeopathic institutes, 2 paramedical institutes, 6 universities, and over 200 ITIs. She granted 27% reservation to OBCs in government hostels.

stories.title: Fire breaks out during gas refilling in Varanasi:Cylinder blast reported; fire brigade rushes to the spot
stories.summary: On Wednesday, a powerful explosion occurred in a shop near a railway crossing in the Shivpur police station area of Varanasi during the alleged illegal refilling of a gas cylinder. The blast was so strong that reports emerged of its sound being heard nearly 2 kilometres away. Following the explosion, high flames of fire began rising from the shop. This caused chaos in the area. Upon receiving information about the incident, police and fire brigade teams arrived at the spot. The teams launched relief and rescue operations. According to initial information, no casualties have currently been reported in the accident. See 3 pictures… Now read the full details In the Shivpur police station area, on the west side of Sonkali Balika Inter College, there is a row of shops along the road connecting the railway crossing to the highway. There are about a dozen shops here. The very last shop is said to belong to Sanjay Tiwari, where gas cylinders and stoves are sold. Information has emerged that a gas cylinder blast took place in this exact shop. Explosions occurred at intervals of about 10–15 minutes According to eyewitnesses, three cylinders exploded during the incident. About 10 to 15 minutes after the first blast, the second cylinder burst. It has been reported that roughly 10 minutes after that, the third cylinder exploded as well. The consecutive explosions created chaos in the area. Police and fire brigade teams arrived at the spot and launched relief and rescue operations. Suspected illegal refilling, administration steps up investigation According to initial information, the explosion occurred during the illegal refilling of a gas cylinder in the shop. However, official confirmation of the causes of the incident and facts related to the refilling will only be possible after the investigation. The administration is investigating the matter. It is being reported that under the guise of a stove repair centre, illegal gas refilling was taking place on a large scale in the shop.

stories.title: Where did BJP go wrong in UP MLC elections?:How SP won 2 seats; ‘Teachers’ group’ wiped out in teachers’ polls
stories.summary: The wind appears to be blowing in favour of the Samajwadi Party (SP) in the Uttar Pradesh MLC election. The SP has taken the lead in two seats in this election among teachers, adding heat to the contest . The SP won three seats in the previous election. For the first time in five decades, not a single candidate from the 'Teachers' Group' has won in the teachers' election. The SP has taken the lead in areas considered to be strongholds of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), including Varanasi, Agra and Prayagraj. Although the SP's Sanjayan Tripathi did not win in Gorakhpur, the SP made the contest difficult there by fielding a BJP rebel against him. Wherever the SP and BJP contested against each other, the margin was not wide. The results show that while the teaching community may not have rejected the BJP, it has certainly accepted the SP. The BJP is also moving towards formulating a fresh strategy. The BJP Uttar Pradesh state working committee meeting in Lucknow on 30 October is certain to discuss the opposition's lead in the MLC election. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya also said, "The SP won in places where it was not supposed to win..." Read where the BJP fell short in this election... The Samajwadi Party won the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers' Constituency and Agra Teachers' Constituency seats. Independent candidates had been elected as MLCs from both seats in the previous election. In Gorakhpur, a candidate from the Sharma faction won, while the Agra seat went to an Independent. The BJP's tally neither increased nor decreased. In the 2020 election, too, the BJP had won six seats. Who won and who fell behind? Teachers' MLC seat Graduate MLC seat Find out where the BJP went wrong in choosing its candidates After the results, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to BJP office-bearers. They themselves admit that there was a lapse in the selection of candidates. Understand it in 4 points: Teachers believed leaders from the ruling party or Opposition would listen to them The teachers' faction, which had maintained its dominance in the Legislative Council elections for five decades, has been wiped out. No teachers' group won in 2026. The teachers themselves rejected the teachers' factions. The reason is understandable. Teachers believe that only someone from either the ruling party or the Opposition can get their demands accepted. Dhruv Kumar Tripathi, an MLC from the Teachers' Group, has also joined the BJP. The council now has only one member left from the Teachers' Group-Raj Bahadur Singh Chandel. He was elected from the Kanpur Teachers' Constituency. The Teachers' Group held sway in the council for nearly five decades. Its MLCs were regarded as the voice of financially unaided teachers in the state. Yadavs leave the Samajwadi Party in Gorakhpur-Faizabad On the Gorakhpur-Faizabad seat, the Samajwadi Party withdrew the ticket of its announced candidate, Kamlesh Yadav, and fielded Sanjayan Tripathi instead. However, the election results show that the seat's Yadav voters did not accept this decision by Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav. The Yadav voters of Gorakhpur-Faizabad chose independent candidate Rajeev Yadav instead of Samajwadi Party candidate Sanjayan. The consolidation of Yadav votes in Rajeev's favour kept him in the contest. BJP pays the price for relying on state and district teams Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath campaigned in the Agra, Bareilly, Varanasi, Gorakhpur and Lucknow constituencies. The BJP won most of these seats. Only the Lucknow Graduates' seat and two seats in Varanasi slipped away. However, resentment and factional equations were more influential here. The BJP suffered its biggest setbacks in seats where the elections were left to the state and district teams. Most of the office-bearers are new and have little experience of managing elections. The party won where the reins remained in capable hands. Election Commission Put in the Dock This is the first time that shortcomings in the Election Commission have come to light in a Legislative Council election. The Commission had to acknowledge its mistake and take corrective action. It had to replace the observer for the Gorakhpur-Faizabad seat and hold repolling at three booths for the Agra Teachers' seat. Political analysts believe that the Opposition will now intensify its allegations against the Commission until the Assembly elections. BJP sweeps teacher seats, SP rides one-sided wave on graduate seats Teacher seats: Bareilly-Moradabad- BJP's Dr Hari Singh Dhillon defeated the Samajwadi Party candidate by a wide margin of 17,676 votes, the biggest winning margin on the teacher seats. Meerut-Saharanpur- BJP's Shrichand Sharma won by a wide margin of 13,241 votes. Lucknow- BJP's Umesh Dwivedi secured victory by 4,808 votes. Gorakhpur-Faizabad: The contest here was extremely close, with the BJP's Dr Dhruv Tripathi securing victory by a narrow margin of just 307 votes. SP's margin: The SP won the Varanasi seat by 5,025 votes and Agra by 4,263 votes-limited margins compared with the BJP's decisive victories. Graduate seats: Allahabad-Jhansi: The SP's Dr Mansingh Yadav defeated the BJP candidate by a massive margin of 27,663 votes, the largest vote margin in the entire election. Lucknow: The SP's Kanti Singh left the BJP far behind with a strong lead of 12,225 votes. Varanasi: The SP's Ashutosh Sinha defeated the BJP's heavyweight candidate by 7,195 votes. BJP's margin: In the graduate category, the BJP won the Meerut-Saharanpur seat by 12,855 votes and the Agra seat by 8,856 votes. Defectors won the election In the Legislative Council election, Shikshak Dal candidate Dhruv Kumar Tripathi's decision to join the BJP and independent candidate Akash Agrawal's decision to join the Samajwadi Party proved beneficial. In the prevailing circumstances, it would not have been easy for either Dhruv Kumar, contesting from Shikshak Dal, or Akash Agrawal, contesting as an independent, to win. However, Sanjayan Tripathi, who rebelled against the BJP and joined the Samajwadi Party, did not gain much on the Gorakhpur seat. There was a reason for this too. Akhilesh Yadav had travelled to Ballia to attend the thirteenth-day ceremony of his party leader Ram Govind Chaudhary. On his return, he was scheduled to address a meeting in Deoria. During the meeting, he forgot the name of Sanjay Tripathi, who was standing beside him. He asked Sanjay Tripathi his name and then appealed to the people through the microphone to vote for him. In such a situation, it can be said that Sanjay Tripathi did not receive the support of the Samajwadi Party cadre. Moreover, at the last moment, the Samajwadi Party cancelled Kamlesh Yadav's ticket and gave it to Sanjayan Tripathi. It is therefore being speculated that if the Samajwadi Party had not changed its candidate, the Yadav vote would have gone to the SP. Sanjayan Tripathi, meanwhile, would have contested as an independent candidate and cut into the BJP's vote. The SP's path here could have been easier. SP prevails with Kurmi candidates on the Lucknow Graduates' seat In the contest between Kurmi candidates for the Lucknow Graduates' constituency, Kanti Singh and her husband, SP Singh, proved stronger. Although the entire BJP cadre was campaigning for sitting MLC Avnish Singh Patel, state president Pankaj Chaudhary and Jal Shakti Minister Swatantra Dev were also personally putting in their efforts. However, the Kurmi leaders of the Awadh region could not win over 50,000 Kurmi voters. The constituency had the highest number of voters at 3,13,531. Voter turnout was 38.02%. Teachers chose Kanti Singh to raise their voice for their rights. Kanti Singh is the wife of Samajwadi Party MP from Pratapgarh, Shivpal Singh Patel. Kanti has become an MLC for the second time. In 2014, she won the MLC election from the Lucknow Graduates' constituency on an SP ticket. In 2020, the BJP wrested the seat from the SP. The BJP maintained a strong hold in western Uttar Pradesh The Samajwadi Party once again failed to make any significant mark in the MLC elections in western Uttar Pradesh. There were five seats in western Uttar Pradesh in all. These included two seats from the graduate and teachers' sections in the Meerut-Saharanpur division, two seats from the graduate and teachers' sections in the Agra division, and one seat from the teachers' section in Bareilly-Moradabad. The SP won only the Agra graduate seat, while the BJP retained the other four seats. The BJP won both seats in Meerut and the Bareilly-Moradabad teachers' seat. In Meerut, the victory margin on both seats was more than 12,000 votes, while in Bareilly-Moradabad, the BJP candidate won by 17,676 votes. In Agra, meanwhile, BJP candidate Manvendra Singh, also known as Guruji, won the graduate seat by around 11,000 votes. Fielding a Muslim candidate did not work The Bareilly-Moradabad seat is considered Muslim-majority. However, this was an election for the teachers' section, where the numbers are mixed. The Samajwadi Party had fielded Muslim candidate Danish Akhtar from this seat, but he lost by a wide margin of 17,000 votes. SP retains its lead in Purvanchal-Bundelkhand The BJP has suffered a setback in Varanasi. The SP has won both seats here. Lal Bihari Yadav won the teachers' constituency, while Ashutosh Sinha emerged victorious in the graduates' constituency. The SP had held both these seats previously as well. These seats cover half of Purvanchal. The region covers Varanasi, Chandauli, Ghazipur and Jaunpur districts in the Varanasi division; Azamgarh, Ballia and Mau in the Azamgarh division; and Mirzapur, Sonbhadra and Bhadohi districts in the Mirzapur division. The Samajwadi Party also won the highest number of seats in this belt in the 2022 Assembly elections and the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Maan Singh won the graduate constituency seat of the Jhansi-Allahabad division. He had previously been an MLC from here as well. Two distinct pictures emerged in the MLC elections. The BJP won the teachers' constituency seats by a wide margin, while the Samajwadi Party dominated the graduate constituency seats.

stories.title: Gangster Dharmendra Tiddi, carrying ₹1 lakh bounty, killed in Ghaziabad:Encounter with SOG near Niwari Ganga Canal; three policemen also injured
stories.summary: Ghaziabad Police have gunned down Dharmendra 'Tiddi' alias Bawariya, a criminal carrying a reward of ₹1 lakh on his head, in an encounter. The encounter took place on Wednesday evening at 6:30 pm on the Gang Canal track in the Niwari area. A total of 15 rounds of bullets were fired from both sides during the encounter, in which Dharmendra was hit by two bullets. Additional DCP (Crime) Piyush Singh said that Dharmendra, a resident of Bashi village in Amroha, used to commit dacoities in Ghaziabad and Baghpat. Ghaziabad and Baghpat Police had been searching for him for the past one year. Three policemen—Vineet, Amit, and Himanshu—sustained gunshot injuries. They have been admitted to the hospital for treatment. See 2 pictures… Dharmendra used to commit crimes by changing his identity Police Commissioner J. Ravinder Goud stated that information about Dharmendra was received from an informer. Under the leadership of Additional DCP (Crime) Piyush Singh, a team from the Crime Branch was deployed on the Gang Canal track. Meanwhile, Dharmendra was seen approaching on a motorbike. When the police signalled him to stop, Dharmendra opened fire on the team. In retaliatory firing, he was also hit by two bullets. The police team admitted him to a private hospital for treatment, where Dharmendra died. A pistol has also been recovered from the spot. Dharmendra alias Tiddi was a notorious criminal of the Bawariya gang. The Ghaziabad and Meerut police had declared a reward of ₹50,000 each for his arrest. In this way, there was a total reward of ₹1 lakh on his head.

stories.title: UP electricity bills to fall in November with 9% discount:Lower power purchase and fuel costs will bring down bills
stories.summary: Electricity consumers in Uttar Pradesh will receive a 9.17% discount on their November electricity bills. The relief will be provided under the Fuel and Power Purchase Adjustment Surcharge (FPAS). Domestic, commercial and other categories of electricity consumers will benefit from it. According to the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL), consumers will benefit from the lower actual cost of electricity procurement and fuel. Relief has been provided on electricity bills for five consecutive months, from July to November. 4.43% relief in July, 9.17% in November According to UPPCL, consumers have received relief under the FPAS for the past four months. The relief was 4.43% in July, 2.92% in August, 7.93% in September and 5.24% in October. It has now increased to 9.17% in November. Consumers to benefit from lower electricity procurement costs Under the FPAS mechanism, consumers are given the benefit when the actual cost of electricity procurement and fuel is lower than the estimated cost included in the tariff. UPPCL is providing relief on electricity bills under this mechanism. UPPCL said that efforts were being made across the state to improve consumer services while ensuring reliable, high-quality power supply.

stories.title: ‘Without Modi you won’t have a tilak on your forehead':Swatantra Dev Singh speaks in Lakhimpur, Keshav says police earlier feared criminals
stories.summary: In Lakhimpur Kheri, Minister Swatantra Dev Singh said that if one abandons Modi-Yogi, the tilak on his forehead will not remain. “If you feel safe today, it is because of Yogi Ji. Even if your child is stranded in Australia, Modi Ji brings them back to India,” Swatantra said. “Therefore friends, leave everything behind. Leave casteism, regionalism, individualism, dynastic politics, and lineage politics behind. Look at only one thing—nationalism. Otherwise, the tricolour flag will not flutter at Srinagar Square,” Swatantra said. Meanwhile, Deputy CM Keshav Maurya said that earlier, the police used to fear criminals, rather than criminals fearing the police. In fact, a Kabir Mahotsav was organised at Kabir Dham in Gola Gokarannath on Wednesday. Speaker of the Lok Sabha Om Birla and Minister-in-Charge Nitin Agarwal also arrived here to attend it. After taking part in the programme, Minister Swatantra Dev and Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla will depart for Lucknow at 4:30 pm. They will reach Lucknow at 5:40 pm. In view of the VIP movement, police forces have been deployed on all routes.

stories.title: ED attaches property of Azam Khan’s Jauhar University:Land and buildings have a market value of ₹1,170 crore
stories.summary: The Lucknow Zonal Office of the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has provisionally attached the land and buildings of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University linked to senior Samajwadi Party leader and former cabinet minister Mohammad Azam Khan. According to the ED, the attached properties are valued at ₹426.46 crore, while their estimated market value is around ₹1,170 crore. The action was taken in a money-laundering case. The ED said Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust operates Jauhar University. Azam Khan founded the trust and is its principal trustee. The university campus is located in the Jauhar Nagar area of Rampur. The agency has alleged that proceeds of crime, obtained through irregularities involving government funds, money received from contractors and land-related matters, were used to build the university's properties.

stories.title: UP to open Jan AI cafés in 25 districts:Govt will set them up over the next 12 months to help people access welfare schemes
stories.summary: JanAI cafes will be opened in 25 districts in the eastern part of Uttar Pradesh to bring artificial intelligence (AI) to the general public. Aavishkaar Foundation, Head Held High Foundation and JanAI Technology Private Limited signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) for this at Sankalp Bharat 2026. Under the agreement, one cafe each will be established in the selected 25 districts over the next 12 months. These cafes will enable rural families, young people, women, farmers and small entrepreneurs to use AI in their own language. The aim is to help people access information about government schemes, explore employment opportunities and start new businesses. Access to government schemes and employment with the help of AI JanAI cafes will serve as centres for local residents, where trained operators and JanAI ambassadors will help people use AI technology. Through these centres, people will be able to handle everyday tasks, access government schemes, explore employment and market-related opportunities, and advance their business ideas. Through this initiative, the plan is to connect AI technology with local needs, strengthen people's livelihoods and economically empower families. Each of the three organisations will have separate responsibilities As part of the project, JanAI Technology Private Limited will provide its multilingual AI platform. Head Held High Foundation, meanwhile, will be responsible for recruiting and training JanAI ambassadors. In addition to helping local residents use AI, these ambassadors will identify the problems, needs and available opportunities in the area. Aavishkaar Foundation will connect young people with entrepreneurship through its Youth Entrepreneurship Programme. According to the organisation, the programme has so far reached more than 60,000 students across 1,000 schools and colleges. It aims to reach 10 lakh students by 2030. Under the new partnership, students will also receive support through GenAI tools to develop their business ideas and launch enterprises. Districts to be selected based on local needs The scheme will be implemented in phases. Local needs and available opportunities will be taken into account while selecting and prioritising districts. The three organisations will jointly prepare a framework for café locations, district-level partnerships, links with government schemes, ambassador training and the use of technology. The outcomes of the scheme will also be assessed. Focus on making entrepreneurship easier Avishkar Foundation CEO Lisa Rodrigues said the organisation aims to make entrepreneurship an accessible route to economic progress in eastern Uttar Pradesh. The partnership could help young people and local entrepreneurs turn their ideas into businesses and gain access to the necessary networks and capital. JanAI Technology Private Limited co-founder and CEO Vishwesh Pai said AI can bring about effective change only when it understands people's needs in their language and provides practical solutions. Meanwhile, Head Held High Foundation Managing Trustee Madan Padki said the real benefits of AI emerge when it helps young people access opportunities, entrepreneurs secure livelihoods, farmers make better decisions and families avail themselves of government schemes. AI-based model to be developed in 25 districts The three organisations want to develop these 25 districts as AI models based on people's needs. Under the plan, the technology will be linked to local institutions, employment and entrepreneurship opportunities so that its benefits can reach villages and small towns. The success of the initiative will be assessed based on the extent to which the use of AI improves people's livelihoods, employment and economic opportunities.

stories.title: Three people lose ₹1.46 crore in fraud in Lucknow:Fraudsters take ₹86 lakh for land and swindle ₹59.46 lakh through an investment scheme
stories.summary: Three cases of fraud have come to light in Lucknow's Gudamba area, where people were lured with offers of land and profits on investments. A real estate businessman from Madiyaon was defrauded of ₹86 lakh on the pretext of arranging four bighas of land in Barabanki. In another case, a retired Agriculture Department employee and his brother-in-law were defrauded of ₹59.46 lakh after being promised a monthly profit of 7.5% on their investment. ₹86 lakh transferred after showing four bighas of land In a complaint filed with the police, real estate businessman Vishvendra Vikram Singh, a resident of Pritinagar in Madiyaon, said he met jeweller Rahul and his father, Girish Chandra, residents of Harinaam Market in Gudamba, in November 2024. The two offered to arrange land at a low price. They subsequently showed him four bighas of land in Fatehpur, Barabanki. After he liked the land, the deal was finalised for ₹86 lakh. According to Vishvendra, they transferred ₹86 lakh into the accounts of the father and son between 11 December 2024 and 21 October 2025. The accused had said they would register the land four days later. It is alleged that on 22 October, they discovered that the land shown to them belonged to someone else. The victim alleged that the accused threatened to kill him when he asked for his money back. After no action was taken despite a complaint to the police, he approached the court. According to the ACP, Ghazipur, Gudamba police registered a case and began an investigation on the court's orders. Promised 7.5% monthly profit Narayan Verma, a retired Agriculture Department employee from Gayatripuram in Gudamba, said Manoj Sharma, who lived opposite his house, used to visit him. Around a year ago, Manoj introduced him to Gaurav Shukla, Anuj, his wife Priya, Satish and Neeraj. It is alleged that they lured him with the promise of profits if he invested in various schemes, including the Portcure Cap company. According to Narayan, when he initially refused to invest, the accused assured him of a monthly return of 7.5%. He subsequently invested ₹40,46,647 in the company on 7 May 2025. It is alleged that he received neither any profit nor a refund of the principal amount. Brother-in-law also cheated of ₹19 lakh Narayan Verma alleges that the accused similarly took ₹19 lakh from his brother-in-law, Brijendra Singh. When the money was not returned, the two filed separate complaints at Gudamba police station, but no action was taken. They subsequently approached the court. In all three cases, the victims approached the court, accusing the police of failing to hear their complaints. On the court's orders, Gudamba police registered three cases.

stories.title: Astrologer Indu Prakash’s wife loses MLC election:Predicts others’ futures but failed to foresee his wife’s electoral fate
stories.summary: Smita Mishra, wife of astrologer Acharya Indu Prakash Mishra, faced defeat in the Lucknow Division Graduate MLC election. Acharya Indu Prakash, who makes predictions, could not change his wife's electoral fortunes. Smita Mishra campaigned extensively to win the election, but the result did not go in her favour. Smita Mishra joined the Congress on 28 September. She became a member of the party in the presence of state Congress president Ajay Rai. She was subsequently assured that the Congress would declare her its candidate for the Lucknow Division Graduate seat. However, just a few days later, Ajay Rai was removed as state president. The new president, Aradhana Mishra 'Mona', decided not to contest the MLC election. Despite this, Smita Mishra continued to contest the election as an independent candidate. She did not even receive 300 votes. Indu Prakash Mishra Trolled Over Wife's Defeat Smita Mishra left no stone unturned in campaigning for the election. She reached out to graduates, young people and those associated with educational institutions. She also placed full-page s in newspapers as part of the campaign. Despite this, she could not win the election. During the election campaign, she had also received the support of various social organisations, including Nav Yuvak Dal, Karni Sena and the local Brahm Samaj. Following her defeat, people have been heavily trolling astrologer Acharya Indu Prakash Mishra. They are taking digs at him, asking how an astrologer who predicts the future for others failed to foresee his wife's electoral prospects. He also tells people about various remedies and rituals to protect themselves from problems, so why did he not tell his wife about them? However, Smita Mishra herself said that she had not asked the astrologer anything about her electoral prospects. People associated with different political parties visit him and have achieved success by following the rituals or remedies he recommends, but I did not contest the MLC election for power or office. My intention was to serve the public and work for charitable causes. Key Predictions on Indu Prakash Mishra's Website The website Acharya Indu Prakash dot com mentions seven major predictions. Find out what Smita Mishra said about her defeat After losing the Lucknow Graduates' MLC election, independent candidate Smita Mishra raised questions about the election process. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, she alleged that booth capturing had taken place during the election. Her agent was not allowed to sit inside the polling station. Officials reprimanded the agent in front of her and threw him out. Smita Mishra said she had prepared for the election for two years. She visited schools and colleges in 37 tehsils to reach out to teachers, students and graduates. Despite this, the administration did not allow votes to be cast for her supporters, and several people were prevented from voting. She also alleged irregularities in the electoral roll and bogus voting. Smita Mishra said, "Our agent was reprimanded and thrown out right in front of us. The SDM said, 'Which rule book says that an agent will sit inside the polling booth?' Our agent was not allowed to sit there. The entire election was influenced." Smita Mishra also alleged the use of money in the election. She said there had been complaints that money was given to some voters to secure their votes. She questioned, "When educated people are voting in a graduates' constituency, what more can I say?" '22,000 online forms were submitted, but names were not added to the voter list' Smita Mishra also questioned the process of preparing the voter list. She said her supporters had filled in around 22,000 forms online. According to her, despite these forms being submitted, no clear response was received about adding the names to the voter list. Citing the example of Ikra village in Barabanki, she claimed that the voter list included the names of some people who had no connection with the village. When I complained about this, I was told that the portal had now been closed. I filed more than 100 complaints with the Election Commission, but did not receive a response to even one of them. 'We trusted the BJP, but will now contest against it in 2027' Smita Mishra said that she had once trusted the BJP, but had been disappointed by alleged irregularities in the election. She said that her party, Navyuvak Dal, would now field at least 50 candidates in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. She said, "Our party was formed in 2014. We held protests during the Nirbhaya case. The need now is to contest elections through our own party. Talks are under way with several people." She said that several organisations, including Karni Sena, had supported her during the election campaign. She would speak to them as well. Smita Mishra said that despite losing the election, her social work would not stop. Through the IP Foundation, work to provide education in schools, help teachers and guide students would continue. Her opposition to the UGC would also continue. She said she would continue to run a public campaign against it. Smita Mishra comes from a freedom fighter's family Smita's parental home is in Kurari village in Unnao district. Her husband is astrologer Acharya Indu Prakash Mishra. They have one son and two daughters. Their daughters live in Canada, while their son lives in Gurugram. Her in-laws' home is in Ikra village in Barabanki district. Smita Mishra's Ramsundar Nath Shukla was a police officer and received 26 medals. He also received a special award allowing him to attend parades in uniform for as long as he lived. Her grandfather, Shambhu Ratan Shukla, was a freedom fighter and an associate of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.

stories.title: Man slits girlfriend's throat in Kushinagar:Enters her room, stabs her repeatedly; angry over her marriage being fixed elsewhere
stories.summary: Man allegedly broke into his girlfriend's house in Kushinagar and slit her throat with a knife, killing her. He stabbed her repeatedly, severing her neck. She died on the spot. The woman was engaged to another man, which had angered the accused. At around 8.30 pm on Tuesday, he entered the house and went to the woman's room on the second floor. Before anyone could understand what was happening, he locked the room. Hearing the commotion, family members rushed to the spot. Meanwhile, when the boyfriend tried to flee, villagers caught and beat him before handing him over to the police. The woman was Muslim, while the accused was Hindu. In view of the tension, police forces have been deployed in the area. The incident took place in the Hata Kotwali area, around 12 km from the district headquarters. Read the full story… Roshni alias Rukhsana (18) was the youngest of three children in the family of Alham Ansari, a resident of Belwa Sudama village. His wife is Razina Khatoon. Their elder daughter, Mehrunnisa, is married, while their son, Abdul, is studying. Roshni had studied up to Class 12 but discontinued her education two years ago. She had been in a relationship for around three years with Surjeet (20), a resident of nearby Jhanga Bazaar village. Surjeet worked as a painter in Mumbai. Roshni's family did not approve of the relationship because they belonged to different religions. They had therefore arranged her marriage to another man. Following this, Roshni reduced contact with Surjeet. He was upset about this and was pressuring her to elope with him, but she was not willing to do so. Mother says he had threatened the family several times after returning from Mumbai According to Roshni's mother, Razina Khatoon, Surjeet had returned to the village from Mumbai around a month ago. She alleged that he had visited their house several times and threatened the family. On Tuesday night, Surjeet came straight to their house. He climbed the stairs in the veranda to reach the second floor, where her daughter's room was located. The two argued initially. Her daughter raised an alarm, shouting that he had come to kill her. Surjeet then shut the room's door and repeatedly stabbed Roshni in the neck, severing it. Villagers break down door and catch accused After the incident, screams filled the house. Hearing the noise, people from the neighbourhood rushed to the spot. As the room was locked, villagers broke down the door and found Roshni lying in a pool of blood. The accused tried to escape by pushing people aside, but villagers chased and caught him. They beat him before the Hata Kotwali police arrived and took him into custody. He was injured and was sent for medical treatment. SP Keshav Kumar reached the spot. The forensic team collected evidence from the scene. The police took custody of Roshni's body and sent it for a post-mortem examination. Tension in village, police from three stations deployed Roshni's death has plunged the family into grief. Her relatives are inconsolable. In view of the tension following the incident, police personnel from three police stations have been deployed in the village. The ASP and the CO of Kasya are also present at the spot. SP Keshav Kumar said, There was a romantic relationship between the two. He was upset because the girl's marriage had been fixed elsewhere. The accused has been arrested and is being questioned.

stories.title: Uproar at Allahabad High Court:Bar Association writes to Chief Justice, warns of court boycott if no action is taken
stories.summary: A case of vandalism on the Allahabad High Court premises has come to light. The High Court Bar Association has written to the Chief Justice, seeking action in the matter. The association alleges that a lawyer was threatened with being sent to jail and was made to apologise to a police officer in court. The Bar Association has warned that it will boycott the judge's court if appropriate action is not taken. According to the letter written by the Bar Association on 27 October, the judge's court has a provision for separate chairs for police officers and other senior officials. It is alleged that, during the hearing, an officer of Superintendent of Police (SP) rank was sitting in the row behind the Additional Government Advocate (AGA). A lawyer then told the officer that it was not his seat and that he should sit at the back. According to the letter, the Additional Government Advocate reprimanded the lawyer over the matter and said he would complain to the judge. Later, when the judge arrived in court, the Government Advocate complained against the lawyer. The Bar Association alleges that the judge then pointed a finger at the lawyer and said he would send him to jail. When the lawyer apologised, he was also asked to apologise to the police officer. The association also alleged that comments were made about a senior advocate present in the court. Describing the matter as one concerning the dignity of advocates, the Bar Association has sought the Chief Justice's intervention. The association has said that it may boycott the judge's court if appropriate action is not taken.

stories.title: ₹35 crore vanishes from PNB accounts in Noida:Customers shocked by zero balances; bank manager among 5 suspended
stories.summary: Around ₹35 crore has reportedly gone missing from accounts at a Punjab National Bank (PNB) branch in Greater Noida. Customers who had opened fixed deposits (FDs) are seeing zero balances in their accounts. Meanwhile, customers who had ₹3–4 lakh in their savings accounts are now left with just ₹16,000. The money has also gone missing from accounts of people who received ₹1 crore and ₹29,000 in government compensation. Around 18 people who visited the bank with similar complaints have approached the police. Following their complaints, Beta-2 police station has registered an FIR. After the matter came to light, PNB's regional office in Sector 1, Noida, suspended five employees, including the bank manager. New staff have been appointed in their place. Bank officials have assured customers that their money will be credited back to their accounts by Thursday. However, it is still unclear whether the money was stolen from the bank, went missing due to some other irregularity, or was siphoned off through a digital heist. The bank has not issued any official statement on the matter. An investigation is currently underway into the alleged negligence and irregularities by bank employees. The anti-corruption team is also probing the case. The incident took place at the PNB branch in Aichhar village. How the case came to light Money allegedly transferred to another account in the name of mutual fund investments Vineet Bhati, a transporter living in Aichhar village, visited the PNB branch in Sector Pi-1 on Tuesday. He runs a firm called Jai Shiv Transport and holds a current account with the bank. He said he had approached bank employees to invest in mutual funds. On the branch manager's instructions, he signed a cheque and the relevant brochures. However, instead of transferring the investment amount to his savings account, the money was sent to another account. Although the account was reportedly in Vineet Bhati's name, he said it did not belong to him. On Tuesday, he submitted a complaint at Beta-2 police station, demanding an investigation into the bank employees and the return of ₹25 lakh. Meanwhile, five to six account holders present at the bank began creating a commotion, bringing the matter to light. Here are the accounts of some customers whose money has gone missing. Over ₹1 crore missing from ₹1.29 crore received as compensation Brijesh said his mother's land had been acquired for the Noida airport project. In compensation, around ₹1.29 crore had been credited to his account. The family had withdrawn only ₹15 lakh from this amount. Now, more than ₹1 crore is missing from the account, and the balance is showing zero. They demanded KYC documents whenever I tried to withdraw money An elderly man, Dharamveer, said, “I have ₹17.5 lakh in my account. The bank has not even allowed me to make a single entry for the past two years. I have been badly cheated. Sometimes they would close my account, sometimes they would claim my PAN card was defective, and at other times they would ask me to complete Aadhaar KYC. “I came to the bank yesterday. I had ₹17.5 lakh in my account, but the manager showed me that there was no money in it. My grandmother has an account with ₹61 lakh in it. I don't know whether that money is still there either. I also have a fixed deposit of ₹2.25 lakh. I wonder if that is still there.” Bank account empty, what should we do now? Santosh, an elderly woman sitting outside the bank with her sister, said, “I received ₹1.29 crore. She received the same amount. We are sisters. “We withdrew some money, and the rest was still in the account. Now, ₹1.18 crore of our money has gone missing. The balance is showing zero. The bank staff are not telling us anything. They are not saying a word. When we ask them, they say they have only recently joined. “My children are living in rented accommodation, and my house is under construction. I have no other means left. My daughter was in hospital. We received ₹32 lakh from her father's retirement benefits, but that money was spent on her treatment. She passed away, and that money is gone too. We don't have even a single rupee left. “Then, a month later, my mother-in-law also passed away after being unable to bear the shock of my daughter's death. We have been completely ruined. Now our bank accounts are empty too. Where will we live? What will we eat?” Bank official said, ‘I will lose my job, so don't come again’ Saroj said, “We received ₹1.29 crore as compensation. We withdrew ₹10 lakh in cash and had ₹20 lakh transferred. When we asked to withdraw more money from the bank, the woman official said there would not be that much available and asked us to come back later. “When we returned, she said we should inform the bank two days in advance if we needed a large amount, and they would provide it then. We subsequently got ₹20 lakh transferred to one account. When we visited again a few days later, the woman official said, ‘Brother, don't come again. I will lose my job. A CBI investigation is underway, and a large amount of public money has come in.’ We now have ₹76 lakh left.” Money missing from several account holders' accounts Shrichand said, “We had fixed deposits worth around ₹1.16 crore in the bank. This money has been misappropriated. Several account holders in Biraundi Chakrasenpur and nearby areas have faced similar fraud.” Two fixed deposits belonging to a man named Kartari were allegedly tampered with, involving ₹9.87 lakh and ₹6.89 lakh. A further ₹10.34 lakh was allegedly misappropriated from Amichand's fixed deposit. More than ₹1 crore has gone missing from Vijaypal's account, over ₹1 crore from Subhash's account and around ₹1.18 crore from Santosh's account. Around ₹88 lakh has reportedly gone missing from Bijendra Singh's account and ₹25 lakh from his fixed deposit. Approximately ₹90.43 lakh has allegedly been misappropriated from Ranpal's account. Around ₹40 lakh is missing from Hanif Khan's account, ₹1.07 crore from Sonu's account, ₹23 lakh from Jagdish's fixed deposit and ₹80 lakh from Sunita's fixed deposit. 16 people file complaints, five bank employees suspended The police said 16 people had filed complaints related to the bank so far. Five employees, including the bank manager, have been suspended in connection with the case. Bank representatives have assured account holders that their money will be returned. Meanwhile, investigations into the alleged misappropriation and negligence are ongoing. The police and the anti-corruption team are examining different aspects of the case. The bank has not yet issued an official statement on the matter.

stories.title: Sexual harassment case:Brij Bhushan gets final chance to respond, next hearing on November 20; women wrestlers challenge his discharge
stories.summary: The Delhi Rouse Avenue Court heard at 11 a.m. on Wednesday an appeal against the acquittal of former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) president and former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and former secretary Vinod Tomar in a case related to the sexual harassment of women wrestlers. The court gave Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh a final opportunity to file his response. His lawyer appeared online and sought a week to file the response. The special judge, granting the final opportunity, scheduled the next hearing in the case for 20 November. On 9 October, Special Judge Digvijay Singh of the MP/MLA Sessions Court, while hearing the case, directed Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh to file his response by 28 October. The court had said that the digital record of the entire court proceedings conducted in the lower court from beginning to end, in a pen drive, should be made available to the petitioning wrestlers, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, Vinod Tomar and the Delhi Police. The court had also asked Delhi Police whether it would file an appeal against the decision, to which the police had sought time to respond. Wrestlers filed petition a month and a half later The Rouse Avenue Court acquitted Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and Vinod Tomar on 3 August. Nearly a month and a half later, on 28 September, the women wrestlers filed an appeal in the Sessions Court against the acquittal. The wrestlers had alleged that the lower court selectively and erroneously assessed the evidence on record and that its decision was based merely on assumptions and speculation. The petition also argued that the decision relied on stereotypical assumptions about the conduct of victims of sexual harassment, which is not legally justified. The wrestlers sought a review of the order on these grounds. They had sought a review of the lower court's decision, describing it as legally unsustainable. Brij Bhushan had said: "What Ram has ordained will happen" After the verdict, Brij Bhushan said: The judge said, "Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar, you are being honourably acquitted. I had said earlier that if any allegation was proved, I would hang myself. This is a day of happiness for me. What Ram has ordained shall happen." After the court's verdict, wrestlers Vinesh Phogat and Bajrang Punia said, "We have not lost hope. We will challenge the verdict in the High Court." This sexual harassment case came to light in January 2023.

stories.title: BJP's Umesh Dwivedi wins Lucknow teachers' seat for 3rd time:Vows to fight for teachers' honour; SP's Kanti Singh leads on graduates' seat
stories.summary: BJP candidate Umesh Dwivedi secured a hat-trick of victories in the Lucknow division Teachers' MLC seat. He expressed his gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and the party leadership. He said the BJP had fielded an ordinary teacher from a seat in a capital city like Lucknow for the third time. He was grateful to the party for this. He also thanked the lakhs of teachers who had placed their trust in him for the third time. Umesh Dwivedi said, "I assure the teachers that if I ever have to stand up to anyone for their honour, dignity and pride, I will not back down." Meanwhile, in the first round of counting for the Lucknow division Graduates' seat, Samajwadi Party candidate Kanti Singh was leading BJP candidate Avnish Singh until 1 a.m. She is currently leading by 10,000 votes. See three pictures from the victory celebrations... Kanti Singh leads in the initial trends for the graduate constituency SP candidate Kanti Singh led BJP's Avanish Singh in the initial trends of counting for the Lucknow division graduate constituency. Kanti Singh received 6,579 votes in the first round, while Avanish Singh received 4,387 votes. Kanti Singh was therefore ahead by around 2,000 votes. A total of 13,980 votes were counted in the first round. Counting for the graduate constituency is to be conducted in a total of nine rounds. After the first round, eight rounds of counting remained. BJP claims victory on all 11 seats BJP graduate constituency candidate Avanish Singh claimed that the party would win all 11 seats. He also expressed confidence that it would win the Lucknow seat by a huge majority. Responding to SP candidate Kanti Singh's allegations of irregularities, he said that the SP begins making allegations when it fears defeat. He said the party was misleading the public. Kanti Singh alleges irregularities in vote counting Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party candidate Kanti Singh expressed 200 per cent confidence in her victory. She alleged irregularities at several booths, said agents had been stopped from entering and accused officials of facilitating bogus voting. She claimed that between 1,000 and 2,000 votes had been affected. During the counting, she also alleged that bundles contained more ballot papers than they should have. Assistant District Election Officer Abhay Kishore said the counting was being conducted with complete transparency. According to him, the bundling of ballot papers in the Lucknow Division Teachers' Constituency was completed at 6 pm. The counting of the candidates' votes in the first round then began. The counting in the Teachers' Constituency is to be conducted in two rounds. Meanwhile, the bundling of ballot papers in the Lucknow Division Graduates' Constituency was under way. There are 13 candidates contesting the teachers' seat and 16 contesting the graduates' seat. Fourteen tables have been set up in each of the two halls at the rally venue for the counting. The contest for the graduates' seat is between BJP candidate Avnish Singh and Samajwadi Party candidate Kanti Singh. BJP's Umesh Dwivedi and the Samajwadi Party's Sushil Kumar were contesting the teachers' seat.
