stories.title: Gorakhpur man searching for bride for 16 years:BA graduate roams in groom's attire, says he wants to marry Urfi Javed
stories.summary: A BA graduate in Gorakhpur has been searching for a bride for the past 16 years. He often roams around dressed as a groom and says he will marry only actor Urfi Javed. Otherwise, he is ready to remain a bachelor for the rest of his life. He says he will continue waiting until Urfi agrees to marry him. He has also said that if she comes to take him, he will one day travel to Mumbai on a bicycle to meet her. Read full story below : Abhay Pandey, alias Dulhe Raja, a 35-year-old resident of Khadda in Kushinagar, leaves home on his bicycle every morning. Wherever he goes, he sets out in full bridal attire. A sehra on his head, a sherwani, a tie around his neck and towels draped over his shoulders have become his everyday look. Abhay says that after he completed his studies, his family searched for a match for several years. But no girl liked him, which is why he could not get married. Therefore, he has been travelling around dressed as a groom for 16 years, hoping that a girl will like him and he will be able to settle down. Abhay saw Urfi on social media five years ago Abhay said that five years ago, he saw model and actor Urfi Javed on social media. He was very impressed by her style. He has followed her ever since. He watches all of Urfi's videos and looks at her photos. Over time, he began to feel a connection with Urfi and decided that he wanted to marry her. Since then, he has left home every day in the hope that he will meet Urfi one day. Urfi should come by helicopter and take him away Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Abhay said that he wanted to tell Urfi Javed, "Look, your future groom is out enjoying a boat ride. So come by helicopter and take him with you." More than 30 marriage alliances fell through Abhay said that more than 30 marriage alliances had fallen through so far. Around 50 proposals also came, but the marriages could not take place for one reason or another. That is why he keeps roaming around like this. Dream of Becoming a Major Actor Abhay says he is extremely fond of acting, singing and writing poetry. His dream is to become a major actor one day. He has no idea how to enter the film industry. However, he hopes that he will definitely become an actor one day. He is currently using social media to become famous. He has accounts on Instagram and YouTube under the name Hero Abhay Pandey. He has been making and posting reels on them for the past few years. He has 37,000 followers on Instagram and 4.7 thousand on YouTube. Studied for a BA in Sociology Abhay said that he completed his BA in Sociology in Kushinagar itself. His family wanted him to become an engineer in the future. So, they enrolled him in a BTech programme, but he left his studies because he was more interested in acting.

Last day of UP PET exam today:1,372 centres under surveillance by 37,000 cameras; cheating can lead to life imprisonment
stories.summary: The Preliminary Eligibility Test (PET-2026) is being held in Uttar Pradesh today, Sunday. This is the third and final day of the examination. A total of 1,372 examination centres have been set up across 60 districts of the state. Around 35.41 lakh candidates have registered for the examination. More than 16 lakh candidates have already appeared for the examination on October 25 and 30. On the final day, 11.80 lakh candidates are registered to take the test. The examination will be held in two shifts. The first shift will run from 10 am to noon. Entry will begin at 8 am and close at 9.30 am. The second shift will run from 3 pm to 5 pm. Entry for this shift will begin at 1 pm and close at 1.30 pm. Legal action will be taken against anyone caught cheating, arranging for an impersonator to take the examination or engaging in other forms of malpractice. Those found guilty will be barred from the examination as well as future examinations conducted by the commission. Under the law, offenders may face life imprisonment and a fine of up to ₹1 crore. Monitoring through more than 37,000 cameras Control rooms have been set up at the commission's headquarters and the headquarters of all the districts concerned to monitor the examination. Examination centres will be monitored through live CCTV footage. A total of 2,744 sector and static magistrates have been deployed to ensure the smooth conduct of the examination. Around 93,738 officers and staff members have been assigned examination-related duties. A total of 37,602 CCTV cameras installed at the centres will be used to monitor the examination. One-fourth of a mark will be deducted for each wrong answer The examination will be conducted offline using OMR sheets. It will consist of 100 multiple-choice questions, each carrying one mark. One-fourth of a mark will be deducted for every incorrect answer. The question paper will include five questions each on history, geography, economics, the Constitution, general science, mathematics, Hindi, English and reasoning. There will be 10 questions each on current affairs, general knowledge, Hindi comprehension passages, and graph and table analysis. Candidates should note that biology and chemistry will not be tested as separate subject combinations. Questions on science will be covered under general science. Examination centres allotted 500-600 km away Siddharth Singh, from Jaunpur, has to travel 520 km to Mainpuri to appear for the Preliminary Eligibility Test (PET). He said, “I will have to leave home a day before the examination.” Mohammad Rehman, from Prayagraj, faces an even greater inconvenience. His examination centre has been allotted in Ghaziabad, 650 km away. These are not just the stories of two candidates but reflect the difficulties faced by lakhs of young people appearing for PET. They are struggling to decide whether to focus on their examination preparations or the time-consuming journey, as centres have been allotted 500 to 600 km away. Commission chairman says centres were allotted by computer Commission chairman Satya Narayan Sabat said, “Uttar Pradesh is a large state, with a distance of around 1,100 kilometres from one end to the other. The most suitable arrangement possible has been implemented, considering the available centres for 35 lakh candidates.” The number of candidates is higher in eastern Uttar Pradesh districts such as Varanasi, Azamgarh, Ballia and Jaunpur. In comparison, there are fewer examination centres in these areas. Meanwhile, western Uttar Pradesh has fewer candidates and more centres. Therefore, examination centres have been adjusted according to the requirements. Dainik Bhaskar asked commission chairman Satya Narayan Sabat about the issue. He said the commission takes steps to prevent cheating during examinations. Examination centres are now allocated through an automated system. As a result, some candidates have been allotted centres farther away this time. Understand in 3 points: Who was allotted a centre, where and why Passing PET is mandatory for recruitment to Group B and C posts Passing this Preliminary Eligibility Test is mandatory for government jobs recruited through the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC). Only after qualifying can candidates apply for recruitment to Group B and Group C posts. Since the admit cards were released, candidates have been demanding changes to their examination centres on social media. They argue that PET is only an initial screening test for Group B and Group C government jobs, such as lekhpal, junior assistant and village development officer (VDO). It is not a final selection examination for a job, they say, so there is no justification for making candidates travel such long distances to take it. PET candidates outnumber Sikkim's population by 5 times The three-day examination is being held in two shifts each day. The commission has set up a total of 1,372 centres across 60 districts of the state. A record 35,41,296 candidates have applied this time. An average of around 6 lakh candidates will appear in each shift, with approximately 12 lakh taking the examination each day. The total number of candidates appearing for PET is around five to six times Sikkim's population, which stands at approximately 7 lakh.

stories.title: How did SP outsmart BJP despite winning fewer seats?:If MLC election voting patterns repeat in 2027 Assembly polls, who stands to lose?
stories.summary: Despite winning one seat fewer than the BJP in the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections, the Samajwadi Party (SP) surprised everyone. The reason lies in the results of the Graduate Constituencies, where the SP won three of the five seats. Only teachers can vote in Teacher Constituency elections, but young voters play an important role in Graduate Constituency elections. The results indicate that the preferences of young voters may be changing. As a result, Uttar Pradesh’s 3.27 crore young voters have become crucial for both the BJP and the SP ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. What challenges does the BJP face, given that it was once the first choice of young and women voters? How could the voting pattern in the MLC elections change the political equation in the 2027 Assembly elections? Read on in today’s Sunday Big Story… Of the state’s 13.39 crore voters, 21%, or 3.27 crore, are aged between 18 and 29. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the victory margin was less than 5% in 131 constituencies. This means young voters could change the outcome in these seats in favour of either the BJP or the SP. Both Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and SP chief Akhilesh Yadav understand this. That is why the Chief Minister claims at every public meeting that the government has provided more than 10 lakh government jobs in 10 years. Meanwhile, the SP chief is trying to win over young voters by raising issues such as paper leaks and contractual and outsourced employment. The voting pattern among young people in the MLC elections offers signals that should put the BJP on alert. There were 11.85 lakh voters across the five MLC Graduate Constituencies. People who had graduated at least three years earlier were eligible to vote. Young people make up a significant proportion of this group. However, only 3.26 lakh voters turned out. Of these, the BJP received 1.75 lakh votes, while the SP secured 2.12 lakh. Senior journalist Yogesh Mishra says, “The figures clearly show that young voters displayed greater enthusiasm for the SP than for the BJP. This is why the SP managed to win three of the five seats—Lucknow, Varanasi and Allahabad-Jhansi. These areas fall in Purvanchal, Bundelkhand and Awadh.” Young people are often described as either supporters of a political party or those who help shape the political atmosphere. Until now, the BJP has enjoyed the support of young voters. The MLC election results indicate a change in this pattern. This can be understood by comparing the votes received by the BJP and the SP in the 2022 Assembly and 2024 Lok Sabha elections. This means the gap between the BJP and the SP in the last two elections was only around 70–85 lakh votes. West remains a BJP stronghold; Purvanchal and Awadh are causes for concern The SP performed particularly well in Varanasi, Prayagraj, Lucknow, Bundelkhand and Agra. BJP may have suffered from not fielding women candidates There were 3.26 lakh women voters across the MLC Graduate Constituencies, of whom around 1.22 lakh cast their votes. Similarly, of the 63,000 women teachers registered to vote across the six Teacher Constituencies, around 36,000 voted. The Lucknow Graduate Constituency recorded the highest number of votes cast by women. According to political observers, women voters supported the SP in the Graduate Constituencies. Women are generally considered a core vote bank of the BJP. The government runs several schemes for women, and women voters have consistently preferred the BJP in elections. The BJP did not field a single woman among its 11 candidates. The SP, however, fielded Kanti Singh from the Lucknow Graduate Constituency. This suggests that the BJP may need to change its strategy for the Assembly elections. Akhilesh Yadav has already claimed that the SP received greater support from women in the MLC elections. He has said that the SP will field more women candidates than the BJP in the Assembly elections. Suresh Bahadur Singh says MLC and Assembly elections are different. “The BJP has introduced several schemes for women. It would not be right to draw conclusions about women voters based on the MLC election pattern.” What message do the MLC election results hold for different parties? The ATEWA faction is now emerging as an influential group among teachers. Rajiv Yadav, who contested the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teacher Constituency with ATEWA’s support, gave BJP winner Dhruv Kumar Tripathi a tough fight. Sanjay Tripathi, who rebelled against the BJP and contested as the SP candidate, finished third. This indicates that voters did not accept the rebel candidate. Meanwhile, Rajiv Yadav also received support from Yadav voters, who are considered part of the SP’s core vote bank. In the Lucknow Graduate Constituency, Independent candidate Vijay Kumar Bandhu, who contested with the support of ATEWA, received more than 10,000 votes and finished third. The Azad Samaj Party, led by Chandrashekhar Azad, fielded Daksh Pratap Yadav from the Agra Graduate Constituency, but he failed to secure even 600 votes. Eight Congress leaders contested as Independents after failing to secure party tickets. Smita Mishra, wife of astrologer Indu Prakash Mishra, received only 740 votes in the Lucknow Graduate Constituency. Sanjay Rai Priyadarshi and Arvind Singh Patel, who contested the Varanasi Teacher and Graduate Constituencies, respectively, also failed to cross the 1,000-vote mark.

stories.title: Azam Khan’s university case involves ₹426 crore:ED attaches property worth ₹1,100 crore; why, and could Jauhar University face closure?
stories.summary: On October 28, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) attached Azam Khan’s Jauhar University. The agency claims that 85% of the money used to build it came from ‘proceeds of crime’. Funds from government contracts and the MLA Local Area Development Fund were also allegedly used for the university. Surprisingly, although the alleged proceeds of crime amount to ₹426.46 crore, the ED has attached property worth more than ₹1,100 crore. Why did the ED take this step? Will Jauhar University now shut down? What will happen to the students studying there? We explain in today’s UP Explainer. Question 1: If the case involves ₹426.46 crore, why was property worth ₹1,100 crore attached? Answer: In a report dated November 10, 2023, the District Valuation Officer of the Income Tax Department in Rampur stated that a total of ₹499.09 crore had been spent on purchasing land and building the university. The ED alleges that Azam Khan and the Jauhar Trust could account for only ₹72.63 crore of this amount. The remaining ₹426.46 crore was treated by the ED as ‘proceeds of crime’. Construction of the university began around 2015-16. Since then, the market value of the land and the 59 buildings on it has increased to ₹1,170 crore. However, the entire university was built using allegedly illegally earned money and illegally occupied land. Therefore, the ED attached the entire university. Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), if a property has been created using proceeds of crime, the entire property can be frozen until the court delivers its verdict, regardless of how much its value has increased. In short, the ED has not attached any additional property. The alleged proceeds of crime have been assessed at ₹426 crore, but their market value has now risen to ₹1,170 crore, which explains the higher figure. Question 2: How was ‘proceeds of crime’ allegedly used to build the university? Answer: To build the university, Azam Khan arranged for 114 parcels of land to be registered through the Jauhar Trust. According to FIRs registered against him, the land included plots belonging to farmers and Waqf properties. An investigation against Azam Khan began after the BJP government came to power in 2017. It was alleged that Azam Khan forcibly occupied farmers’ land for the university. According to an investigation report by the Rampur district administration, 45 plots covering around 34 acres of enemy property in Singhan Khera village were also illegally occupied. Enemy property refers to land belonging to someone who has left India and moved to Pakistan or China. In July 2019, 26 FIRs were registered against Azam Khan at the Azeem Nagar police station in Rampur. On the basis of these cases, the ED began an investigation under the PMLA in August 2019. Following its investigation, the ED said on October 28, 2026, that office-bearers of the Jauhar Trust and Azam Khan had failed to establish the legitimate source of the money invested in the university. The ED found that funds released for government projects were also allegedly used for construction work at Azam Khan’s private university. Most contractors in Rampur allegedly diverted money and construction materials from government contracts to build the university. One contractor admitted that he had received a government contract worth ₹186 crore from the Public Works Department (PWD), around 40% of which was spent on work at the university. In addition, work worth ₹6.60 crore was carried out on the private university campus using the MLA Local Area Development Fund. The work was executed by the Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam, of which Azam Khan was the chairman at the time. In 2015, the Uttar Pradesh government sanctioned ₹23.41 crore for a pavilion for cultural programmes, a hostel for OBC students and a hospital on the campus. One condition for the pavilion was that ownership would remain with the Culture Department. It could not be sold or transferred and had to be made available to the state government free of charge whenever required. The conditions were changed in 2016. Ownership was transferred to Jauhar University, and the requirement for government use was removed. Azam Khan was the cabinet minister in charge of the department when both orders were issued. Citing these irregularities, the ED attached all 59 buildings at Jauhar University. Question 3: Will the university shut down now? What will happen to students’ education and degrees? Answer: Attaching a property means temporarily freezing or locking it. This is done to prevent the accused from selling the property or transferring it to someone else while the case is pending. The property cannot be used to obtain a bank loan either. If it generates rental income, for example, the money may be deposited into a government account instead of the accused’s bank account. People often assume that a property is immediately locked up once it is attached, but that is not necessarily the case. If a house is attached, the accused may often be allowed to continue living in it until the court delivers its verdict. In Jauhar University’s case, classes, examinations and other academic activities may continue. A university's authority to award degrees comes from government recognition or the legislation governing that university, not from the name in which its buildings are registered. Unless the government or the university's governing authorities revoke its recognition, degrees awarded to students will remain valid. The ED can provisionally attach property for 180 days. During this period, the PMLA Adjudicating Authority examines whether the action was justified. Azam Khan can present his case before the authority. If no decision is made within 180 days, the university's property will be released from the provisional attachment. If the authority upholds the ED's action and confirms the attachment, Azam Khan can challenge the decision in the High Court and the Supreme Court. If he receives no relief from the higher courts either, the property will remain attached until the court delivers its verdict in the ED's PMLA case. If it is established that illegally earned money was used to build the university, the property could be permanently confiscated by the government. If the allegations are not proved, the property will be returned. Question 4: What happens if it is proved that the university was built with illegally earned money? Can the government take it over? Answer: In that case, ownership of the university's buildings and land could permanently pass to the government. However, this does not necessarily mean that classes would stop immediately or that the buildings would be demolished. Legal options exist to ensure that students' education is not disrupted. Appointing a government receiver: The government could appoint an official to head the university. Its operations could then continue under government supervision, broadly as they do now. Affiliating it with a government university: The government could affiliate Jauhar University with a government university, such as Bareilly or Lucknow University. This would bring its management directly under the supervision of the government university. Taking over the university: The government also has this option. Under the Uttar Pradesh Private Universities Act, 2019, if allegations of corruption, financial irregularities or serious violations of rules are established against a private university, the government can revoke its recognition and take control of its assets. In Jauhar University's case, the possibility of a takeover is considered significant because, according to the ED, government funds and resources were also used in its construction. If the allegations are proved, the government could potentially convert it into a fully government-run university. In short, if Azam Khan loses the case, his trust and family could suffer the financial consequences. The university's land and buildings could pass into government ownership, and the government could run the institution as a public university for the benefit of students.

stories.title: Bhati gang's sharpshooter Maya Tyagi killed in encounter:Took contracts for murders; 2 Noida cops shot at
stories.summary: Police killed a criminal carrying a reward of ₹50,000 in an encounter in Noida on Saturday evening. Aman alias Maya Tyagi was a sharpshooter for the Randeep Bhati gang. The police and the district's Crime Response Team (CRT) cornered Aman in the area under Sector 126 police station. During the operation, he opened fire on the police personnel. Three police personnel were also shot during the encounter. According to the police, Aman alias Maya Tyagi was wanted by the Badalpur police station. A reward of ₹50,000 had been announced for his arrest. Senior police officers also reached the spot after receiving information about the encounter. The police are gathering details about Aman's criminal history and the cases registered against him. More than a dozen cases registered against Maya More than a dozen cases, including murder and attempted murder, have been registered against Maya at the Dadri, Badalpur and Bisrakh police stations in Gautam Buddha Nagar, as well as in Ghaziabad and Muzaffarnagar. Maya was involved in an encounter in 2019 too In 2019, Maya was involved in an encounter with the Phase 2 police. He was shot in both legs during the incident, after which the police arrested him. Robin Bhati introduced him to Randeep Aman alias Maya Tyagi had carried out several major crimes, including murder, in Muzaffarnagar. Due to a personal rivalry with Robin Tyagi, Maya began operating a gang alongside him. Robin later became friends with Randeep Bhati. To evade the police, Maya also sought refuge with Randeep and began living discreetly in Greater Noida. He worked with the Randeep gang for several years. As a sharpshooter, Maya was highly valued by both the Robin and Randeep Bhati gangs. Maya is also said to have played a key role in the murders of Devendra Bhati and a contractor from Jhummanpura in Greater Noida, as well as a double murder in Junpat. Rajkumar Sharma and his gunman were killed in the double murder. Maya did not engage in robbery. He carried out murders in exchange for payment or alongside members of his gang.

stories.title: BJP district chiefs found lagging on social media:90% are inactive, with Awadh and Maharajganj leaders among those exposed
stories.summary: A review meeting was held at the BJP's state headquarters in Lucknow on Saturday. The meeting exposed the level of social media activity among office-bearers and district presidents. State general secretary (organisation) Dharampal Singh had the social media activity of each district president and regional president assessed. It was found that 90% of the district presidents in the state were completely inactive on social media. Avadh region president Avadhesh Dwivedi was found to be completely inactive on social media. The party leadership expressed strong displeasure over this. Meanwhile, the district president of Maharajganj, the parliamentary constituency of state president Pankaj Chaudhary, also lagged behind in this regard. The state president could only smile after seeing the report on Ashok alias Sanjay Pandey. If not on Facebook, then what can I talk about on X? While reprimanding them, state general secretary (organisation) Dharampal Singh said, "When office-bearers are not even active on Facebook and Instagram, what is there to talk to them about X (Twitter)?" Dharmapal questioned how many district presidents repost the official posts of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, state president Pankaj Chaudhary, and the national and state BJP. Have district presidents become limited to posting only their own photographs? While presenting the report card at the meeting, it was stated that not a single post had been found from several district presidents over the past month, while even those who appeared active had posted only 15 to 20 times. Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde said bluntly, "Recognise the power of social media. We were once very strong on social media, but the opposition is now shaping the narrative. Prepare a list of 50 active workers in every Assembly constituency." State co-in-charge pointed out shortcomings, resentment among office-bearers At the meeting, state co-in-charge Pradeep Verma highlighted organisational shortcomings among the office-bearers and workers in their presence. He said that when he visits the districts, workers do not even raise slogans. After Verma's sharp remarks, internal resentment was also visible among the district presidents and district in-charges as soon as the meeting ended. BJP will re-add 1.25 crore votes that were removed Dharmapal Singh said that the names of more than 1.25 crore BJP-supported voters had been deleted from the SIR (SIR) electoral roll in the state. Under the Special Summary Revision campaign being conducted by the Election Commission of India, BJP workers will visit homes to verify the voter list and have the deleted names added again. 'Election Operations Committees' will also be formed soon at the assembly and district levels, with experienced workers willing to devote their full time assigned responsibilities. The rally, foot march and upcoming programmes were also discussed-find out about those too...

stories.title: ED arrests Azam Khan as he walks out of jail:Says, 'I am getting punished for being a Muslim'; was released after 11 months
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan walked out of Rampur Jail alongside his son Abdullah after 11 months, but the Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested him right at the jail gate. Enforcement Directorate (ED) officials initially questioned Azam outside the jail before taking him away in their vehicle. The ED will produce Azam before a Ghaziabad court. The ED alleges that Azam misused government funds and money linked to contracts in the construction of Jauhar University. The agency is investigating irregularities and money laundering involving expenses of ₹416.14 crore. Prior to this, a lengthy argument broke out between the ED and Azam outside the jail. Meanwhile, Azam remarked emotionally, "What is left to say now? This is the punishment for being a Muslim. The mistake is that a Muslim built a university. This is our crime." Meanwhile, his son Abdullah Azam headed home following his release. In fact, an ED team had entered the jail premises about 15 minutes before Azam's release, with 24 CRPF personnel also deployed. On 29 October, the Allahabad High Court suspended the 10-year sentence of Azam and Abdullah in a dual PAN card case, granting bail to both. Reacting to Azam's arrest, Akhilesh Yadav posted on X, "The entire nation, as well as the whole world, is watching the conspiracy of cases being orchestrated against Azam Khan Sahib." "The wrong precedent being fanned by those currently in power will claim them as victims when the tide turns. There will be nowhere to run then."

stories.title: Bullet train to cut Delhi-Varanasi journey to 3.5 hours:Stops at Agra, Kanpur and Lucknow; PM Modi approves northern corridor
stories.summary: A bullet train will connect New Delhi to Varanasi in 3 hours 30 minutes and cover the distance from New Delhi to Agra in one hour, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said in Varanasi on Saturday, announcing that the Prime Minister had approved the Northern Corridor of the Delhi-Varanasi-Guwahati bullet train project. The corridor will begin in Delhi and connect Agra, Kanpur, Lucknow and Ayodhya before extending to Guwahati via Varanasi, Patna and Siliguri. : New Vande Bharat sleeper-train to cover Varanasi-Delhi in 9 hrs The journey to Varanasi currently takes 10 hours Varanasi is around 807 km from Delhi. Trains such as the Tejas and Rajdhani take more than 10 hours to cover this distance. The bullet train will reduce the journey time to just 3 hours 30 minutes. According to railway sources, the schedules of the bullet train arriving in Varanasi from Siliguri and the train departing from Varanasi for Delhi will be planned in such a way that passengers can get off one train and board the other. A flight takes around 4 hours A flight from Varanasi to Delhi takes 1 hour 40 minutes. However, when the time spent travelling to the airport, boarding the aircraft and leaving the airport after landing is included, the total journey takes around four hours. The bullet train will have more seats than the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train India's first bullet train will operate between Mumbai and Ahmedabad. The bullet train between Varanasi and Siliguri will have a higher passenger capacity. At present, plans are in place for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train to have 731 seats. In comparison, the bullet train running from Varanasi to Siliguri via Patna will be able to carry 750 passengers. Bullet train to have an earthquake warning system An earthquake warning system is being installed on a bullet train in India for the first time. The system is based on Japanese technology. If an earthquake occurs, it will immediately cut off the power supply. Once the power is cut, the emergency brakes will engage and bring the train to a halt. Benefits of the bullet train

stories.title: 15 IAS officers transferred in UP:Chief Secretary Shashi Prakash Goyal given additional charge of ACS, Civil Aviation Department
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government carried out a major administrative reshuffle on Saturday. Five IAS officers were transferred, while the responsibilities of 10 officers were changed. Chief Secretary Shashi Prakash Goyal has been given the additional charge of Additional Chief Secretary, Civil Aviation Department. Anurag Srivastava has been appointed Agriculture Production Commissioner. Alok Kumar-2 has been given charge of the Infrastructure and Industrial Development Commissioner's post. M. Devaraj has been appointed chairman of the State Vigilance Commission and Administrative Tribunal-1. Dr M.K.S. Sundaram has been appointed Principal Secretary, Coordination. Alok Kumar-3 has been given charge of the Finance and Institutional Finance departments. In addition, Ajay Chauhan has been appointed Chief Executive Officer of UPSIDA. Pankaj Yadav has been relieved of the additional charge of Principal Secretary, Externally Aided Projects. These officers also get new responsibilities View list

stories.title: Two SDMs placed on waiting list, new postings cancelled:Removed from Pilibhit the day before amid allegations of irregularities in 13,150 votes
stories.summary: In Pilibhit, the new postings of SDM Mayank Goswami and Hemant Chaudhary, who were removed over allegations of irregularities in the electoral roll, have also been cancelled. Both officers have now been placed on the waiting list. They had been posted in Lucknow in the transfer list issued at 7 p.m. on Friday evening. According to the list, Mayank Goswami was appointed Settlement Officer (Consolidation) at the Consolidation Headquarters in Lucknow, while Hemant Chaudhary was appointed Officer on Special Duty at the Uttar Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority. Meanwhile, Mandhata Pratap Singh and Ajay Kumar were given charge as SDMs in Pilibhit in their place. In fact, on 21 October, Congress leader Supriya Shrinate and state president Aradhana Mishra had alleged that 13,150 Muslim voters in the Pilibhit Sadar Assembly constituency had identical EPIC numbers, but their names and their fathers' names had been changed. It was alleged that the voters' real names had been removed and replaced with other names. See the pictures... Instructions to check voter lists for all Assembly seats After complaints emerged, Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa had directed officials to check the voter lists for all Assembly seats in Pilibhit and submit a report within two days. The Chief Electoral Officer said that wherever a complaint of irregularities in the voter lists was received, an investigation would be conducted. Now, here are the allegations made by Congress... Congress national spokesperson Supriya Shrinate held a press conference in Lucknow on 21 October. She had alleged irregularities in Pilibhit's voter list. She said, "The changes have mainly been made to the names of Muslim male voters according to a specific pattern." This would prevent the male heads of families from going to vote and could also affect voting by the women in their families. Supriya Shrinate had claimed that 2,600 new voters were added in the Pilibhit Sadar Assembly constituency without following the prescribed procedure, while the names of 804 voters were deleted. This is the Assembly constituency of Sanjay Gangwar, a minister in the Uttar Pradesh government. Gangwar won the 2022 Assembly election by 6,920 votes. He alleged that the names of 13,150 voters had been changed, while their EPIC numbers remained the same. Irregularities affected more than 16,000 votes in the constituency. Names were added and removed while the process was closed Supriya Shrinate alleged that the final SIR draft list for Uttar Pradesh was released on 10 April 2026. The names of around 2 crore 4 lakh voters were removed from it. Pilibhit Sadar has a total of 3,48,937 voters. Even after the draft list was released in April and the process was closed, voters' names were deleted and new names were added between July and September. The Form 6 and Form 7 processes were not under way during that period. They claimed that these changes were made through the software based on a pattern. Several names were changed at 7:19 pm, followed by sudden changes to hundreds of names exactly one minute later, at 7:20 pm. The question is, if such irregularities occurred through the software, where can ordinary voters go with their complaints? Villagers had also lodged a complaint... A large number of people, including Congress leader Kumud Gangwar, had also complained. There were allegations of irregularities in the electoral rolls for Bhikharipur village under the Pilibhit Sadar Assembly constituency and booth number 83 in Amariya in the Jehanabad-Kashmir area. Villagers complained that names and fathers' names had been changed and votes deleted. On 15 October, Faizan and Farhan, residents of Awas Vikas, also complained to the district magistrate. They alleged that incorrect names had been recorded against the EPIC IDs. On the same day, former minister Hemraj Verma and Samajwadi Party workers also complained to the Election Commission. SDM also in the news over complaints of collecting money from trucks SDM Mayank Goswami came to Pilibhit on transfer from Bilaspur in Rampur around three years ago. He was initially posted as Additional SDM. He was later given his first posting in the district as SDM Amaria. During this period, complaints emerged accusing him of extorting money from trucks. Lawyers also protested, accusing him of corruption. On 16 July, the then SDM of Puranpur, Ajit Kumar Singh, was transferred to another district. The then District Magistrate, Gyanendra Singh, subsequently handed Mayank Goswami responsibility for Puranpur, the district's largest tehsil.

stories.title: Transgender group kicks constables on Kanpur Highway:Strips and tears uniform; cops claim police station failed to send help
stories.summary: A group of transgender persons allegedly assaulted police personnel on the Kanpur-Sagar Highway, kicked one of the constables and tore a policeman's uniform. They also allegedly removed their clothes and created a disturbance. The incident took place near the Aliyapur toll plaza at around 10 pm on October 26. The police response vehicle (PRV) personnel had reached the spot after receiving a complaint of alleged extortion. CCTV footage of the incident has also surfaced. The 28-second video shows two policemen on the road arguing with three transgender persons. The argument escalates into pushing and physical assault. One of them, who is partially undressed, grabs a constable and kicks him. The policeman steps back and tries to move away. The three then appear to follow him, while another person is seen removing their clothes. Police reached the spot after extortion complaint In his complaint to the police, Ankit Singh, a resident of Banjari village in Bhadohi, said he was returning home from Hamirpur at around 9.30 pm on October 26. Near the Sajeti toll plaza, some people dressed as transgender persons allegedly stopped his car and demanded ₹2,000. When he told them that his vehicle had broken down and he did not have change, they became aggressive. He alleged that they dragged him out of the car, assaulted him and damaged his vehicle. Feeling unsafe with his family, he called the police emergency helpline 112. Following the complaint, PRV constables Rajesh Kumar and Praveen Bansal reached the spot. Rajesh Kumar, also known as Sonu Yadav, said his colleague Praveen was trying to reason with the group when Kajal, Muskan and others allegedly attacked them. They assaulted the policemen with kicks and punches and tore Praveen's uniform. Constable questions lack of backup after attack After the incident, Rajesh Kumar expressed his frustration over the alleged lack of support from Sajeti police station and the failure of backup personnel to reach the spot. He posted a message about the incident in the official WhatsApp group of Dial 112, questioning the lack of response. He said his team had reached the location after receiving information under event number 29317 at 9.42 pm. Some people were allegedly demanding money from a man by force. When the policemen tried to help him, the group allegedly misbehaved with and attacked them. Rajesh said police personnel often go out at night to help people in unfamiliar and difficult situations. They expect their police station and senior officers to support them when they face trouble. However, when their own dignity is at stake and complaints go unheard, it affects their morale. He also raised concerns about the dignity of the uniform and the safety of police personnel. Constable alleges police station failed to send backup Rajesh said he immediately informed the Sajeti station house officer and the local area in-charge. On their instructions, he also obtained a written complaint from the victim. However, he alleged that no action followed. After waiting for help, he informed the PRV in-charge about the incident on WhatsApp. He claimed that he received no response and no additional personnel arrived at the spot. He further alleged that members of the group climbed onto the PRV vehicle and engaged in obscene behaviour. They also tried several times to snatch his mobile phone when he attempted to record the incident. Rajesh said the prolonged wait for assistance and the lack of response to his complaint left him frustrated. Toll staff allege repeated extortion attempts Employees at the Aliyapur toll plaza said groups of transgender persons frequently stop vehicles near the toll plaza and demand money from drivers. They alleged that those who refuse to pay are sometimes subjected to misbehaviour. The employees said they had repeatedly informed the local police about the issue verbally, but alleged that no action had been taken. FIR registered, says ACP ACP Ghatampur Krishnakant said a video showing the alleged assault by transgender persons had gone viral. He said the police had taken cognisance of the footage, obtained a complaint from the policeman and registered an FIR. Further action is underway.

stories.title: 2 men run over by train in Kanpur:Returning after Karwa Chauth, deceased dragged nearly 100 metres
stories.summary: A video has surfaced from Kanpur showing two men being run over by a train while crossing a railway crossing. The train was moving so fast that both men were dragged along for around 100 metres. Their bodies were badly mutilated, making them difficult to identify. One of the men has been identified from his Aadhaar card as Sanjeev alias Sanju (35), a resident of Mainpuri. The other man is yet to be identified. Had gone to wife’s maternal home four days ago Tikam Singh, a farmer from Kishni Katra in Mainpuri, has three sons: Rakesh, Dilip and Sanjeev alias Sanju. Sanjeev worked as a mason in Gurugram. He is survived by his wife Sangeeta and two children, Lakshmi and Avnish. Tikam Singh said Sanjeev had gone to his wife’s maternal home in Patarsa about four days ago to celebrate Karwa Chauth. Sangeeta was staying at her parents’ home. On Thursday night, after the Karwa Chauth puja, Sanjeev set off for home. Wife had urged him not to leave at night Sangeeta said she had repeatedly asked Sanjeev not to leave as it was late, and had suggested he go in the morning, but he did not listen and left late at night. At around 10 pm, he reached the Panki Padav railway crossing. The gates were closed at the time and people were waiting for a train to pass. Sanjeev and another man allegedly tried to cross the track despite the closed gates when the speeding Unchahar Express hit them. Locals called the police on 112. Panki police and the Government Railway Police (GRP) reached the spot. Identified through Aadhaar card, mobile phone Police recovered an Aadhaar card and a mobile phone from one man’s pocket, which helped identify him as Sanjeev. His family was informed. The second man’s body was so badly mutilated that he could not be identified. Police are trying to establish his identity. ‘I had asked him not to go at night’ A distraught Sangeeta said: ‘I had told him not to go home at night. I had asked him to leave in the morning, but he did not listen to me. I had kept the Karwa Chauth fast for my husband’s long life. After the puja, he left saying he would go home, but soon the news of his death came.’ Police working to identify second man ACP Panki Amit Chaurasiya said police received information about the accident at the railway crossing late at night through 112. Local police and the GRP reached the spot. One of the men was identified, while the other remains unidentified.

stories.title: Mumbai wildlife smuggler arrested in Lucknow:Gang's network extended to Dubai and Gulf countries
stories.summary: A joint team of the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) and the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) has arrested a Mumbai-based wildlife smuggler in Lucknow. The accused had arrived in the city with wildlife belonging to protected species. During questioning, he allegedly revealed that his gang sourced animals and birds from forests in Gorakhpur, Lakhimpur Kheri and Sitapur before transporting them through Mumbai to Dubai, Saudi Arabia and Bahrain. The team also recovered protected wildlife from his possession. Mumbai man arrested in joint operation According to the STF, it had received information about a gang involved in the illegal trade of protected wildlife in Uttar Pradesh. Several teams were directed to gather intelligence and take action. An STF team led by Sub-Inspector Faizuddin Siddiqui, part of Additional Superintendent of Police Avnishwar Chandra Srivastava's team, was working in Lucknow when it received information that a Mumbai-based smuggler was bringing protected wildlife into the city. The STF shared the information with the Lucknow team of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau. The joint team arrested the accused from Iradat Nagar in Madeyganj. He was identified as Firoz Musrat Khan, a resident of Byculla, Mumbai. Gang allegedly supplied wildlife to Gulf countries During questioning, Khan allegedly told investigators that he was associated with a gang involved in smuggling prohibited and protected birds and animals. According to his account, gang members collected wildlife from forests in Gorakhpur, Lakhimpur Kheri and Sitapur. The animals and birds were then transported through Mumbai for supply to foreign countries. He allegedly said the gang supplied wildlife to Dubai, Saudi Arabia and Bahrain. Schedule I species receive the highest legal protection Under India's wildlife protection law, species listed in Schedule I receive the highest level of legal protection. These include tigers, leopards, elephants, rhinoceroses, blackbucks and falcons. Hunting or illegally trading in these species is a serious offence.

stories.title: Gorakhpur to get ₹1,663 crore Diwali development boost:CM Yogi to inaugurate ROB and first phase of Godhoiya Nala project on Nov 1
stories.summary: Gorakhpur is set to receive a Diwali gift of 88 development projects worth around ₹1,663 crore on November 1, a week before the festival. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will inaugurate several completed projects, including a railway overbridge (ROB) in Chauri Chaura and the first phase of the Godhoiya Nala project. He will also lay foundation stones for the second phase of the drainage project, a road along the drain and the Gorakhpur Sewerage Scheme Zone A3. The projects cover road connectivity, infrastructure, urban amenities and flood protection. ROB in Chauri Chaura to ease traffic congestion The Chief Minister will begin his public programme on November 1 from the Chauri Chaura Assembly constituency. He will inaugurate the ROB at Bhopa Bazaar, built at a cost of ₹59.44 crore. He will also inaugurate and lay foundation stones for 84 other development projects worth a total of ₹287.56 crore in the constituency. The ROB is expected to provide relief from traffic congestion in the Chauri Chaura area. For years, residents, traders and schoolchildren had faced long traffic jams at railway crossing number 147B on the Gorakhpur-Bhatni railway section. The railway gate had to be closed several times a day due to train movements, causing inconvenience to commuters. The nearly 650-metre-long overbridge is expected to improve traffic movement in Chauri Chaura town and save time and fuel for residents of dozens of nearby villages. The overbridge also features murals depicting the historic Chauri Chaura incident of February 4, 1922, which holds an important place in India's freedom struggle. The pillars and walls feature artwork dedicated to the freedom fighters who lost their lives in the incident. The murals aim to introduce younger generations to the area's historical legacy. Godhoiya Nala project to address waterlogging and sewage Yogi Adityanath will also inaugurate the first phase of the Godhoiya Nala project, completed at a cost of ₹495.24 crore. He will lay foundation stones for the second phase, estimated to cost ₹92.72 crore, a road running parallel to the drain costing ₹65.93 crore, and the Gorakhpur Sewerage Scheme Zone A3, worth ₹721.40 crore. The first phase includes infrastructure to improve drainage and sewage management across 17 wards in the northern part of Gorakhpur. Of the 9.25-km-long drain, 7.75 km has been converted into a covered concrete drain. The project also includes 17.50 km of intercepting sewer lines and a sewage treatment plant (STP) with a capacity of 38 million litres per day (MLD). A main pumping station with a capacity of 61 MLD and 14 bridges and culverts have also been constructed. The project involves drain construction, diversion, sewage interception and treatment. Treated water from the STP is being discharged into Ramgarh Tal lake. The treatment process is also helping improve the lake's water quality, according to the project details. Second phase to include drain construction and access road The second phase of the Godhoiya Nala project will cost ₹92.72 crore. It will involve converting the remaining 1.50-km unlined stretch of the drain into a reinforced cement concrete (RCC) structure. An approach road measuring 1.50 km will also be built alongside the drain to provide access to the 38-MLD STP near the Bichhiya Railway Colony. Currently, the STP can be reached through a narrow road passing through residential areas inside the railway colony. The proposed alternative route is intended to ensure access if the Railways builds a boundary wall around its residential colonies in the future. The second phase will also include the installation of 120 streetlights and landscaping. The tender process for the work has begun. 7.75-km road to be built alongside drain A 7.75-km road will be constructed parallel to the Godhoiya Nala at an estimated cost of ₹65.93 crore. The project will include carriageways measuring 3.75 metres in width on both sides of the drain, along with plantation for beautification, crash barriers for safety and streetlight poles. The road is expected to improve connectivity for residents living along the drain. 350 km of sewer lines planned under Zone A3 The Gorakhpur Sewerage Scheme Zone A3 will involve laying around 350 km of sewer lines in the catchment area of the Godhoiya Nala. The project, approved under the AMRUT 2.0 programme, will cost ₹721.40 crore. It will cover 17 wards connected to the Godhoiya Nala and include 43,604 household sewer connections. Two intermediate pumping stations, with capacities of 37.50 MLD and 27 MLD, will also be constructed. Yogi Adityanath will lay the foundation stone for the scheme on November 1.

stories.title: Kashi Vishwanath Dham celebrates Sardar Patel's birth anniversary:Devotees pledge to promote national unity, harmony and cleanliness
stories.summary: A message of national unity and cleanliness was shared at Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham in Varanasi on Saturday to mark the birth anniversary of Bharat Ratna Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The programme was organised by Namami Gange in front of the statue of Jagadguru Shankaracharya. Devotees from different states raised slogans promoting national unity and took a pledge to make national unity and cleanliness part of their daily lives. Rajesh Shukla, Namami Gange's Kashi region coordinator and the Municipal Corporation's cleanliness brand ambassador, said Lord Shiva and Kashi Vishwanath Dham symbolise national unity. He said the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva connect the country geographically and culturally. Remembering Sardar Patel at the Vishwanath Dham, Shukla said the programme conveyed a message of national unity, cultural harmony and brotherhood. Jaydev, Pranay, Souvik, Yogesh, Suhasini and Shakuntala, among others, attended the programme.

stories.title: Stray dogs kill child in Saharanpur:Blood-soaked body found in field; dogs chased him before mauling him throughout the night
stories.summary: Eleven-year-old Priyanshu went missing while playing outside his house in Belda Junardar village, Saharanpur, on Friday evening. His body was found in a field near the village on Saturday morning. According to reports, three or four stray dogs chased the child towards the field and attacked him. He is believed to have died after being attacked by the dogs during the night. News of the body being found spread through the village on Saturday morning, leaving the family and local residents in shock. The incident took place under the Nagal police station area. Priyanshu, the 11-year-old son of Ravinder, who lives in Belda Junardar village, left home to play at around 5 p.m. on Friday. He did not return home until late evening. When Priyanshu did not arrive home after a considerable amount of time, his family became worried. They began searching for him in nearby houses and across the village. The family and villagers continued searching for the child until late at night, but there was no trace of him anywhere. The family also shared information about the child's disappearance on social media so that anyone who found out anything about him could pass it on to the family. However, even after searching throughout the night, there was no trace of Priyanshu. The family hoped that the child would be found somewhere. Child's body found lying in field in the morning, uproar in village But on Saturday morning, Priyanshu's body was found lying in a field near the village, around 200 metres from his home. It is being reported that dogs attacked the child and mauled him badly. As soon as news of the incident spread, a crowd of villagers gathered at the spot. When the family arrived and saw the child's body, they began screaming and crying. The child whom the family had searched for throughout the night was found dead in the morning. The police were immediately informed about the incident. As soon as they received the information, Nangal police reached the spot. A forensic team also inspected the scene with the police and collected the necessary evidence. The police took possession of the body, completed the inquest proceedings and sent it for post-mortem examination. Necessary legal action has been initiated in the case. Priyanshu was the eldest of three brothers and studied in Class Five Priyanshu was the eldest of his three brothers. He studied in Class Five at a school in the village. But his life was cut short in an attack by stray dogs. Since the incident, the family has been inconsolable. Two days earlier, dogs had targeted two children as well Villagers say that the menace posed by stray and ferocious dogs in the village is continuing to grow. Two days earlier, dogs had attacked two children named Aarav and Sonu, injuring them. Even after that incident, the villagers remained fearful of the dogs. Following the death of 11-year-old Priyanshu, the village is now gripped by fear and anger. Villagers say that if effective steps had been taken in time to curb the menace posed by stray dogs, perhaps such a tragic incident could have been prevented. They have demanded that the ferocious dogs roaming the village be removed and that the responsible departments take immediate action. Police sent the body for a post-mortem examination Station House Officer Inspector Radheshyam Yadav said that after the child's body was recovered, the police reached the spot and carried out the necessary procedures. An inquest report was prepared and the body was sent for post-mortem examination. A forensic team also examined the scene. The police are taking legal action in accordance with the rules.

stories.title: Azam Khan's lawyer speaks on sentence suspension and bail:Three lawyers present arguments; Shashwat Anand says there is no evidence, only allegations
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has suspended the sentences of former Uttar Pradesh minister Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam in the two PAN cards case and granted them bail. However, the court refused to stay their conviction. Senior advocates Abhishek Manu Singhvi and N.I. Jafri, along with advocate Shashwat Anand, argued on behalf of Azam Khan and Abdullah. Speaking about the court's decision, advocate Shashwat Anand said Abdullah was accused of having two PAN cards and using them in election papers. He said the court had already stayed the conviction in the birth certificate case. Anand argued that the conviction in the PAN card case should not have happened as it was not supported by enough evidence. He said there was no evidence apart from the allegations to prove the charges against them. The court accepted their request to suspend the sentence and granted them bail. 10-year sentence suspended, but Azam may not walk out of jail immediately The High Court suspended the 10-year sentences of Azam Khan and Abdullah on Thursday and granted them bail in the two PAN cards case. The decision has cleared the way for Abdullah to come out of jail. However, it is not yet clear whether Azam will also be released, as two other cases are pending against him. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has recently registered one case against Azam. Another case was registered by the Uttar Pradesh Vigilance Department on September 10. Azam may be released if the police do not obtain a production warrant, also known as a B-warrant, in these cases. Even if he gets out of jail, Azam will not be able to contest elections. He has already been sentenced to two years in a separate case for calling officials in Rampur 'tankhaiya'. What arguments did the defence lawyers make? During the hearing on October 15, senior advocates Abhishek Manu Singhvi and N.I. Jafri, along with advocate Shashwat Anand, presented arguments on behalf of Azam and Abdullah. Advocates Sharad Sharma and Nawab Kazim Ali Khan, also known as Nawed Mian, represented BJP MLA Akash Saxena, who filed the complaint. The defence challenged the decisions of the trial court and sessions court. They argued that the conviction and sentences should be reconsidered. The Uttar Pradesh government opposed the request to suspend their sentences. In its appeal, the government had also sought life imprisonment for Azam and Abdullah. How Azam's sentence was increased to 10 years Azam Khan and Abdullah were convicted in the two PAN cards case by the Rampur MP-MLA court. On November 17, 2025, the court sentenced both of them to seven years in prison. On May 5, 2026, the government lawyer filed an appeal in the Rampur court seeking an increase in their sentences. On May 23, 2026, the court increased Azam's sentence by three years, making it 10 years. However, Abdullah's sentence was not increased.

stories.title: Gorakhpur records highest rainfall in UP:Khorabar gets 84.5 mm in 12 hours, maximum temperature breaks 57-year record
stories.summary: Rain has stopped in Gorakhpur since Saturday morning, but the sky remains cloudy and cold winds are making the weather chilly. According to the Meteorological Department, the weather is expected to improve from today. Rainfall is likely to decrease and the sky is expected to remain clear. The maximum temperature may rise by 5-7 degrees next week, while the minimum temperature could drop by 3-5 degrees Celsius. According to the department, Khorabar in Gorakhpur recorded the highest rainfall in Uttar Pradesh, with 84.5 mm of rain by 8:30 pm. Bhathat recorded 69.5 mm, Campierganj 57 mm and Sahjanwan 56.5 mm of rainfall. October was the coldest month for the third time According to the Meteorological Department, the maximum temperature fell by 11.1 degrees Celsius on Friday. This broke a 57-year record. From 1969 to 2026, October has been this cold only three times. Before this, the maximum temperature was recorded at 20.6 degrees Celsius in 2005, 21.8 degrees in 2013 and 22.1 degrees Celsius on 30 October this year. Blankets come out in homes The weather has changed completely because of two days of continuous rain. Temperatures have fallen due to cyclonic winds, and the cold has suddenly intensified. People have taken out blankets at home, while children and the elderly have started wearing woollens. Weather to Remain Clear Today According to meteorologist Kailash Pandey, the city's maximum temperature is expected to be 28 degrees Celsius and the minimum temperature 23 degrees Celsius today. Light showers may occur in the morning, while the weather is expected to clear by afternoon. Some areas may receive scattered rain.

stories.title: 52-year-old Harishankar to drive India's second Vande Bharat sleeper:32-year-old Jyoti to be first-time guard, 7 of 13 crew members are women
stories.summary: The country's second Vande Bharat sleeper train, running between Varanasi and New Delhi, will begin operations on October 31. The train will be driven by 52-year-old loco pilot Harishankar Yadav, while 32-year-old Jyoti will take charge as the guard for the first time on a Vande Bharat sleeper train. Harishankar has been operating Vande Bharat trains since 2020. However, this is the first time he has been given the responsibility of driving a train during the launch of a new service. For Jyoti, too, this will be her first time working as a guard on a Vande Bharat train. Both see this as a special responsibility. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw will flag off the train at a programme at Banaras station. The train is scheduled to depart from the station at 4:56 pm. The train will have 16 coaches and a total of 823 berths for passengers. It will leave Varanasi at 8:50 pm and reach New Delhi at 6:10 am the next day. From freight trains to Vande Bharat Fifty-two-year-old Harishankar Yadav will drive the country's second Vande Bharat sleeper train from Varanasi to Delhi. He said the technology used in Vande Bharat and Vande Bharat sleeper trains is almost the same, but operating the new train during its launch will be a different experience. Harishankar said, "Driving a train in front of so many people and taking responsibility for its operations is a challenge. I am happy and proud, but also a little nervous." He explained that the technology used in ordinary trains is different from that of Vande Bharat trains. In Vande Bharat trains, the engine is built into the train instead of being separate. A display screen provides regular updates about the train's operation and technical condition. It also shows any problem that may occur while the train is running. 32-year-old Jyoti Kumari will take on the guard's responsibility Thirty-two-year-old Jyoti Kumari will serve as the guard on this train. Jyoti is a resident of Bijita in Patna. She has been serving with the railways since 2021. She had earlier performed the role of a guard during the inauguration of the Amrit Bharat train, but this will be her first experience on a Vande Bharat train. Seven women among the 13-member crew A total 13-member crew will operate the Vande Bharat Sleeper. It includes seven women. Shreeni Srivastava will serve as the assistant loco pilot, while Jyoti will be the guard. Ten TTEs will be deployed on the train, including five women and five men. Thus, women employees will also play a significant role in responsibilities related to the train's operation and passenger services. 823 berths in 16 coaches, with AC coaches in all three classes Vande Bharat Sleeper is a modern 16-coach trainset. It will have a total of 823 berths. The train will have AC first-class, AC second-class and AC third-class coaches. It has been designed to make long-distance overnight travel faster, safer and more comfortable. The train has a maximum operating speed of 160 kilometres per hour. It is equipped with modern propulsion and control systems. Regenerative braking has been provided to save energy. The train also features improved noise and vibration control, thermal insulation and an advanced fire-safety system. The process of accelerating and braking the train has been made smoother so that passengers experience fewer jolts during night journeys. It also features intelligent diagnostics and a modern train management system. Varanasi-to-Delhi journey to take nine hours According to the regular timetable issued by the Railways: Will operate six days a week The train will operate from Varanasi on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday. From New Delhi, it will operate on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Sunday. Stops at four stations between Varanasi and New Delhi It will stop at Prayagraj, Kanpur Central, Aligarh and Ghaziabad stations. Will depart at 4:56 An inauguration ceremony will be held at Banaras railway station on 31 October. According to Station Director Shriram Yadav, the programme will begin at 3:50 p.m. and continue until 5 p.m. The Vande Bharat sleeper train will be flagged off at 4:56 p.m. After this, the Varanasi-Rajatalab and Prayagraj Rambagh-Banaras MEMU services will also be inaugurated. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw will attend the programme. Public representatives from Varanasi and senior railway officials will also be present.

stories.title: Chaos at Prayagraj Run for Unity marathon:5,000-6,000 people protest, break chairs and snatch certificates over race starting without flag-off
stories.summary: A commotion broke out during the Run for Unity marathon held in Prayagraj on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary. Around 6,000 students took part in the event. The trouble started when the race began soon after registration without explaining the rules or holding a formal flag-off. This led to confusion among the participants, and chairs were broken during the chaos. The marathon was organised by the BJP's Yamunapar unit. Around 5,000 people took part in the 5-km race held in Naini. Check 3 pictures below : The BJP's Prayagraj Yamunapar unit is organising a 5-km marathon in Naini on the occasion of National Unity Day. The race will start at 7 am from Abhinandan Guest House in Mewalal ki Bagiya and end at the selfie point near Sachcha Baba Ashram. BJP district vice-president Prof. Dr Devi Singh Patel is coordinating the event. According to the organisers, around 5,000 people are expected to take part in the marathon. Participants, public representatives and people working for public welfare, including those involved in de-addiction work, will also be honoured during the event. The winner will receive a prize of ₹11,000, while the runner-up will get ₹7,000. Sardar Patel statue to be unveiled at 1:30 pm Meanwhile, a grand statue of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, also known as the Iron Man of India, installed by the Prayagraj Municipal Corporation on Sardar Patel Marg, will be unveiled on October 31. State Jal Shakti Minister Swatantra Dev Singh will unveil the statue at 1:30 pm. Preparations are under way for both events. Public representatives, BJP office-bearers, party workers, young people, sportspersons, prominent citizens and journalists have been invited to the National Unity Day programmes.

stories.title: Shah outlines 3 key issues for UP elections:Says, 'UCC will be implemented after 2027 polls'; lashes out Akhilesh by calling him ‘Babu’
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah laid out the BJP's roadmap for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections on Friday. During his visit to UP, Shah referred to the firing on Ram devotees in Ayodhya on October 30, 1990, and indicated that development, nationalism and the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) would be among the party's key poll issues. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will remain the BJP's face in the elections. Shah also stressed the need to target the Samajwadi Party (SP) over law and order, corruption, lawlessness and alleged Muslim appeasement. Shah addressed around 2,850 party office-bearers for 37 minutes at a meeting held at Dr Ram Manohar Lohia National Law University in Lucknow. He urged party workers to take ownership of the organisation, saying their hard work and commitment were more important than anything else during elections. Yogi Adityanath also credited party workers for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's success. The meeting also decided that the BJP would launch a large-scale public outreach campaign in November and December. The party plans to organise visits and public meetings across Uttar Pradesh involving its central leadership, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. Five major political takeaways from Shah's speech 1. Attempts to pacify disgruntled party workers Amit Shah described party workers as the owners of the organisation and 'devotees'. He urged them to put aside their grievances, saying, "Throw all your anger and complaints into the Gomti today itself. It is not the government or leaders, but party workers who win elections." His remarks directly addressed complaints about internal tensions and the influence of bureaucrats within the organisation following the 2022 elections. The message is being seen as an attempt to address dissatisfaction among party workers and resolve their grievances within the organisation. 2. Targets SP over the Ram Mandir issue Amid the political debate surrounding the Ram Mandir, Shah raised the issue of police firing on kar sevaks in Ayodhya on October 30, 1990. Targeting the government led by then Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav, he questioned how the SP could seek to form the government again. Shah said, "You ordered firing on Ram devotees, while we built the Ram Mandir." Through this statement, he sought to corner the SP over the Ram Mandir issue and remind voters of the firing on Kar Sevaks. 3. Makes UCC a key election issue Shah announced that the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) would be implemented in Uttar Pradesh if the BJP forms the government for a third consecutive term. The announcement could become one of the party's major issues in the 2027 Assembly elections. The BJP is likely to present the UCC as a common legal framework and link it to its ideological agenda. 4. Calls BJP's position in UP as firm as 'Angad's foot' Shah compared the BJP's position in Uttar Pradesh to 'Angad's foot', saying that no one could dislodge the party from power. He referred to the BJP's victory in the 2017 Assembly elections and its vote share in the 2022 polls. Taking a swipe at the SP, Shah said it would not be able to form the government in Uttar Pradesh for the next 30 years. He also challenged Rahul Gandhi to discuss his allegations of 'vote theft' in Parliament. 5. Signals preparations for 2029 alongside Mission 2027 Shah urged party workers to prepare for the elections, saying, "Get ready. Put aside all other thoughts and focus like Arjun, who could see only the eye of the bird. The time has come to form the BJP government in UP for the third consecutive time with a massive majority." He also spoke about taking the saffron flag from Gangotri to Gangasagar and expressed confidence that Narendra Modi would become Prime Minister for a fourth consecutive term. These remarks are being viewed as a signal that the BJP is preparing not only for the 2027 Assembly elections but also for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. Shah also indicated that Yogi Adityanath would be the party's face in the 2027 elections, while Modi and Shah would lead the wider campaign. Shah is also expected to play a key role in steering the organisation's preparations. What is the BJP's election strategy? Key points explained BJP Uttar Pradesh organisational general secretary Dharampal Singh presented the election preparation roadmap at the state executive committee meeting. He assigned responsibilities for the party's programmes scheduled for November and December. 1. 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' marches across six organisational zones The BJP will organise large-scale marches across all six organisational zones in Uttar Pradesh under its 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' campaign. The party is targeting the participation of around 25,000 or more workers in each march. The campaign will begin on November 3 in Lucknow and Bareilly. Events will be held in the Prayagraj and Gorakhpur zones on November 4, followed by a march in Ghaziabad on November 5. 2. Special focus on new voters The party has also made voter registration an important part of its election strategy. After Diwali, the BJP will launch a special campaign to ensure that new voters are added to the electoral rolls. Young people and women will receive particular attention. Party workers will help eligible voters fill out Form 6 online to register their names. 3. Teams of five active workers at every polling booth To strengthen its organisation at the grassroots level, the BJP will identify 25 active workers in each of Uttar Pradesh's 1,918 organisational mandals. Additionally, teams of five active workers will be formed at every polling booth. Assembly-level in-charges and organisational expanders will assess the party's position at Shakti Kendras. 4. Outreach to young people, women and beneficiaries The BJP will organise youth conventions at 200 locations for people aged between 18 and 21. Conventions will also be held in every mandal for first-time voters. The party will organise smaller meetings to reach young and women voters. In addition, it will reach out to farmers, members of cooperative societies and small business owners. What did ministers and MPs say after the meeting? Rajya Sabha MP Priyanka Rawat said senior leaders had guided party workers during the state executive committee meeting. She said the party should use social media to communicate its work to the public. She alleged that the Opposition was unnecessarily trying to create a negative atmosphere, adding that the government worked for the people and that the public remained paramount. Minister JPS Rathore said Amit Shah had described the BJP government's position in Uttar Pradesh as being as firm as 'Angad's foot'. He said no force, however powerful, could uproot or dislodge the government. Minister Dayashankar Singh said the Assembly elections were approaching and that Shah and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had energised party workers. He said BJP workers were ready to form the government in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term. He added that just as the BJP had formed the government at the Centre for a third consecutive term under Narendra Modi, it would do the same in Uttar Pradesh under Yogi Adityanath's leadership. What did the Opposition say? SP MP Awadhesh Prasad calls UCC Shah's 'wishful thinking' Samajwadi Party MP from Ayodhya, Awadhesh Prasad, criticised Union Home Minister Amit Shah's announcement about implementing the Uniform Civil Code in Uttar Pradesh. He described the proposal as nothing more than an imagination and a pipe dream. Dharmendra Yadav says people no longer trust BJP's claims SP leader Dharmendra Yadav said the BJP had raised the slogan of '400-plus' during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and had also claimed that it would win all 80 seats in Uttar Pradesh. However, he said people no longer trusted the party's claims. Referring to the recent MLC election results, he alleged that the SP would have won 10 seats and an independent candidate would also have emerged victorious if electoral malpractice had not taken place. Imran Masood says people want development, not old agendas Congress leader Imran Masood said the BJP's old agenda of communal polarisation no longer had an impact on people. He said voters were tired of such politics and wanted work and development rather than just promises.
