SP candidate Pravendra Singh Bhati has conceded defeat on the Meerut-Saharanpur segment graduate seat and left the counting venue. Meanwhile, a triangular contest is taking place in Gorakhpur. SP is leading in Varanasi and Agra. Ajay Singh Advocate, an independent candidate for the Gorakhpur-Faizabad segment teacher seat, has alleged that 50 excess votes were found in the ballot box at the Mau Municipality polling booth. He has submitted a written objection. Following this, Additional Commissioner of Ayodhya Division, Ajay Saini, left the counting site. Akhilesh Yadav wrote on X: "Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar should ensure the results are transparent. Delays are being deliberately caused in the UP MLC vote counting. Votes are being counted at a slow pace." He further added, “The Election Commission should not make a mockery of democracy. If DMs and Commissioners attempt any form of dishonesty, we will launch an agitation and file lawsuits against them.” There are a total of 152 candidates in the elections held across 5 graduate and 6 teacher constituencies. The election was conducted using ballot paper, meaning winning and losing trends will emerge by this evening, with the final results expected after tomorrow afternoon.

stories.title: Which 10 seats has Swami Prasad sought from Congress?:Wants to launch BJP MLA daughter’s political career with Congress; plans to field her from Bilsi
stories.summary: Swami Prasad Maurya, president of the Apni Janata Party, wants to prove his political relevance in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Maurya, who has already announced an alliance with the Congress, had sought 12 seats. Sources say an agreement has been reached on 10 seats, subject to the condition that all candidates contest on the Congress symbol. Swami Prasad Maurya himself and his son, Utkrisht Maurya, will also contest elections on the Congress ‘hand’ symbol. To demonstrate his loyalty, Swami is soon planning to have his daughter, Dr Sanghamitra Maurya, join the Congress. She is preparing to contest the Assembly election from Bilsi. How beneficial will Swami Prasad Maurya be for the Congress? Which 10 seats has he sought? How influential are Maurya voters in Uttar Pradesh politics? Read the full report. Swami Prasad Maurya has a distinct identity in Uttar Pradesh politics. He began his political career with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) and has been an MLA five times. He was elected to the Assembly four times on a BSP ticket and once on a BJP ticket. Although he was born in Pratapgarh, his family lives in the Unchahar Assembly constituency in neighbouring Rae Bareli district. How beneficial will Swami be for the Congress? The Maurya-Kushwaha community in Uttar Pradesh includes sub-castes such as Koeri, Shakya, Saini and Kachhi. These extremely backward communities account for an estimated 6% to 15% of the state's population. They have a sizeable presence in Agra, Bareilly, Jaunpur, Ghazipur, Ballia, Mau, Kushinagar, Gorakhpur, Maharajganj, Mainpuri, Etawah, Kannauj, Badaun, Farrukhabad, Chandauli, Deoria, Fatehpur, Pratapgarh, Rae Bareli, Prayagraj, Kaushambi and several districts of Bundelkhand. Swami Prasad Maurya's family has influence in Kushinagar, Pratapgarh, Rae Bareli and Badaun districts. At present, most of this community's support goes to the BJP. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya also belongs to this community. Several other prominent leaders, including Amarpal Maurya and Baby Rani Maurya, are currently active in BJP politics. However, Swami Prasad Maurya also has his own support base within the community. When he was active in BSP politics, the party received considerable support from this community. Following his announcement of an alliance with the Congress, the party hopes to gain support from the community through him. This could be particularly beneficial in constituencies with a large Maurya-Kushwaha population where the BJP fields candidates from other castes. The Congress could then field candidates from the Maurya-Kushwaha community in these seats. Could Swami's alleged anti-Hindu stance become a liability for the Congress? According to senior journalist Yogesh Mishra, Swami Prasad Maurya's controversial statements were the main reason the Samajwadi Party (SP) distanced itself from him. This is why he wants to become part of the broader alliance through the Congress. Currently, the SP has the highest number of Maurya MPs in Uttar Pradesh, while the BJP has the highest number of Maurya MLAs. In such circumstances, it would be difficult for this community to abandon both parties and shift its support to a third party. Swami Prasad Maurya's politics has been anti-Hindu, according to Mishra. He directly abuses Hindu deities. However, the Maurya community is considered the second-largest vegetarian community after the Yadavs and is a community that follows Sanatan traditions. This raises questions about how much support Swami himself will receive from the Maurya community. At a time when politics has increasingly revolved around Sanatan traditions, the Congress's decision to align with a leader perceived as anti-Hindu also raises questions about its political judgement. Swami sought 12 seats in Congress alliance; these 10 are on the list Sources associated with the Congress say Swami Prasad Maurya initially sought 12 seats and has submitted a list of 10 constituencies. These include Unchahar in Rae Bareli; Padrauna and Fazilnagar in Kushinagar district; Pratapgarh Sadar; Phaphamau in Prayagraj; Bilsi in Badaun; Mauranipur and Babina in Jhansi district; Kalpi in Jalaun district; Tundla in Firozabad; and Charkhari in Mahoba district. Swami Prasad Maurya has been elected MLA from Padrauna in Kushinagar three times. He contested the 2022 Assembly election from Fazilnagar. He has sought the Unchahar seat for his son, Utkrisht Maurya. Utkrisht contested the 2017 Assembly election on a BJP ticket but lost to Manoj Pandey by a narrow margin. Meanwhile, Swami is preparing to field his daughter, Dr Sanghamitra Maurya, from Bilsi. The constituency falls under the Badaun Lok Sabha constituency. Sanghamitra was elected MP from Badaun in 2019. Here is the political equation in these 10 constituencies Swami Prasad Maurya is seeking 10 Assembly seats from the Congress. Most of these constituencies currently have BJP MLAs. Two seats were won by SP candidates in 2022, but those MLAs have since joined the BJP. In other words, apart from Unchahar and Kalpi, the SP does not currently hold any of the other eight seats on the list. This is one reason Swami Prasad Maurya is seeking these 10 constituencies from the Congress. Sources say the Congress has also agreed in principle to allocate these seats, on the condition that all candidates, including Swami Prasad Maurya, contest on the Congress symbol. Sanghamitra did not leave the BJP even when her father rebelled; why is she leaving now? Before the 2022 Assembly elections, Swami Prasad Maurya left the BJP and joined the Samajwadi Party. This created a political dilemma for Sanghamitra. Despite her father's departure from the BJP, she did not leave the party and continued to remain with it. However, she was denied a ticket in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. She still did not leave the party. She had hoped to secure a place in the state executive committee but was not included. She was also left out of the national executive committee. The Bilsi constituency from which she wants to contest the Assembly election already has a BJP MLA. It appears that she may join a party where she has a better chance of securing a ticket to fulfil her political ambitions. She had also secured the Lok Sabha ticket from Badaun with the help of her father, Swami Prasad Maurya. Now, owing to her father's bargaining power, she is expected to get the Bilsi ticket. However, she will have to join the Congress as a primary member in November to do so. Sources say an agreement has already been reached on this. Senior journalist Ratanmani Lal says, “Sanghamitra Maurya was never seen openly standing with the BJP while she was in the party. Her statements often reflected uncertainty. Her father, Swami Prasad Maurya, has repeatedly switched parties.” Why does Swami want Sanghamitra to contest from Bilsi? The discussion about Sanghamitra Maurya contesting from Bilsi is considered significant because the constituency falls under the Badaun Lok Sabha constituency. Harish Chandra Shakya of the BJP is currently the MLA from Bilsi. The BJP won the seat in the 2022 Assembly elections. Dalit, Muslim, Shakya-Maurya, Thakur and Brahmin voters are considered important to the electoral outcome in Bilsi. According to local estimates, Dalits account for around 20% of voters and Muslims for approximately 18%. Voters from the Maurya-Kushwaha, Yadav, Lodh and Vaishya communities could also influence the electoral equation.

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab’s impact:UP to turn colder despite storm being 1,000 km away; temperatures to drop by up to 8°C
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh may see a major change in weather due to Cyclone Arnab. According to the weather department, eastern UP and the Awadh region may receive heavy rain and strong winds from October 29 to 31. The surprising part is that the cyclone is not expected to reach UP directly, but it may still affect the state's weather. How can a cyclone hitting the Andhra Pradesh coast affect UP, which is around 1,000 km away? What changes can people expect, and how could farmers be affected? How can a cyclone in Andhra Pradesh affect UP? A cyclone is a large weather system that can spread across hundreds of kilometres. Even if its centre is near the Andhra Pradesh coast, its clouds and winds can pull moisture from the Bay of Bengal. As the system moves inland, it can change wind patterns and carry moisture towards areas far from the coast. This is how moisture-filled clouds may reach Uttar Pradesh even though the cyclone itself does not hit the state directly. What changes are expected in UP's weather? After reaching the coast, Cyclone Arnab is expected to weaken. The weather system may move inland towards the north through areas including Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha before affecting UP. By then, it is expected to have weakened considerably, but it may still carry a large amount of moisture. From October 29 to 31, eastern UP and the Awadh region may receive heavy rain. Dusty winds and storms with speeds of 40 to 50 kmph are also possible. Around 15 districts in eastern UP, including Prayagraj, Varanasi, Ballia, Mirzapur and Chandauli, may receive heavy to very heavy rain. Continuous rain and thick clouds may also bring a sharp drop in temperature. According to the weather department's forecast, temperatures could fall by 6 to 8 degrees Celsius, making the weather noticeably cooler. What damage could the cyclone cause in UP? Farmers may face the biggest losses because of unseasonal rain and strong winds. Paddy crops are ready for harvesting in many areas, while preparations are underway to sow wheat, potatoes and mustard. Paddy crops may suffer the most: Strong winds of 40 to 50 kmph could flatten standing paddy crops. If harvested paddy lying in the fields gets soaked, the grains may turn black and begin to rot. Vegetables and fruit crops: Waterlogging could damage cauliflower, tomato and chilli crops and their young plants. Banana and papaya trees may also break or fall due to strong winds. Delay in sowing wheat, mustard and potatoes: Farmers who plan to sow wheat, mustard or early potatoes may have to wait if their fields become waterlogged. Sowing could be delayed by 10 to 15 days, affecting the winter crop season. What precautions should farmers take? According to the information provided about the IMD and Agriculture Department guidelines, farmers should take the following steps: Harvest ready crops: If paddy or maize crops are 80% to 85% ripe, farmers should try to harvest them before October 28. Store harvested crops safely: Do not leave harvested crops in open fields. Keep them under a solid roof or on higher ground and cover them properly with a strong tarpaulin. Make arrangements to drain water: Prepare drainage channels in paddy, vegetable and fruit fields to prevent water from collecting. Avoid spraying and irrigation: Farmers should avoid applying fertilisers or pesticides and should not irrigate fields for the next three to four days, as advised in the source information. Report crop losses: Farmers covered under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana should report crop damage within 72 hours by calling the toll-free number 14447. How does a cyclone form? A cyclone forms when the sea surface becomes warm and heats the air above it. The warm air rises, creating a low-pressure area. Cooler air from nearby areas moves in to fill the space. Because the Earth rotates on its axis, the moving air begins to spin around the low-pressure area. When wind speeds rise above 63 kmph, the system is classified as a cyclone. According to the IMD timeline mentioned in the source information, a low-pressure area formed over the Bay of Bengal on October 23. It strengthened into a deep depression around 11:30 am on October 25 and developed into a cyclone during the night of October 25-26. It then became a severe cyclonic storm during the night of October 26-27. The system is moving at around 15 kmph. The weather department expects it to strengthen further before reaching the Andhra Pradesh coast on the morning of October 28. Winds could reach 120 kmph, with gusts of up to 140 kmph, along with very heavy rain. How have earlier cyclones affected UP? Cyclones that hit India's eastern or southern coasts have sometimes affected Uttar Pradesh through rain, strong winds and thick clouds even after weakening inland. The main risks in UP have included waterlogging, damage to crops and disruption to daily life. Cyclone Montha (October 2025): The cyclone formed over the Bay of Bengal and hit the Andhra Pradesh coast. It then moved through Telangana and Chhattisgarh towards UP. According to the source information, districts including Varanasi, Gorakhpur, Jaunpur and Sultanpur experienced heavy rain and winds of 40 to 50 kmph. The rain reportedly damaged harvested paddy lying in fields. Wet grains turned black, reducing their market value. Cyclone Fengal (November-December 2024): The cyclone hit the coast near Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. After affecting southern India, its cloud system moved north and interacted with a western disturbance already affecting UP. This was followed by colder weather in Lucknow, Kanpur, Bareilly, Agra and Noida. Dense fog, cold winds and light rain were reported in several districts. Day temperatures reportedly fell 5 to 7 degrees below normal in some areas. The rain and cooler weather helped wheat crops, but fog and cold conditions caused problems for daily travel and road traffic. Cyclone Dana (October 2024): The cyclone formed over the Bay of Bengal and hit the Odisha coast before moving towards eastern UP through Jharkhand. Prayagraj, Varanasi, Ghazipur, Chandauli and Mirzapur reportedly received rain for three days. Continuous rain and winds flattened paddy crops in fields and caused losses. The weather also delayed the sowing of early potatoes and mustard by around 10 days.

stories.title: Sahil's family accepts Muskaan as daughter-in-law:Sahil's lawyer will also fight her death penalty in HC
stories.summary: The family of Sahil has stepped forward to save Muskaan, who was handed the death sentence in Meerut's blue drum murder case. A single lawyer has filed a petition in the High Court seeking the commutation of the death penalty for both Sahil and Muskaan. Private advocate Sushil Shukla, representing Sahil's family, will also plead the case for Muskaan. He filed a joint petition on 23 October on behalf of both, in which Sahil's name is listed first, followed by Muskaan Rastogi's name below it. The fact that Sahil's lawyer will also represent Muskaan in the High Court has led to the belief that Sahil's family has accepted Muskaan as their daughter-in-law. Sahil's family regularly visits him in jail. Sahil's younger brother Divyansh Shukla, maternal grandmother, and his uncle visit him. Meanwhile, in the 18 months following the murder, no one from either her maternal or in-law's family has come to visit Muskaan to date. Jail Superintendent states: Sahil's family engaged the lawyer for Muskaan Senior Jail Superintendent of Meerut District Jail, Dr Viresh Raj Sharma, stated: “Sahil's family itself has engaged the lawyer to contest Muskaan's case. Earlier, Muskaan had expressed a desire to the jail administration to arrange a private lawyer for herself. Preparations were underway to provide her with a state-appointed lawyer. However, she later refused to take a state-appointed lawyer.” Muskaan herself informed that Sahil's lawyer would be representing her case as well. Senior High Court advocate Sushil Shukla is fighting the case for both of them. He alone is pleading in the High Court for the commutation of the death penalty for both. Sahil's family itself hired the lawyer for both of them. Muskaan and Sahil's friendship began at school; they grew close after her marriage Muskaan and Sahil alias Mohit's love story originally began at Vivekananda School in Brahampuri. Both Sahil and Muskaan studied together up to Class 8 in this school. They were friends and liked each other. After this, they separated and never met. Later, Muskaan married Saurabh. In 2019, Sahil reconnected with Muskaan through their school's WhatsApp group. Friendship developed between the two once again. Saurabh used to live abroad, leaving Muskaan alone. Muskaan also remained troubled due to Saurabh's drinking habit. Consequently, she grew closer to Sahil. Sahil wanted to be with Muskaan, so he began introducing her to drugs. Muskaan's daughter mostly stayed at her maternal grandmother's home. As a result, Muskaan moved around freely with Sahil and invited him to her house. Even Muskaan's family was unaware of their love story. Later, Saurabh came to know about their affair. Muskaan studied only up to Class 9 Muskaan's mother, Kavita, stated that Muskaan studied only up to Class 9 because her mind was not into studies. She had a completely different temperament. She herself declared that she did not want to study further, so she dropped out. Prior to the sentencing, Muskaan's parents had also given it in writing to the police that whatever punishment the court awards to Muskaan, they would neither ever meet her nor take any steps to seek commutation of her sentence. Muskaan wishes to meet her elder daughter, but to date, her parents have not allowed them to meet. They explicitly stated before the media that Muskaan is dead to them, and they will not allow even her shadow to fall upon the child. Under these circumstances, the biggest challenge before Muskaan was hiring a private advocate for herself. However, Sahil's lawyer, Sushil Shukla, will now represent both of their cases. Told neighbours that Sahil was her brother Where Muskaan and Saurabh lived as tenants, Muskaan, along with her boyfriend Sahil, committed Saurabh's murder. The neighbours living there also came to know about this murder case on 18 March. Neighbours revealed that these people lived there on rent, while Pihu stayed at her maternal grandmother's house. Muskaan did not talk to anyone. Sahil frequently visited her home. Only online food delivery delivery workers visited the house; otherwise, Sahil often arrived at Muskaan's house carrying boxes and bags. Muskaan had told the neighbours that Sahil was her brother, who brought food for her from home. Muskaan created a Snapchat account in the name of Sahil's deceased mother "If you slaughter (kill) Saurabh, your mother's soul will attain peace." "If you want to start a new and good life, you will have to marry Muskaan." "My last wish is that you marry Muskaan; only then will I find peace." These three messages were sent by Muskaan to Sahil. Meerut Police recovered 136 messages from Muskaan's Snapchat account. The police investigation revealed that Muskaan had created fake accounts in the names of Sahil's mother and sister. She repeatedly sent messages to Sahil from these accounts. She knew that Sahil believed in occult practices. He had even told Muskaan that he communicated with his mother's spirit. Taking advantage of this, she messaged him using the fake account created in his mother's name. Sahil made Muskaan commit Saurabh's murder by holding her hand The police investigation revealed that Sahil had brought Saurabh's head and severed hands to his room. During interrogation, Muskaan told the police that she had told Sahil he would have to slaughter Saurabh, only after which they could start a new life. Sahil made Muskaan kill her husband with her own hands. Sahil first made Muskaan sit on Saurabh's chest. He then brought a knife from the kitchen and gave it to her, teaching her how to hold it. He instructed her to drive the knife into Saurabh's heart three times. When Muskaan was unable to wield the knife, Sahil held her hands and forced her to stab the knife into his heart three times, committing the murder. After Saurabh's murder, the duo continued partying in Himachal After murdering Saurabh, Sahil and Muskaan went on a trip to Shimla, Kasol, and Manali, staying there for 15 days. There, they celebrated Holi, indulged heavily in drugs, and threw parties. Upon returning from this trip, when the case came to light and Muskaan was sent to jail, she was found to be pregnant. The duo spent the period from 5 to 17 March celebrating a honeymoon, staying in hotels across various locations, dancing, and indulging in debauchery. While pronouncing the death sentence, the judge stated: Muskaan and Sahil's mindset was fueled by lust On 14 October 2026, when District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra awarded the death sentence to Muskaan and Sahil in the Meerut District Court, he observed: Muskaan and Sahil have no remorse for Saurabh's murder. Their conduct following the crime reflects their repulsive mindset and lust. The District Judge noted: Murdering one's husband in his own home, dismembering the body, and the manner of destroying evidence shocks the conscience of society. There is no possibility of Muskaan and Sahil reforming or returning to the mainstream of society. Under these circumstances, there is no ground to grant them any leniency in sentencing. Muskaan had entered into a love marriage with her childhood lover Saurabh Rajput against the wishes of their families. Following the marriage, she re-established her relationship with her former school lover, Sahil. Owing to this illicit affair, Muskaan and Sahil murdered Saurabh, chopped his body into pieces, and hid them inside a blue drum.

stories.title: Formalin tanker overturns in Lucknow:Eye irritation reported up to 1 km away; road closed, SDRF and police deployed at site
stories.summary: A tanker carrying formalin overturned near the Manpur-Bama underpass on Kisan Path in the Bakshi Ka Talab (BKT) area of Lucknow at around 7:30 pm on Monday. After the accident, people within a radius of around one kilometre reported irritation in their eyes. BKT police reached the spot after receiving information. Teams from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and the fire brigade were also sent to the area. As a precaution, police barricaded the area around the accident site and stopped people from passing through it. The tanker was travelling from Sandila in Hardoi district to a factory in Gudamba when the accident occurred. Chemical being neutralised with help from factory staff Police said an area of more than one kilometre has been cordoned off, and vehicles approaching the site are being turned back. Police, fire service personnel, SDRF teams and staff from the nearby Flywood Varun factory are working to neutralise the chemical. Contact with formalin can cause irritation in the eyes, throat, nose and skin. People living in nearby areas may experience these symptoms. Medical teams are also present at the spot. Officials said there was no need to panic. Anyone experiencing irritation should wash the affected area with cold water.

stories.title: 10 lakh teachers in UP to get free treatment:Yogi Cabinet to meet tomorrow, over 16 proposals likely to be approved
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet will meet on Tuesday under the chairmanship of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Chief Secretary S.P. Goyal has issued the agenda, which includes 16 proposals for approval. The Cabinet will consider a proposal to provide cashless healthcare to teachers and employees working in aided and unaided secondary schools, Sanskrit schools and aided junior high schools under the Basic Education Council. Non-teaching staff working under the Samagra Shiksha project may also be included. Under the proposal, eligible teachers and employees will be able to get cashless treatment of up to ₹5 lakh. More than 10 lakh teachers and employees, along with their families, could benefit from the scheme. The total number of beneficiaries is expected to be around 50 lakh. Key proposals on the Cabinet agenda 1. Land for Sainik School: The government will consider providing 9.524 hectares of Gram Sabha land in Nauner, Mainpuri, free of cost for construction work at the Sainik School. 2. Education Services Tribunal Bill: A proposal will be placed to send the Uttar Pradesh Education Services Tribunal Bill, 2021, to the Government of India for amendments. 3. Four hospitals under the PPP model: The Cabinet will consider a proposal to run four hospitals in the state, each with 200 or more beds, under the public-private partnership (PPP) model. 4. Warehouses in Jhansi and Lalitpur: Free land will be provided to the State Warehousing Corporation to build warehouses in Jhansi and Lalitpur in the Bundelkhand region. 5. Subsidies for companies investing in UP: The Cabinet will consider providing subsidies to eligible companies under the investment promotion policy linked to foreign direct investment (FDI), foreign capital investment and Fortune 500 companies. 6. Housing for Allahabad High Court staff: A total of 845 houses will be built in Devghat-Jhalwa, Prayagraj, for Class-I and Class-II officials. These will include 533 Type-3 houses and 312 Type-4 houses. 7. Cybersecurity centre at IIT Kanpur: A proposal will be considered to set up the Uttar Pradesh Cyber Security Operations Centre (UP-COCS) at IIT Kanpur. 8. Panchayati Raj rules: The Cabinet will consider the 2026 rules for determining ordinary residence under the Uttar Pradesh Panchayati Raj Act. 9. State Livestock Mission: A proposal to establish a State Livestock Mission in Uttar Pradesh is also on the agenda. 10. Three link expressway projects: The Cabinet will consider selecting developers for two packages of the Farrukhabad Link Expressway, the link expressway connecting the Agra-Lucknow Expressway with the Purvanchal Expressway, and two packages of the Jhansi Link Expressway. 11. Global Capability Centre policy: Recommendations from a high-level committee under the Uttar Pradesh Global Capability Centre (GCC) Policy-2024 will be placed before the Cabinet for approval. 12. Changes to the Stamp Act: Amendments to certain sections and provisions of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, will be considered. 13. Inland Waterways Rules: The Cabinet will consider approving the Uttar Pradesh Inland Waterways Rules-2026. 14. Expansion of Prayagraj hospital: The capacity of Swaroop Rani Nehru Hospital, affiliated with Motilal Nehru Medical College in Prayagraj, is proposed to be increased from 1,250 beds to 3,000 beds.

stories.title: UP MLC election observer Abhay Singh removed:BJP rebel Devendra Singh had complained; 6 officials suspended in Agra
stories.summary: Abhay Singh has been removed as the observer for the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers' Constituency in the Uttar Pradesh MLC elections. IAS officer Prakash Bindu has been appointed in his place. According to an order issued by the Chief Electoral Officer, Abhay Singh has been relieved of his duties with immediate effect and placed in the reserve pool. Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa has directed Prakash Bindu, a 2009-batch IAS officer, to reach Gorakhpur immediately and oversee the vote counting, which begins on Tuesday. The decision came after BJP MLC and rebel leader Devendra Pratap Singh sent an email and complaint letter to the Chief Election Commissioner, demanding Abhay Singh's immediate removal. Abhay Singh faced controversy earlier In 2019, the CBI registered an FIR against Abhay Singh in a case related to illegal mining. At the time, he was the District Magistrate of Bulandshahr. The CBI had also recovered a large amount of cash from his residence. Citing the earlier case, Devendra Pratap Singh had questioned whether Abhay Singh could remain impartial as the election observer. He told the commission that appointing an officer linked to such a controversy to oversee counting in the sensitive Teachers' Constituency could raise concerns about possible irregularities. Election officer directs Prakash Bindu to reach Gorakhpur immediately Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa has directed Prakash Bindu to reach Gorakhpur immediately and oversee the counting of votes in the MLC elections, which begins on Tuesday. Who is Devendra Singh, whose complaint led to IAS Abhay Singh's removal? BJP MLC Devendra Pratap Singh, who represents the Gorakhpur-Faizabad seat, had shown signs of disagreement with the party before the elections. He wrote an open letter to teachers, urging them to vote against injustice and disrespect in the Legislative Council elections. He later accused officials of threatening teachers. The dispute began on October 12, during a teachers' conference in Gorakhpur. As Devendra Pratap Singh was going towards the stage, BJP regional president Vinod Rai asked him to step down from it. Devendra saw the incident as an insult. Since then, Devendra Singh has been unhappy with the BJP SP also raises questions over Lucknow Graduates' seat The Samajwadi Party has written to the returning officer of the Lucknow Graduates' Constituency, seeking booth-wise details of the number of voters and votes cast after polling. He said the government claimed to have freed Uttar Pradesh from mafias, but people linked to the ruling party and belonging to the same caste as the Chief Minister were displaying weapons and creating fear among poor people. “The government says from the stage that it has driven mafias out and freed the state from them. But mafias linked to the same party and belonging to the Chief Minister's caste are displaying weapons and spreading fear among the poor. Goondaism is at its peak under this government,” Chandrashekhar said. On October 20, Raja Bhaiya had performed the traditional weapon worship on Dussehra at his ancestral residence, Benti Raj Bhavan, in Pratapgarh. More than 500 small and large Indian and foreign weapons, including carbines, Mausers, pistols, revolvers and rifles, were displayed on tables. Chandrashekhar arrived in Phulpur at around 3 pm with a convoy of 30 vehicles to address a public meeting. Several supporters in the crowd carried posters of Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati. He said he was the ideological successor of Kanshi Ram, while another party was his political successor. He added that he had tried to work with Mayawati but could not succeed, so he was now working to strengthen his own movement. Five key points from Chandrashekhar's speech 1. Unemployment among youth and closure of schools Chandrashekhar said young people in Uttar Pradesh were unemployed despite holding degrees. He accused the state government of failing to provide jobs. He also said schools were closing while liquor shops were being opened, pushing young people towards alcohol. 2. Questions over voter lists and EVMs He alleged that irregularities had taken place in voter lists during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. He claimed that he was the one who had raised the issue of irregularities in the MLC elections. He called for the end of digital voter lists and said people wanted elections to be held using ballot papers instead of EVMs. 3. No alliance announced yet Chandrashekhar said his party had not formed an alliance with any party so far. He said alliances were decided at election time and that any alliance would be announced publicly. He added that his party would work closely with its alliance partners to remove the current government. 4. Claim about the party's election performance He said the Azad Samaj Party had contested two seats in the previous election and won one, while securing more than 80,000 votes on the other. He claimed that if the party had contested the remaining 78 seats as well, many opposition leaders would not have won their seats. 5. Claim that the Bahujan community has lost opportunities Chandrashekhar said that over the past nine and a half years, the Bahujan community had lost many opportunities. He claimed that government jobs had declined, employment had reduced and land mafias had taken away people's land. He also said that the right to education was affected as schools were shut down.

stories.title: UP BJP announces state working committee:Sinod Shakya joins SP in the morning, gets BJP committee membership by evening
stories.summary: In UP, the BJP released the list of the State Executive Committee-2026 on Monday. In the list issued by State President Pankaj Chaudhary, a total of 712 leaders have been included across three categories. These include 30 permanent invitee members, 134 special invitee members, and 548 state executive committee members. The notable highlight is that the BJP has also appointed 92-year-old Dr Murli Manohar Joshi as a permanent invitee member in the State Executive Committee. In this list, senior party leaders, Union ministers, state government ministers, MPs, and MLAs have been given places in different categories. Through this, the organizational structure at the state level has been expanded. Leaders from all six organizational regions of the state, including West, Braj, Kanpur, Awadh, Kashi, and Gorakhpur, have been included in the executive committee. PM Modi and CM Yogi permanent invitee members The list of permanent invitees includes PM Modi, CM Yogi, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, and both Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak. Apart from them, several senior leaders including former National President Dr Murli Manohar Joshi, former State Presidents Laxmikant Bajpai, Swatantra Dev Singh, Mahendra Nath Pandey, and Bhupendra Singh Chaudhary have also been given places. Among Union Ministers, the names of Hardeep Singh Puri, Jitin Prasada, S.P. Singh Baghel, B.L. Verma, Kamlesh Paswan, and Kirtivardhan Singh are included. Meanwhile, former Union Ministers Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi and Smriti Irani have also been made permanent invitee members. Hema Malini and Ravi Kishan special invitees 134 leaders have been included in the list of special invitees. These include Arun Singh, Surendra Nagar, Hema Malini, Arun Govil, Dr Mahesh Sharma, Ravi Kishan, Jagdambika Pal, Baby Rani Maurya, Suresh Khanna, Nand Gopal Nandi, Arvind Kumar Sharma, and Asim Arun, among other leaders. 548 members in State Executive Committee 548 leaders and party workers have been appointed as members of the State Executive Committee. They represent different districts and organizational regions of the state. The list includes leaders from the West, Braj, Kanpur, Awadh, Kashi, and Gorakhpur regions. Through these appointments in the party's organisational structure, representation has been given to leaders and workers from various regions of the state. 7 Muslim leaders included in the state working committee Seven Muslim leaders have been included in the BJP's state working committee list. They include three permanent invitees, one special invitee and three state working committee members. The permanent invitees are Tariq Mansoor, Kunwar Basit Ali and Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi. Danish Azad Ansari has been included as a special invitee. Ashfaq Saifi, Ghairul Hasan Rizvi and Haider Abbas Chand have been made state working committee members. With these appointments, a total of seven Muslim leaders have been included in the BJP's state working committee across the three categories. The BJP has released its Uttar Pradesh state working committee list for 2026, with 712 leaders included. Ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections, the list aims to honour senior leaders, balance regional and social representation, and give responsibilities to party workers. 1. Senior leaders given importance Former BJP national president Dr Murli Manohar Joshi, 92, has been made a permanent invitee. Joshi is associated with the Kashi region, where Prime Minister Narendra Modi is also an MP. 2. Focus on unity ahead of the 2027 elections Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, both Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, and ministers from the central and state governments have been included. This is seen as an effort to improve coordination between the government and the party organisation. 3. Representation for all six regions The BJP's six organisational regions in Uttar Pradesh—West, Braj, Kanpur, Awadh, Kashi and Gorakhpur—have been represented in the committee. This could help strengthen the party across the state. 4. Social groups and popular faces included The list includes leaders from different social groups, including OBC and Dalit communities. Popular figures Hema Malini, Arun Govil and Ravi Kishan have been made special invitees. The party hopes their popularity will help it connect with people at the local level. 5. Effort to reduce discontent among party workers The committee includes 548 members, giving responsibilities to leaders and workers at district and regional levels. The move could help keep workers active and reduce dissatisfaction within the party. The 712-member list is part of the BJP's preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections, with a focus on senior leaders, regional and social balance, and party unity.

stories.title: ‘कन्नौज के बाद अब आजमगढ़ की बारी’, ओपी राजभर बोले- अखिलेश यादव, PDA का सत्यानाश अपनी आंखों से देखने के लिए तैयार रहिए
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh News: उत्तर प्रदेश में विधानसभा चुनाव से पहले सुहेलदेव भारतीय समाज पार्टी (सुभासपा) के अध्यक्ष और कैबिनेट मंत्री ओम प्रकाश राजभर ने समाजवादी पार्टी के प्रमुख अखिलेश यादव पर निशाना साधा है। उन्होंने कहा कि अखिलेश यादव, आपके ‘काल्पनिक गढ़’ एक के बाद एक ढह रहे हैं, कन्नौज के बाद अब आजमगढ़ में भी आपकी विदाई का बाजा बजने वाला है। पीडीए के नाम पर जो ढकोसला फैला रखा है आपने उसका ‘सत्यानाश’ अब अपनी आंख से देखने के लिए तैयार रहिए। राजभर ने PDA की राजनीति पर सवाल उठाते हुए कहा कि राजभर, निषाद, चौहान, प्रजापति, पटेल और पाल समेत गैर-यादव पिछड़े समाज को सिर्फ चुनाव के समय याद करने का दौर अब खत्म हो गया है। उन्होंने कहा कि 29 नवंबर को आजमगढ़ में गैर यादव पिछड़ा और बहुजनों की असल ताकत देखकर आपकी बेखबरी का सारा नशा उतर जाएगा।

stories.title: 24th All India Science Fair to begin on November 27:Aims to foster innovation, creativity and practical knowledge among students
stories.summary: The 24th All-India Science Fair will be held from 27 to 29 November at Saraswati Shishu Mandir in Pakkibagh, Gorakhpur. A crucial meeting was held on Monday to discuss preparations for the event. Various arrangements, responsibilities and action plans were discussed in detail to make the fair grand, well-organised and successful. Organised by Vidya Bharati Akhil Bharatiya Shiksha Sansthan, the fair will promote a scientific approach, innovation, creativity and practical knowledge among students. National leadership provides guidance Addressing the meeting, Vidya Bharati National Organisation Secretary Govind Chandra Mahant and National President Dr Ravindra Kanhere guided the workers and teachers present. They highlighted key points related to the action plan of various departments, coordination of arrangements and the efficient fulfilment of responsibilities for the successful organisation of the science fair. They said that well-planned preparation, mutual coordination, timely action and the strength of dedicated workers play an important role in the success of any major event. All workers were expected to discharge their respective responsibilities with complete dedication, promptness and accountability so that this national-level event could set new benchmarks in excellence. Senior Office-Bearers Were Present Senior office-bearers of Vidya Bharati and affiliated educational organisations attended the important meeting. They included Regional Organisation Minister Hemchandra, Assistant Regional Organisation Minister Dr Ram Manohar, All-India Science Coordinator Nagendra Pandey, State Inspector of Shishu Shiksha Samiti Ram Singh, State Inspector of Jan Shiksha Samiti Jiyalal, Divisional Inspector for Gorakhpur Ajay Dubey and Divisional Inspector for Ballia Kanhaiya Chaubey. In addition, several subject experts and acharyas associated with science at the provincial and divisional levels were present. They offered important suggestions on planning the science fair, conducting its various activities and making the event more effective. At the beginning of the programme, the school's principal, Dr Rajesh Singh, introduced and welcomed the guests present. He expressed his gratitude to all the senior officials, office-bearers and subject experts who had come to the school campus for the planning meeting of the science fair.

Teen girl kills father for 5-month relationship:Crushes his head with a grinding stone in Etawah, hides body in a trunk
stories.summary: A man was killed by his 17-year-old daughter and her lover in Etawah. After the incident, they wrapped his body in a blanket, locked it inside a box and fled. Four days later, neighbours informed the police after a foul smell began coming from the house. The police revealed details of the incident, which took place on October 21, at 2:30 pm on Monday. They arrested the daughter and her lover and sent them to jail. The incident took place in the Civil Lines police station area. Full sequence of events Shyamsunder Katheria lived with his 17-year-old daughter on the premises of the TB Hospital in Kanshiram Colony, Etawah. He worked as a security guard at a hotel. His elder daughter, Kajal, is married and lives with her in-laws in Bhikanpur village in Jaswantnagar. According to SSP Brijesh Kumar Srivastava, the girl told investigators that around five months ago, she had asked her elder sister, Kajal, to recharge her mobile phone. Kajal shared her younger sister's number with her husband, who got it recharged through his friend Abhilash Singh (21), a resident of Matantola Aheiripur. Abhilash works as a labourer. After recharging the number, Abhilash started talking to the girl. When her father, Shyamsunder, found out about their relationship, he began opposing it. He tried to counsel his daughter several times, but when she did not listen, he assaulted her. This led the girl to develop resentment towards her father. Daughter planned father's murder The girl wanted to live with her boyfriend, Abhilash. According to the police, she conspired with him to kill her father, Shyamsunder. On October 21, the girl allegedly mixed sleeping pills into her father's tea. After he fell into a deep sleep, the two tied him to a charpoy. They then attacked his neck with a knife and hit his head several times with a grinding stone, killing him. Body hidden in a trunk, mobile phone thrown into a drain After the murder, the two allegedly tried to hide the evidence. They first tried to put the body in a fridge, but it did not fit. They then wrapped the body in a blanket and placed it inside a trunk. They also threw Shyamsunder's mobile phone into a drain before fleeing the scene. Neighbours alert police after noticing foul smell On Sunday, October 25, neighbours became suspicious after noticing a foul smell coming from inside the room. They informed the police, who broke open the lock and entered the house. The police recovered Shyamsunder's body from the trunk. The police then informed his elder daughter, Kajal, about the murder. Kajal told them that she had been unable to contact her father and younger sister for the past three to four days. On Monday, Kajal filed a murder complaint against her younger sister and her boyfriend at the Civil Lines police station. Daughter found at boyfriend's house On Monday, police were checking vehicles near Gwalior Tiraha in the Civil Lines area when they received information that the girl and her boyfriend, Abhilash, were in Sarai Esar village. The police reached the village and arrested Abhilash Singh near the check road. During questioning, he told the police that the girl was at his house. The police then took her into custody from his house. The police also recovered a grinding stone, a knife, bloodstained clothes and the trunk allegedly used in the crime.

stories.title: 'After 2027, Congress leaders will dance on streets':BJP MP Ravi Kishan on Kharge's statement, says entire Congress has lost its mental balance
stories.summary: BJP MP Ravi Kishan Shukla strongly criticised Congress national president Mallikarjun Kharge over his recent statement on Monday. He said Congress leaders were frustrated and had lost their mental balance after seeing the BJP move ahead. He added that after 2027, Congress leaders would beat their chests and dance on the streets. Speaking to people at his residence in Gorakhpur on Monday morning, Ravi Kishan said such language was not expected from a senior leader like Kharge. He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi's father was no longer alive, yet comments were still being made about him. He said this showed the thinking of Congress leaders and their frustration. Ravi Kishan also said Congress leaders knew they had no political future left. He claimed that 10 lakh people had gathered in Varanasi to see the Prime Minister, while Congress leaders could not even fill a hall with a capacity of 500 people. He said this was the reason behind their frustration. They start having epileptic seizures as soon as they see the Prime Minister's face Ravi Kishan said that whenever Congress leaders see Prime Minister Narendra Modi's face, they start having epileptic seizures. Their mental condition will worsen further after the 2027 Assembly elections. He said that using such derogatory language about the Prime Minister's father was against Indian civilisation, culture, values, moral principles and decency. Was such language used at the behest of the Gandhi family? Ravi Kishan also shared a post on his Facebook wall condemning the incident. He said he wanted to ask Sonia Gandhi whether Kharge had used such language at the behest of the Gandhi family and, if not, whether Congress would ask him to resign. He said the Prime Minister was held in the hearts of crores of people. The country would not tolerate insults to him and his family. Congress should answer whether such indecent language was in keeping with the dignity of the office of national president.

stories.title: 63-year-old man dies by suicide in Gorakhpur:Records video accusing landlord and his wife of harassment
stories.summary: A 63-year-old man died after consuming poison at his shop in Gorakhpur. Before the incident, he had recorded a video accusing his landlord and the landlord's wife of mentally harassing him by involving him in false cases. He held them responsible for his death. After receiving information about the incident, his family rushed to the shop and found him unconscious. They called an ambulance and took him to the hospital, where he died late on Sunday night during treatment. The police took his body into custody and sent it for a post-mortem examination. Further investigation is underway. The case falls under the Kotwali police station area. What happened? Shadab Khan, a resident of Bakshipur, told the police that his 63-year-old uncle, Nazir Ahmad Khan, also known as Pappu, had consumed a poisonous substance at his shop at around 3 pm on Sunday. The family members said they found a video on their mobile phone on Monday. After watching it, they filed a written complaint against the accused at the police station. In the 1-minute-30-second video, Nazir Ahmad Khan said he was taking this step because he was troubled by his landlord, Anoop Kumar Jaiswal, who lives in Bakshipur under the Kotwali police station area, and the landlord's wife. The police have started an investigation into the case. The allegations made in the video are being investigated. He had accused him of molesting his wife They would regularly harass me over one matter or another. Some time ago, Anoop had accused me of molesting his wife. I presented evidence at the Kotwali police station and managed to prove my innocence. Now, a case has been filed over something else, which I know nothing about. The police came, conducted an inquiry, submitted their report and left. They said that something or the other was being done to the shop without notice. The water pipe has been broken, and no one can even stand inside the shop. I am distressed, and therefore I am ending my life. Police engaged in investigation Shadab Khan said that the deceased was unmarried and had no children. The Kotwali station house officer said that the body had been sent for post-mortem. An FIR has been registered and further action is under way. The situation at the spot is peaceful.

stories.title: Violent clash at Lohia Hospital’s main gate:Two groups attack each other with sticks, overturn several roadside stalls
stories.summary: A fight broke out between two groups on Monday outside Gate No. 8 of Lohia Hospital in the Vibhutikhand police station area of Lucknow. The argument soon turned violent, with both groups attacking each other with sticks. Someone at the spot recorded the incident, and the video later spread widely on social media. The video shows several young men chasing and beating each other with sticks. The fight caused chaos in the area. Patients face problems The fight caused problems for people who had come to Lohia Hospital for treatment. They could not enter the hospital through the gate while the clash was going on. The fight continued for around half an hour. Even after the police arrived following a complaint, the men involved in the fight continued attacking each other in front of them. Some people who had come to the hospital for treatment had stepped outside to buy food and drinks. When a roadside cart was overturned during the clash, their food also spilled onto the ground.

stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh News: उत्तर प्रदेश में प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी को लेकर कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष मल्लिकार्जुन खरगे की टिप्पणी पर मंत्री योगेंद्र उपाध्याय ने अपनी प्रतिक्रिया दी है। उन्होंने खड़गे के बयान पर नाराजगी जताते हुए कहा कि अभद्र भाषा का इस्तेमाल करना उनकी संस्कृति का हिस्सा है। उपाध्याय ने अपनी बात रखते हुए कहा कि अगर किसी व्यक्ति को तोहफा नहीं दिया जाता है, तो वह कुछ समय के लिए रोता है। लेकिन अगर किसी व्यक्ति को मूल्य नहीं सिखाए जाते हैं, तो वह जीवन भर रोता है। उन्होंने कहा कि जब किसी राजनीतिक व्यक्ति में मूल्यों की कमी होती है, तो वह केवल खुद ही नहीं रोता, बल्कि अपने बयानों से पूरे समाज और देश को भी रुलाता है। मंत्री ने आगे कहा कि ये वही लोग हैं जिनके नेतृत्व में मूल्यों की कमी है और इसी वजह से इस तरह के बयान दिए जाते हैं।

stories.title: Yogi says India has two ‘Miyans’, one junior, one senior:Accuses them of favouring Bangladeshi infiltrators in Kanpur
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will visit Bithoor in Kanpur today for Valmiki Jayanti. He will offer prayers at the historic Maharishi Valmiki Ashram there. He will then address a public meeting at Nanarao Peshwa Park. During the visit, he may announce development projects worth around ₹400 crore for the Bithoor and Bilhaur Assembly constituencies. The district administration has completed preparations for the Chief Minister's visit. On Sunday evening, officials reviewed the security arrangements at the public meeting venue, including the stage and the park. See 3 pictures... Programme to begin at 10 a.m. Activities at the public meeting venue will begin at 10 a.m. as part of the Chief Minister's programme. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will then arrive in Bithoor. He will first pay his respects at the Maharishi Valmiki Ashram, followed by an address at a public meeting in Nanarao Peshwa Park. According to the proposed programme, the Chief Minister may remain in Bithoor for around 2 hours. During this time, he will also review exhibitions set up by various departments. Development projects worth ₹400 crore likely to be announced Development projects worth around ₹400 crore are likely to be announced for the Bithoor and Bilhaur Assembly constituencies at the Chief Minister's public meeting. Preparations have been made for the foundation-laying ceremonies and inaugurations of several development works under these projects. For this, details of projects have been sought from various departments, including the Public Works Department (PWD), Kanpur Development Authority (KDA), nagar panchayat and nagar palika. Beneficiaries of 10 schemes to be honoured The Chief Minister may also honour beneficiaries of various government schemes during the public meeting. The key schemes include: Old-age Pension Scheme Chief Minister Housing Scheme Ration Card Scheme Tool Kit Distribution Scheme Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Scheme Preparations are also under way to honour beneficiaries of other schemes. Beneficiaries of around 10 schemes may be included in the programme. Political discussion over CM's visit after By-election Political circles are also abuzz with discussion over the Chief Minister's visit to Bithoor. Earlier this month, the elder brother of MLA Abhijeet Singh Sanga won the by-election for Nagar Panchayat chairperson in the Bithoor area. In this context, the Chief Minister's visit after the by-election is being considered important not only from the perspective of regional development but also politically.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav says ‘we want power, not sainthood’:Welcomes 4 BJP leaders to SP, gives house keys to 5 beneficiaries
stories.summary: Former Uttar Pradesh-cadre IAS officer Ram Bahadur Pasi, who was close to Mayawati, joined the Samajwadi Party on Monday, 26 October. Several prominent leaders from Badaun, Meerut and other districts also joined the SP in the presence of Akhilesh Yadav and Shivpal Singh Yadav. This is being seen as a major step in terms of the SP's PDA strategy. Who is Ram Bahadur Pasi? Ram Bahadur, a PCS officer of the 1977 batch, was promoted to the IAS in 2010 and retired in 2015. He has held key positions such as District Magistrate of Gonda and Vice-Chairman of the Lucknow/Ghaziabad Development Authority (LDA). In 2017, he contested the Mohanlalganj seat on a BSP ticket but lost to the Samajwadi Party candidate by a margin of just 530 votes. He subsequently formed the Nagrik Ekta Party and joined the BJP in 2022. He is now beginning a new innings with the Samajwadi Party. After joining the Samajwadi Party, Ram Bahadur Pasi said, "I feel fortunate that the national president inducted me into the Samajwadi Party, and I thank him. I was in service until 2015. Akhilesh Yadav was the Chief Minister when I retired." Sabina Parveen enters politics after returning from the United States Sabina Parveen, who returned from the United States, also joined the Samajwadi Party. She said, "I have not come to join the SP; I have come to become part of Akhilesh Yadav's movement. People are leaving India, while I am returning from the United States. We have to fulfil the dreams our ancestors had seen. I want to work in the education, health, research and development sectors." Sabina has expressed her desire to work at the grassroots level in the Kundarki Assembly constituency and become the SP candidate. Prominent figures from Budaun, Meerut and other districts also join the party Other prominent figures joining the party include- After joining the Samajwadi Party, Dara Singh Prajapati said, "I have not joined for a ticket or for an adjustment. I have joined the SP to make Akhilesh Yadav the chief minister." Mantosh Yadav, who builds houses for the poor, honoured During the programme, Akhilesh Yadav honoured Mantosh Yadav, who builds houses for the poor and provides them for just ₹5 lakh. The keys to their new homes were also handed over to five beneficiaries on stage. Senior SP leader Shivpal Singh Yadav, along with MPs Awadhesh Prasad (Ayodhya), Harendra Malik (Muzaffarnagar), Aditya Yadav (Badaun) and the Aonla MP, was also present.

stories.title: Lucknow triple murder over car parking dispute:Neighbour opens fire, killing father, son and brother; son was to marry on December 5
stories.summary: Three members of a family were shot dead in broad daylight in Lucknow on Monday. The victims were a father, his son and the father's younger brother. The father and son died on the spot, while the brother died at a trauma centre. The incident took place at around 10:35 am in the Saadatganj police station area. Shivaji Tiwari (62), who lived in Brahmin Tola in Naubasta, was a retired Secretariat employee. He had also served as the district-level general secretary of the RSS. His brother, Shivendra Tiwari, also known as Shambhu, worked at Lucknow University. Shivaji's son, Suyash (30), ran an electrical goods business. He was scheduled to get married on December 5. On Monday, Suyash parked his car near a raised platform in the area. A short while later, when Shambhu came outside, Rishabh started arguing with him over the parking. Hearing the argument, Shivaji also came out of the house. During the dispute, Rishabh lost his temper and shot both of them. When Suyash came out after hearing the gunshots, Rishabh shot him on the stairs near the house. Rishabh (30) worked as a navigation officer in the Merchant Navy. He was reportedly removed from his job. Police Commissioner Tarun Gaba visited the crime scene. Around 50-60 police personnel have been deployed at the spot. See pictures

stories.title: 3 sisters’ funeral processions leave together in Firozabad:Mother repeatedly faints; father dies of shock after son’s death
stories.summary: An accident in Firozabad devastated an entire family. Five people from the same village died, including three biological sisters. When the three sisters' funeral biers were carried out together, the entire village broke down in tears. Their mother became hysterical on seeing her daughters' bodies. She kept losing consciousness as she wept. Meanwhile, the father could not bear the shock of his son's death. He too, having been battling cancer, passed away. Six people from the village have now died in the accident, while 10 others are injured. The accident took place at around 9 p.m. on Sunday in Chhatanpur village under Nasirpur police station, about 35 kilometres from the district headquarters. After collectively arranging the marriage of Tesu and Jhanjhi, villagers were heading outside the village towards a beri tree for the immersion ceremony. At that point, a Delhi-registered Brezza car coming from the Lucknow-Agra Expressway ran over the villagers walking along the roadside. See the pictures below : Learn about the accident At around 9 p.m. on Sunday, villagers in Chhatanpur village, under the Nasirpur police station area, were heading towards a Bari tree outside the village for immersion after collectively solemnising the marriage of Tesu and Jhanjhi. Women, men and children were moving ahead while singing traditional wedding songs. Meanwhile, a Delhi-registered Brezza car coming from the Lucknow-Agra Expressway ran over the villagers walking along the roadside. Babli, 18, the daughter of Brajesh from the village, died in the accident. After the death, the car driver sped away towards Shikohabad. The villagers pursued the car on motorcycles and reached a spot near a hospital around 9 kilometres away, where they tried to surround it. Seeing himself surrounded, the driver hit a motorcycle and again drove the car towards the accident site. Car occupants flee after hitting someone, return to run them over when surrounded As the car fled, it ran over around 15 villagers again. This time, three daughters of Shishupal Yadav of the village-Akanksha (17), Anjali (15) and Gunnu (10)-and Harish Kumar (25), the son of Gambhir Singh, died on the spot. Chandraveer (55), the son of Amar Singh; Umashankar (40), the son of Ram Brajesh; Dheeraj (30) and Sonu (29), the sons of Sukhveer; and Mayank (11), Chandraveer's son, were among 10 people injured. All of them were admitted to the district hospital, where they are undergoing treatment. After the accident, villagers caught the four youths in the car and beat them with sticks. The police then reached the spot, rescued them from the crowd and took them to the police station. It is reported that the occupants of the car were intoxicated at the time of the accident. After the accident, District Magistrate Santosh Kumar Sharma, Senior Superintendent of Police Aditya Langhe and other officials visited the hospital and took stock of the situation. Witnesses said: The driver had been drinking Shivani, an eyewitness to the incident, said the car hit people from the village. The driver had been drinking. After hitting them once, he drove away. He returned and hit them again. The identities of two people travelling in the car have been established. They include Aqeel and Irfan, residents of Wazirpur in Delhi. Two of them are also reported to be in serious condition after being beaten. Now read the village report The family is devastated following the deaths of Sishupal's three daughters, Akanksha, Anjali and Gunnu, in the accident. His wife Radha and two sons, Govind and Babu, are inconsolable. When the funeral biers of all three daughters were carried out together, hundreds of villagers were moved to tears. While Babli's father Brajesh is employed as a peon at JS University, his wife Sangeeta also fainted after crying uncontrollably. Villagers helped her. Meanwhile, Harish's father, who lost his life in the accident, was suffering from advanced cancer. He had been undergoing treatment in Lucknow for a long time. Harish's wife Soni was inconsolable. Harish had got married three years ago. They had a son a year ago. However, the child died soon after birth. Harish's mother Kanti Devi and brothers Monu and Suraj were devastated. When Harish's father, who was admitted to a hospital in Lucknow, was informed of his death, he too suffered a deep shock. He died shortly afterwards. Relatives are bringing his body to Firozabad.

stories.title: Teen falls 30 feet from overbridge, dies in UP:Parents faint on seeing son's body; had gone out to get guitar
stories.summary: Only son died after falling 30 feet from an overbridge in Sant Kabir Nagar. The teenager fell face down onto the road below. The accident occurred at around 12 midnight. The boy's parents fainted after seeing his body. Police, who reached the spot after receiving information from local residents, sent the body for a post-mortem examination. The teenager was identified as Shashwat Rai (17). His father, Sanjay Rai, is a government teacher at the Composite School in Gagani Babu, under the Mehdawal development block. His mother, Anita Rai, is a private teacher at Blooming Buds private school. Shashwat was originally a resident of the Awal Kewatliya locality in Mehdawal. The family had been living in a rented house in Khalilabad city for the past five years. According to his family, Shashwat left home at around 8 p.m. on a bike to fetch his guitar. Shashwat also had a four-year-old sister.

stories.title: Bank manager’s wife dies after sudden fall at hotel:Head injury proves fatal; couple married four months ago in Jhansi
stories.summary: A bank manager's wife died at a hotel in Jhansi. The couple had married just four months earlier. They had booked a room at the hotel and checked in on Saturday. The next day, as they were preparing to check out, the woman, who was standing at the room's door, suddenly fell backwards, landing on her head and suffering a severe head injury. Blood spread across the floor. Her husband picked her up and carried her into the room before taking her to a nearby hospital with the help of the hotel staff, where doctors declared her dead. The incident took place in the Seepri Bazaar police station area at 12 noon on Sunday. CCTV footage of the incident has also emerged. It shows the woman walking towards the room with her husband and a hotel employee. The employee and her husband enter the room, while the woman follows them to the door. Within four seconds, she collapses while standing. According to the police, the deceased, Muskaan (27), was staying at Hotel Rishabh with her husband, Nilesh (33). Nilesh is a resident of Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh, and is posted as a society manager at MP Gramin Bank. Muskaan's father has accused his son-in-law of murder. Watch two CCTV clips- Married four months earlier and had come to her maternal home for examination Ramjilal Simoliya, who lives in Nainagarh, Premnagar, said, "My daughter Muskaan married Nilesh on 29 June. We held her wedding with great fanfare at Hotel JS Grand. Muskaan's JE exam was scheduled for 28 October, so we brought her home on 10 October. I thought she would sit the exam and stay with me for a few days." "We had no idea that Nilesh would suddenly arrive at night and take Muskaan away early in the morning. Nilesh arrived at around 11:30 pm on the night of 23 October. The next day, he lied to me and took Muskaan with him. He said he was going to his maternal aunt's house in Ganesh Vihar Colony. I told him, 'Go on, son.'" "On Sunday, Nilesh called and said, 'Please come to Rudra Hotel at Chitra Chauraha.' There is no Rudra Hotel in our area. When we searched, we found out that it was Rishabh Hotel. When we reached Rishabh Hotel, we found that instead of taking Muskaan to his maternal aunt's house, he had taken her to the hotel. The hotel register showed their entry from 23 to 24 October." Son-in-law called us to the nursing home Ramjilal said that while they were at the hotel, Nilesh called again and asked them to come to Kapoor Nursing Home. They reached Kapoor Nursing Home, but Nilesh was not there either. Nilesh called them again and asked them to come first to the medical college and then to the Civil Hospital. When they reached the Civil Hospital, they found Muskaan dead there. Nilesh says that Muskaan had fallen. However, I suspect that he grabbed my Muskaan by the face and hit her head against the wall. She has suffered an injury to her head. Father-in-law says: Son-in-law had relationships with other women Ramjilal Simauliya said, "Nilesh used to work in a private job. He got a job at a bank just 15 days ago. He has relationships with other women. He already has a wife who lives in Indore. We learnt this after our daughter's wedding. He would repeatedly tell my daughter, 'My first wife is better. You do not have what she has.'" SP City says cause of death will be known after post-mortem SP City Preeti Singh said, When the police reached the hospital, the husband was present there. He said they were checking out and were going to the room with the hotel staff to collect their belongings. Muskaan suddenly fell at that point. The police reached the hotel and inspected the scene. The couple had stayed in room number 212. CCTV footage is being examined. The allegations made by the deceased's father are being investigated. The cause of death will become clear after the post-mortem report is received.

stories.title: Brother kills sister over interfaith marriage in Mathura:Buries body in cemetery; she married Hindu man 4 months ago
stories.summary: In Mathura, a brother strangled his sister to death for marrying a man from another religion. He then buried her body. When her husband called her from Rajasthan, her phone was switched off. After he was unable to contact her despite making considerable efforts for 15 days, he called her family and asked about her. At first, they kept evading the question, and then stopped answering his calls. He suspected that something had happened to her. He subsequently informed the police at a police station in Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan, that his wife had been kidnapped. Rajasthan Police emailed Mathura Police on 23 October, asking them to investigate the case. Following this, police from the Govind Nagar police station in Mathura began making inquiries. Police first questioned the young woman's family. They continued to give evasive replies. Initially, they said they did not know where the girl was. Later, her brother said that she had died after suffering an electric shock. On the night of 24 October Police detained the brother on suspicion. During questioning, he repeatedly said that his sister had died from an electric shock, but when the police put him under pressure, he said that he had strangled her to death and buried her body in a cemetery. On Sunday, the young woman's body was exhumed from the cemetery on the orders of the city magistrate and sent for a post-mortem examination. The brother, who is accused of the murder, has been arrested. The police are questioning the mother and maternal aunt after taking them into custody. The case relates to the Govind Nagar police station area of Mathura. Read the full case in detail They fell in love after working together in Delhi for two years According to the police, Nazia, also known as Jannat, who lived in Badrinagar Nai Basti in Mathura, worked at a factory in Delhi that manufactured sportswear. It was there that she met Ravindra, a resident of Pacherikalan village in Rajasthan's Jhunjhunu district. They became friends after talking to each other. Their friendship then turned into an affair, which continued for two years. When they told their families about their relationship, Ravindra's family agreed, but Nazia's family did not agree to the marriage. Marriage four months ago When Nazia's family refused to accept the relationship, she left home four months ago. She then married Ravindra. For three months, Nazia's family kept asking her to sever ties with him, but she refused. After this, her family pretended to accept the relationship. On 25 September, Nazia's mother and maternal aunt somehow lured her to Mathura by engaging her in conversation. After she stayed there for a few days and said she wanted to return, her family began opposing her. Husband grew suspicious when Nazia did not return even after 15 days When Nazia did not return even 15 days after going to her parents' home, her husband grew suspicious. He then called Nazia's family members. At first, they kept evading him. Later, they stopped answering his calls. Ravindra then began fearing that something untoward had happened. Ravindra lodged an FIR alleging that his wife had been kidnapped in Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan. On 23 October, Rajasthan Police sent an email to Mathura Police to register the FIR and investigate the case. Police questioned her brother The investigation was handed over to the Govind Nagar police station. When the police questioned the family, they continued to give evasive answers. On the basis of suspicion, the police took the girl's brother, Akram, into custody late on Saturday night. The police then questioned him about how his sister had died. Initially, he said that she had died of electrocution. But when the police applied pressure, he told them that he had strangled his sister to death and buried her body in the cemetery after the murder. Body exhumed on City Magistrate's orders The police then arrested Akram and informed senior officials about the case. Following this, the cemetery was dug up on Sunday on the orders of City Magistrate Anupam Mishra. Nazia's body was exhumed and sent for a post-mortem examination. Akram was also arrested. The police are now waiting for the post-mortem report. SP says investigation report awaited SP City Rajiv Kumar Singh said the matter had come to his notice. The young woman's body was exhumed from the cemetery and sent for a post-mortem examination. The incident is being investigated. As the investigation is still under way, it would be premature to say anything about it.
