stories.title: Rahul Gandhi acquitted in Shah defamation case after 8 years:Judge delivers verdict in 16 minutes; 3 reasons behind court’s decision
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has been acquitted by the MP-MLA court in the defamation case linked to Amit Shah. Rahul was present in court when the verdict was delivered. He appeared before the MP/MLA court in Sultanpur in an eight-year-old defamation case related to his remarks about Union Home Minister Amit Shah. During the previous hearing, Rahul Gandhi's legal team had submitted written arguments. The Congress MP had admitted that he made the remarks against Amit Shah in 2018 in good faith. He said his intention was not to defame anyone. The case was related to remarks Rahul Gandhi made about Amit Shah in Bengaluru in 2018. During the previous hearing, Santosh Pandey, the lawyer for complainant Vijay Mishra, had said that Rahul Gandhi had accepted the incident and his speech. He urged the court to find Rahul Gandhi guilty. According to Congress district president Abhishek Singh Rana, Congress workers from the Kurebhar, Dhanpatganj and Jaisinghpur blocks will welcome Rahul Gandhi at 9:30 am after he enters the area from the Purvanchal Expressway. At 9:40 am, workers from the Kadipur, Akhandnagar, Karaundikala, Motigarpur and Dostpur blocks will welcome him at the Tatiya Nagar bypass. At 9:45 am, Congress workers from the PP Kamicha, Lambhua and Bhadainya blocks will be present at Tedhui intersection to welcome him. At 9:55 am, teams from the Youth Congress and the National Students' Union of India (NSUI) will welcome him in front of Aastha Hospital in Golaghat. At 10 am, workers from the Baldirai, Kudwar and Dubepur blocks will welcome him at the Golaghat Diwani turn. Members of the City Congress Committee and other local leaders will welcome him at the gate of the District Court. Convoy collides in Sultanpur Earlier on Monday morning, vehicles in Rahul Gandhi’s convoy collided on the Purvanchal Expressway in Sultanpur. Five vehicles travelling behind the convoy and an ambulance were involved in the accident. Some people sustained minor injuries. Rahul Gandhi was travelling to Sultanpur to appear before the MP/MLA court. The Special Investigation Team (SIT) will now investigate the accident. The Uttar Pradesh Director General of Police (DGP) has formed the SIT. The SIT comprises three officers and will be headed by Lucknow Range IG Kiran S. Sultanpur ASP Brij Narayan Singh and DSP (Traffic) Ram Krishna Chaturvedi will also be part of the investigation. The SIT will investigate the exact cause of the accident and examine any lapses in security or traffic management. It will also recommend measures to prevent such incidents in the future and submit its report to police headquarters as soon as possible. In this eight-year-old defamation case, Rahul had admitted that he made a statement against Amit Shah in 2018 in good faith. He said his intention was not to defame anyone. Vijay Mishra, a BJP leader from Sultanpur, filed the case against Rahul in August 2018. The allegation is that Rahul made the statement during a press conference in Bengaluru, Karnataka, on 8 May 2018: “The president of a party that talks about honesty is accused of murder.” Welcome to be held at different locations According to Congress district president Abhishek Singh Rana, Congress workers from Kurebhar, Dhanpatganj and Jaisinghpur blocks will welcome Rahul Gandhi at 9:30 a.m. after he gets off the Purvanchal Expressway. At 9:40 a.m., workers from the Kadipur, Akhandnagar, Karaundikala, Motigarpur and Dostpur blocks will welcome him at the Tatiya Nagar bypass. At 9:45 a.m., Congress workers from PP Kameicha, Lambhua and Bhadaiya will be present at Tedhui Tiraha. At 9:55 a.m., the Youth Congress and NSUI teams will welcome him outside Aastha Hospital in Golaghat. At 10 a.m., workers from the Baldirai, Kudwar and Dubeypur blocks will welcome him at Golaghat's Diwani Mod. The City Congress Committee and other local leaders will welcome him at the gate of the civil court. Case against Rahul was filed in 2018 BJP leader Vijay Mishra from Sultanpur filed a defamation case against Rahul Gandhi in the MP/MLA court in August 2018. Mishra said, "On 8 May 2018, Rahul held a press conference in Bengaluru, Karnataka. The Congress leader had said, 'Amit Shah is an accused in a murder case.' The Supreme Court mentioned this in the Judge Loya case. Therefore, I do not believe that Amit Shah has any credibility. The president of a party that speaks of honesty and probity is an accused in a murder case." During the 2018 Karnataka Assembly election, Rahul Gandhi allegedly made the comment about Amit Shah, who was the BJP president at the time, at a rally in Bengaluru. Rahul Gandhi is alleged to have said that the BJP spoke of honest politics, but its president was an accused in a murder case. Amit Shah's name was linked to the 2005 alleged fake encounter case involving Sohrabuddin Sheikh. However, in 2014, a special CBI court in Mumbai discharged him from the charges in the case. When did Rahul Gandhi appear for the first time? The MP/MLA court in Sultanpur summoned Rahul Gandhi in the case on 27 November 2023. Rahul Gandhi subsequently appeared in court on 20 February 2024 and secured bail. Two sureties of ₹25,000 each were furnished for this. Rahul Gandhi's statement in the case was recorded in court on 26 July 2024. During this, he presented his side regarding the allegations against him. Demand for voice sample comparison rejected A CD was submitted to the court on behalf of complainant Vijay Mishra. A request was made to have the voice recorded on it matched with Rahul Gandhi's voice sample through the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL). The trial court rejected the application on 2 May. After this, the complainant's side filed an application in the Sessions Court. The Sessions Court also rejected it on 15 July. The decision was then challenged in the High Court. In September, it came to light that a petition related to matching the voice sample had been filed. Following this, proceedings in the final arguments in the case moved forward. Two sections invoked against Rahul A case has been registered against Rahul Gandhi under Sections 499 and 500 in this matter. Section 499 deals with spreading false rumours about someone, making comments about them and defaming them. Section 500 provides for punishment for defamation. Rahul could face up to two years in prison in this case. Rahul's Parliament membership was cancelled in a defamation case Rahul Gandhi's membership of Parliament was cancelled on 24 March 2023. The Surat court sentenced him to two years in prison in a defamation case. Rahul was then the MP from Wayanad. However, his membership was later restored after his sentence was suspended. Read what the Justice Loya case was about... Justice Loya's son had described his father's death as natural. The Supreme Court had also termed it a normal death and dismissed the petition seeking an SIT investigation into the matter. Justice Brijmohan Harikishan Loya died in Nagpur in December 2014. At the time, he had gone to attend the wedding of his colleague's daughter. Judge Loya was hearing the much-discussed Sohrabuddin Sheikh encounter case in Gujarat, in which Amit Shah was an accused.

stories.title: FIR against SP leader for construction in Dalmandi:Work continued despite court stay, complaint over installing shutter, and threats
stories.summary: Despite a court order restraining construction, work is alleged to have been carried out on a house in Varanasi's Dalmandi. Chauk police have registered a case against two people, including Samajwadi Party leader Imran Ahmed Bablu, in connection with the matter. Mohammad Wasim, the owner of the house, has alleged that the old shutter of the disputed property was removed and replaced with a new one. He was also allegedly threatened with death when he objected. According to Wasim's complaint, the court has barred any change to the condition of the house or any new construction. Despite this, construction was allegedly carried out again on the night of 22 October. Police are investigating the matter. Dispute over ownership of half the house According to Chauk police station in-charge Vijay Kumar Shukla, Mohammad Wasim owns half of a house in Chahmama, Dalmandi. A case concerning ownership of the house is pending in court. The court has ordered that no changes be made to the house until the dispute is decided. Waseem alleges that despite the court's order, Samajwadi Party leaders Imran Ahmed Bablu and Sawab Ahmed removed the old shutter and installed a new one in the remaining part of the house. They then locked the shutter and took possession of the portion. Accused of threatening to kill him when he objected According to Waseem, the Public Works Department (PWD) had marked a red line near the house. It is alleged that the old shutter installed next to it was removed and replaced with a new one. Waseem said this portion had remained after part of the house was demolished during earlier action. He said he had filed a complaint through Dial 112 and at Chowk police station on 20 September. It is alleged that when he objected to the construction, the accused threatened to kill him. Accused of resuming construction on the night of 22 October Waseem alleged that construction was resumed on the night of 22 October. During this, bamboo poles and supports were put up, and two new shutters were installed in place of one. On the victim's written complaint, Chowk police registered an FIR against Samajwadi Party leader Imran Ahmed Bablu and Sawab Ahmed. Police said the case is being investigated.

stories.title: Woman killed after being hit by motorcycle in Gorakhpur:Attacked while returning from an engagement ceremony with husband; hunt on for 2 suspects
stories.summary: Two motorcycle-borne criminals attacked a couple travelling on a motorcycle beyond Bharwal village in Gorakhpur's Belipar police station area on Saturday night. The wife, who was riding pillion, fell from the motorcycle after the criminals rammed into it and died. On the basis of the husband's complaint, police have registered a murder case against the two motorcycle-borne criminals and begun an investigation. Raids are being conducted to trace the accused. Suddenly pushed, woman fell on the road Santosh Pandey, a resident of Malaon village in Belipar, had gone to a marriage hall in Gorakhpur on Saturday with his wife, Meera Pandey (54), to attend the engagement ceremony of a young woman from her maternal family. At around 10 p.m., the couple were returning to their village by motorcycle when two unidentified men riding a racing motorcycle approached them from behind. They had just crossed Bharwal village when, it is alleged, the motorcycle-borne men pushed his wife. Meera fell on the road and sustained serious injuries. Immediately after the incident, Santosh telephoned his cousin, who lives in the village, and informed him. The cousin then reached the scene. The family took Meera to Gorakhpur District Hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Based on the written complaint, police registered a case against two unidentified people. The identification of the accused and the reasons behind the incident are being investigated. Meera was the mother of three daughters The family is in mourning following the death of 54-year-old Meera. She had three daughters, two of whom are married. Her youngest daughter, Shweta, lives in Gurugram. After receiving news of their mother's death, family members are waiting for her to arrive. South SP Dinesh Puri said a case has been registered on the basis of the husband's written complaint. The reason for the incident will become clear once the assailants are arrested.

stories.title: ‘Thank God Ram did not kill a minority’:UP Election Commission hits back at Sanjay Singh; says software isn't casteist
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Election Commission said the voter list for the recent Legislative Council (MLC) election also contained the unusual name 'Ram killed Sharma'. The commission said that computers and software are not casteist and admitted that a mistake had occurred. The commission said, "There is also a strange name in the MLC election voter list: 'Ram ne Sharma ko maara' (Ram beat Sharma). Computers or software are not casteist. We accept that a mistake was made, but fortunately, there was no caste discrimination even when the mistake occurred." (Thank God, Ram did not beat a minority person. Otherwise, along with being accused of caste discrimination, we would also have been accused of communal bias.) The response came after AAP Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh questioned why the voter list included the name "Ram ne Yadav ko maara" (Ram beat Yadav). Sharing a video of a man named Rajesh Yadav on X, Singh asked Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, "Why did Ram beat only Yadav? Why did Ram not beat someone named Singh, Pathak, Asthana, Sharma, Rai or Bisht? Is your computer deeply casteist? Are you carrying out the agenda of a political party?" Election Commission had earlier clarified the name errors On October 22, the Election Commission had issued a clarification regarding the errors in the voter list. In a post on X, it said that the process of adding names to the voter list for the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC) elections had been carried out online for the first time. As a result, some errors occurred in certain places. Out of 14.81 lakh names on the voter list, only 158 appeared unusual when read. The commission explained that the computer was supposed to transliterate English names into Hindi, but instead, it translated their meaning. For example, a person's name was 'Ramhit Yadav'. While typing, the spelling became 'Ram hit Yadav', and the computer translated it into Hindi as 'Ram ne Yadav ko maara' (Ram beat Yadav). Complaints of errors in voter list received Before the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC) elections, complaints of errors in the voter list had surfaced. Some names and addresses were so unusual that readers were left shocked. In some cases, a voter's name was listed as 'Takkar Marna' (to hit), while another entry showed the father's name as 'Ram ne Sharma ko maara' (Ram beat Sharma). Claims also circulated on social media that dozens of names in the voter list for the Allahabad-Jhansi graduate constituency were fake. Dainik Bhaskar investigated these claims by checking the viral lists against the MLC voter lists of the respective districts. The check revealed some surprising details. Names claimed to be fake Part number 73 (serial number 420): Name – Ram ne Maara Yadav Ko; Father's name – Phool Chandra Yadav Part number 69 (serial number 351): Name – Takkar Marna; Father's name – Takkar Marna Part number 133 (serial number 768): Name – Ravi Sharma; Father's name – Ram ne Sharma ko Maara Part number 189 (serial number 1034): Name – Moorkh Kali Devi; Father's name – Ramjeet Patel Part number 15 (serial number 82): Name – Mohammad Pagal Rehan; Father's name – Mohammad Hashim Part number 81 (serial number 696): Name – Narendra Yadav; Father's name – B.Com To verify the viral claims, the updated voter lists for the Jhansi and Prayagraj (Allahabad) areas were checked. One error found in Jhansi voter list The viral list claimed that a voter named 'Khalid Ali ne Kaha' was listed at part number 252, serial number 566, in Jhansi. However, when the official list updated in December 2025 was checked on the Election Commission's website, that part contained only 537 voters. This means there was no entry at serial number 566. However, a major error was found in the name listed at part number 133, serial number 768.

stories.title: Fake captain caught at Varanasi air show:Was roaming in the restricted helipad area of Namo Ghat; intelligence agencies questioned him
stories.summary: A fake captain was caught in the helipad area of Namo Ghat in Varanasi ahead of an air show. He was roaming in the restricted area while claiming to be an Army captain. Security personnel caught him after becoming suspicious. His posting as a captain in the Army could not be confirmed, after which he was handed over to the police. The युवक was identified as Arpit Chaturvedi. Intelligence agencies questioned him for hours. The police registered a named FIR against him. Roaming in highly sensitive helipad area Security arrangements had been tightened in Varanasi in view of the Air Force air show scheduled for Sunday. Despite this, a युवक reached the restricted area of the helipad at Namo Ghat on Saturday. The personnel deployed on duty found his activities suspicious. During questioning, he claimed to be an Army captain. His answers and demeanour increased the personnel's suspicion. The authorities and local police were subsequently informed. After receiving the information, police and administrative officials, along with officers from the Intelligence Bureau (IB), the Local Intelligence Unit (LIU) and the Air Force, reached the spot. The youth was taken into custody and questioning began. No evidence of posting as captain found in army records Given the sensitivity of the matter, the youth was taken to the office of a senior officer of the Varanasi Police Commissionerate. There, intelligence units of the IB, LIU and Air Force questioned him for several hours. During the initial questioning, he identified himself as Captain Arpit. He gave his address as being near the PWD Colony in Jadid Bazar, under the jurisdiction of Cantt police station. However, checks of Army records and the address he provided did not confirm that he was a captain. After the investigation, he was identified as Arpit Chaturvedi. According to officials, he is originally from Varanasi's Nadesar area. Father runs a pathology centre According to the DCP of Kashi, Arpit's father runs a pathology centre in the city. An investigation is under way into why the young man claimed to be an army officer and how he reached the restricted helipad area. Security and intelligence agencies are also gathering information related to the case. A named FIR has been registered against Arpit Chaturvedi at Adampur police station on the complaint of Chandan Kumar, in-charge of the Namoghat police outpost. The police have taken action against him and filed a charge sheet.

stories.title: India’s first urban ropeway to launch soon in Kashi:Bhaskar witnesses trial; cabins every 2 minutes, service stops if wind speed exceeds 60 kmph
stories.summary: The country’s first urban ropeway in Kashi is expected to begin passenger services soon, with 96% of the construction work completed. The 3.85-km route between Cantt and Godowlia has five stations. The journey from Cantt to Godowlia will take just 16 minutes. At present, covering the same distance of around 7 km by auto takes 30 to 40 minutes. An air-conditioned gondola (cabin) will arrive at a station every two minutes. Each cabin will have seating capacity for 10 passengers. The ropeway is expected to provide major relief from traffic congestion to devotees visiting the Kashi Vishwanath Temple and the ghats along the Ganga. During a trial run, a Dainik Bhaskar reporter travelled on the ropeway and got a close look at its technology, safety arrangements and passenger facilities. Read on… Five stations to offer passengers an aerial view of Kashi The ropeway will connect five stations: Cantt, Kashi Vidyapeeth, Rath Yatra, Girijaghar and Godowlia. Designed with modern facilities, the stations will also reflect Kashi’s cultural identity. Their architecture features elements inspired by the Ganga, its ghats and Lord Shiva. Designs incorporating damru and trishul motifs are also being developed. The ropeway journey will give tourists and local residents an opportunity to enjoy an aerial view of the city. Full ropeway journey to cost Rs 50, with Rs 10 fare per station The ropeway will operate for around 16 hours daily, from 6 am to 10 pm. The proposed fares have been set with ordinary commuters in mind. A journey from Cantt to Godowlia will cost Rs 50, while passengers travelling between any two consecutive stations will have to pay Rs 10. Passengers will be able to get off at any intermediate station according to their requirements. Each gondola will accommodate 10 passengers at a time. A total of 153 gondolas manufactured by Swiss company Bartholet are being installed along the route. One of the key features of the service is the short waiting time. A gondola will arrive at each station every 120 seconds, or two minutes. Metro-style entry system with baggage screening before boarding Passengers’ luggage will be screened as soon as they enter the station. They will then have to purchase tickets. Like the Metro, passengers will be allowed to access the platform only after scanning their tickets. A large hall has been built inside the station where passengers can wait for some time during busy periods. The arrangements have been designed to regulate passenger movement and prevent unnecessary crowding on the platform. The ropeway station adjoining Cantt railway station has been designed with passenger convenience in mind. The two-floor Cantt ropeway station will have security checks on the ground floor and ticket counters and a waiting hall on the first floor. Gondolas will arrive on the upper level, from where passengers can board them to travel between stations. Gondolas to travel at speeds of 21–22 kmph The ropeway uses a monocable detachable gondola system, with a maximum operating speed of 6 metres per second, or around 21–22 kmph. When a gondola reaches a station, it detaches from the main cable and slows down to around 0.2 metres per second. This process takes approximately 45 seconds inside the station, allowing passengers to board and get off comfortably. Once it leaves the station, the gondola reconnects to the main cable and resumes its normal speed. Backup system to prevent passengers from getting stranded during power cuts The ropeway is equipped with a backup safety system. If there is a power cut or a fault in the drive system, the backup mechanism will be activated to bring the gondolas to the nearest station. This arrangement is intended to reduce the risk of passengers being stranded mid-route. Anemometers have been installed on all towers to monitor wind speed. If wind speeds exceed 60 kmph, the system will automatically shut down. The system is also designed to minimise sudden jolts caused by wind while passengers are travelling. Gondola doors cannot be opened from inside; helpline will connect passengers to control room Each gondola will have a unique identification number. In case of any problem, passengers will be able to contact the control room directly through a helpline and report the number of the gondola they are travelling in. The doors will not open from inside, ensuring that passengers do not violate safety protocols during an emergency and allowing the rescue team to carry out operations in a controlled manner. The ropeway rescue team has received training in Switzerland. A team from the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) has also inspected the facility recently. A team of experts from Switzerland is examining the ropeway’s technical and safety arrangements. Pooja Mishra, head of the company involved in the ropeway project, said several layers of safety measures had been put in place for passengers. Each station and gondola is inspected in accordance with separate standard operating procedures (SOPs). A team of experts from Switzerland is reviewing the technical and safety systems, while safety consultants have also been appointed. Security teams to manage crowds at all five stations Managing passenger crowds will be a key priority once the ropeway becomes operational. The plan includes deploying State Security Force personnel along with private security staff. The trained operations team will ensure that passengers follow safety rules and movement protocols. Special attention will be given to entry and exit arrangements, as well as the boarding and alighting of gondolas, at all five stations. Godowlia station work yet to be completed More than 96% of the Rs 807-crore project has been completed. Section One is fully ready. In Section Two, the Girijaghar station has been completed, while work on the passenger boarding and exit facilities at Godowlia station is in its final stages. The target is to complete the remaining work within the next few days. A team of experts from Switzerland is currently conducting technical inspections. Testing of the automation and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems is also pending. An international-level company is carrying out these checks. Ropeway expected to ease road traffic congestion At present, travelling from Cantt to Godowlia by road takes around 30 to 40 minutes due to heavy traffic and congestion. Once operational, the ropeway will cover the same distance in just 16 minutes. The service is expected to provide significant relief to devotees visiting the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, tourists and local residents. It is also likely to reduce pressure on road traffic in the city's busy areas.

stories.title: Fake rape and molestation cases become a business in UP:Woman says, ‘You just spend the money; ruining lives is my job’
stories.summary: The Dainik Bhaskar investigative team has traced an alleged network in Uttar Pradesh involving women accused of trapping people in false rape and molestation cases to extort money. The investigation found that several women had allegedly turned such cases into a means of earning money. The findings raise questions about how the alleged network operates and why the police have been unable to stop it. The investigation comes amid strong remarks by the Allahabad High Court on false rape cases, with the court observing, “Most rape cases that reach the police and courts are false,” and calling for FIRs against those who file false rape cases. During a sting operation, a woman from Kushinagar claimed to a Dainik Bhaskar reporter that she could frame anyone in a false case in exchange for money. We also reached people against whom the woman had allegedly filed false cases. After extracting land and lakhs of rupees from them, these women reached settlements. First in the investigation: The woman we caught red-handed on camera We received information that 45-year-old Zarina Khatoon from Kushinagar had filed FIRs against several people. She allegedly also got POCSO cases registered with the help of minor girls. We met Zarina in Ramkola Urdahan village in Kushinagar. We spoke to her using a hidden camera. Reporter: A man is troubling us a lot. We wanted to get a false case registered. Zarina: It is the festive season, and the girls are busy with their families. We will get it done once they are free. Reporter: How long will we have to wait? We are in a bit of a hurry. Zarina: The work will be done as soon as we find a girl. (Showing a photograph on her mobile phone) Look, this is Chandrabhan Singh. He was the station house officer (SHO) at Ramkola police station. He has now been transferred, but that is not a problem. I have a good relationship with the new SHO as well. We can get your case registered through him too. Reporter: We have come from Haryana. The boy is very troubled. Zarina: People have influence in their own areas. You will not be able to get anything done here. I have influence here. We will get everything done. (Showing photographs on her mobile phone) Look, a girl's case came up just today. We helped her at the police station. We handle all the work at Ramkola police station. Reporter: Do you work in the police? How much money will we have to pay? Zarina: We are the police station's chowkidar. We help people more than the police do. The girl and the police officers will discuss it and then tell you. Reporter: Someone told us that madam is very helpful. They said the case would be registered if she wanted it to be. Zarina: The police are always after me. Whatever we do, the police will not question us. Reporter: Look, the boy who has come with me wants to frame a husband and wife, who are his relatives, in a false case. The wife has a government job. The relatives want both of them to go to jail so that they can take over the entire property. Zarina: It will be done. Do not worry. (Showing a copy of a false case) Look, read the sections. We got this case registered. We have many options. If I tell the sub-inspector, he will register the case. Reporter: Will you get a rape case registered against this boy as well? It should be something that attracts serious charges. Zarina: Yes. His house will have to be sold, and he will also be sentenced. If an attempt-to-rape charge is added, no one will be able to save him. Reporter: His wife could have filed the case, but she has a government job and does not want to get involved. Zarina: Do not worry. We will get it done. We have already got four cases registered. Everyone is troubled and wants to get them managed. Reporter: Can you not file the case yourself? Zarina: No, I will not file it myself. I am employed, so it could cause problems. I have already got several cases registered. Reporter: The girl will be an outsider. What if she withdraws her statement after the case is registered? We could end up getting trapped instead. Zarina: No, that will not happen. That is precisely what she gets paid for. After the case is registered, we will arrange for her to give a statement before a magistrate. Once she gives her statement, she cannot back out. If she does, she will get into trouble herself. Reporter: What if the other party spends money at the police station? Zarina: They can spend as much money as they want. Nothing will happen. There will be a settlement eventually. (Showing a copy of a case) Look, we got this POCSO Act case registered. Bail is not granted in such cases. Once a statement is given, the person will be convicted. Reporter: Will the girl be an adult or a minor? Zarina: We will get the case filed through a minor girl. The money will be settled at that point. I have not spared even my husband and his friend. They, too, have been ruined by cases. Reporter: What if we cannot find a minor girl? Zarina: We will get a married woman to do it. She called a sub-inspector and said, “I need to get a case registered.” To convince us, Zarina called a sub-inspector at the police station. The mobile screen displayed the name 'Naib Daroga'. When the call was answered, she said, “Hello, sir. What is happening? Are you at the police station or at your quarters? I had some work with you. I need to get a case registered. All right, fine. We will come to the police station itself at 10 am tomorrow morning. He will also pay the expenses, and we will keep receiving money later as well.” Reporter: Look, this boy is afraid to go home. His relatives are beating him up there. Zarina: They must have found his weak spot. If they beat him, he should come to me. Transfer some money into this boy's account now. I will put in whatever is needed for his case. It can be done anywhere in Kushinagar or Deoria. Reporter: We will transfer the money into his account by tomorrow evening or the morning after. How will you arrange the girl who will file the case? Zarina: A girl cannot be found immediately. Someone close to the person is usually approached. I have the courage to speak to the district magistrate, the police chief or the SP. We have already spoken to the sub-inspector. We will get the case registered as State versus the accused. You will not have to fight it. The police will fight it themselves. An agent who agreed to arrange a case out of greed for money Zarina: But you will transfer the money to this boy's account. Yes, whatever money you give him, make sure you ask me how much was spent and where. Reporter: How much money should we transfer to his account now? Zarina: Transfer at least ₹1 lakh. Once the case is registered, you will see that they will call you themselves and ask you to come and settle the matter. Everyone will be ready to fall at your feet. The police have immense power through their pen. Reporter: Your man is asking for ₹3 lakh. Zarina: Not ₹3 lakh right now. Pay some amount first. We will ask you for the rest later, as much as is needed. Once the case is registered, we will send you a copy on WhatsApp. Zarina continued to claim on camera that she had links with the police station. After promising to pay her ₹1 lakh, we left her house. We tracked down the people she had mentioned during the conversation. We found that she had allegedly pressured several people by submitting complaints at the police station and later withdrawn the cases after reaching settlements involving money or land. She had reportedly been running this operation for several years. Victim 1: Ramjeet Kharwar A land dispute led to his arrest in a molestation case Eighty-year-old Ramjeet Kharwar of Ramkola had a land dispute with Murtaza. The two had fought several times. After failing to get his way despite repeated attempts, Murtaza allegedly turned to Zarina Khatoon. Zarina got a molestation case registered against Ramjeet. As soon as the case was registered at Ramkola police station, Ramjeet was jailed for a month. He is now struggling to reach a settlement, and a substantial amount of money is reportedly being demanded. Victim 2: Angad He caught Zarina's son stealing, after which an FIR was registered against him Angad said, “I run a grocery shop. One day, Zarina's son stole something from my shop. A quarrel broke out over the incident. Angered by this, Zarina got an FIR registered against me for attempted rape. When I went to meet her, she demanded money from me.” Victim 3: Ranjit Govind Rao 'She filed a false rape case because I refused to give her a passage.' Ranjit Govind Rao and Zarina Khatoon had a land dispute in Chakawat village in Ramkola, Kushinagar. Ranjit's land lies in front of Zarina's house, which is built behind it. Zarina wanted a passage through this land. A fight broke out over the issue. Zarina got a case registered against Ranjit Govind Rao at Ramkola police station for molestation and attempted rape. Ranjit and Govind Rao began suffering mental harassment. Under pressure, they agreed to provide a passage and also paid money to settle the case. Zarina is not a police station chowkidar but a police informer During the sting operation, Zarina claimed that she was a chowkidar at the police station. We investigated the matter at the station and found that a man named Idrish had previously worked as a chowkidar in Urdahan Masjid Tola, the area where Zarina lives. Idrish died seven years ago. Zarina had been trying to secure the chowkidar's position herself, but later began providing the police with information about everything happening in the area. In this way, she started working as a police informer. Now, Shalini from Agra: She allegedly trapped 11 men in false cases A 26-year-old woman from Agra, referred to as Shalini (name changed), filed rape and molestation cases against three people. The men against whom FIRs were registered in Shahjahanpur, Etah and Agra investigated her themselves and discovered that she had been in relationships with 11 men. Complaints of rape and molestation had also been filed against these men in different districts, but most cases ended in settlements. After uncovering these shocking facts, the men submitted evidence against Shalini to the police. The police sent her to jail, but she was later released on bail. We reached young men who said they had been harassed by Shalini. Pawan (name changed), from Shahjahanpur, was studying while living in a rented house in Etah. One day, Shalini, who lived on the floor above him, called him to her room and said that the internet on her mobile phone was not working. When Pawan visited her, she gave him her mobile number. The two then began talking. One day, Shalini suddenly demanded ₹50,000 from him. When he refused, she threatened to frame him in a rape case. Frightened, Pawan transferred ₹10,000 to her. Shalini then demanded ₹1 lakh. When he refused to pay, she got an FIR registered against him at Sikandrabad police station. During a video call, Shalini proposed that she would settle the case in exchange for ₹2 lakh. Pawan approached the police and conducted his own investigation. He discovered that Shalini had filed similar cases against 10 other men. Police action: The police registered an FIR against Shalini and sent her to jail. She is currently out on bail. The Bhaskar investigation revealed three key findings: These issues have come before the courts. The Supreme Court suggested that the government consider amendments. How are these women able to get false FIRs registered so easily? We discussed the issue with Alok Singh, a senior advocate in Lucknow. He said that Section 166A of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) states that if a police officer refuses to register an FIR after receiving information about sexual offences against women, such as rape or molestation, the officer can face criminal proceedings. The punishment can include rigorous imprisonment for six months to two years, along with a fine. Read about some cases that the courts found to be false:

stories.title: Labrador dog chases away leopard in Uttar Pradesh:Chased it for up to 50 metres after it entered the house boundary
stories.summary: A Labrador dog chased away a leopard after it entered a house in Uttar Pradesh's Lakhimpur Kheri district. The dog not only confronted the big cat but also chased it for nearly 50 metres before driving it out of the property. The entire encounter lasted around 18 seconds and was captured on CCTV. The incident took place at around 4.05 am on Wednesday in Manjhra Purab village, under the North Nighasan Forest Range. The leopard quietly entered the house through its main gate and stepped inside the boundary wall. A Labrador sitting inside the premises sensed its presence. As soon as it noticed the leopard, the dog moved towards it and prepared to attack. The leopard initially stepped back after seeing the dog approaching. However, the Labrador continued barking and charged towards the big cat. Faced with the dog's resistance, the leopard turned around and fled to save itself. The CCTV footage of the incident surfaced on Thursday. Leopard entered house looking for prey The house belongs to Gursaheb Singh, who was sleeping with his family when the incident occurred. According to the CCTV footage, the leopard entered the premises quietly at around 4.05 am. After walking a few steps, it stopped and looked around before slowly moving ahead, apparently searching for prey. It was then that the Labrador came face to face with the wild animal. Instead of backing away, the dog stood its ground as the leopard moved towards it. Within seconds, the Labrador began barking and lunged at the leopard without showing any fear. See 3 pictures... Labrador chased leopard for 50 metres The dog did not stop after forcing the leopard to retreat. It continued chasing the animal for nearly 50 metres and drove it all the way outside the main gate. The Labrador returned only after ensuring that the leopard had left the property. The CCTV footage captures the entire confrontation, showing how the dog stood up to the much larger wild animal and forced it to flee. Encounter lasted around 18 seconds The confrontation between the Labrador and the leopard lasted approximately 18 seconds. The sequence of events, as captured on CCTV, was: Family woke up after hearing dog bark The family members were sleeping when the incident took place. They woke up after hearing the Labrador barking. When they checked the CCTV footage, they were surprised to see their pet confronting the leopard and chasing it out of the house. According to local villagers, leopards have been spotted in the area for the past several days. Their repeated sightings have raised concerns among residents. Forest department installs cage to catch leopard Forest Ranger Bhupendra Singh confirmed that the department had received the CCTV footage showing the Labrador coming face to face with the leopard. He said a forest department team had been sent to the spot to assess the situation. Residents have also been advised to remain alert and take precautions. The forest department has installed a cage in the area to capture the leopard. Officials have urged villagers to remain cautious, particularly during the early morning and night hours, when the chances of encountering wild animals may be higher.

stories.title: Criminals shot a constable three times in Varanasi:One bullet hit his hand and two his abdomen; team had gone to arrest arms smugglers
stories.summary: A crime team went to Nariya Tiraha in Varanasi on Friday evening to apprehend arms smugglers. During the operation, three suspected smugglers opened fire at the team, hitting a constable with three bullets. The constable sustained one gunshot wound to his hand and two to his abdomen. He was rushed to the trauma centre and admitted in critical condition. One of the accused was also shot in the left leg during the exchange of fire. A large police force has been deployed at the spot, and the Police Commissioner has also reached the scene. Three teams have been formed to investigate the incident, which took place in Ashutosh Nagar under the Lanka police station area of the Varanasi Police Commissionerate. See 3 pictures… Third suspect opens fire while police question the group The incident took place in Ashutosh Nagar, behind Sunderpur vegetable market. According to information, four constables from the Lanka police station’s crime team reached the spot after receiving a tip-off that arms smugglers were present there with weapons. The team found three young men at the location and began questioning them. Two of them were detained, but the third suddenly opened fire directly at the police personnel. The sudden firing triggered panic at the scene. As shots rang out, police personnel ran for cover. During the chaos, Constable Amit Shukla was hit by three bullets and collapsed to the ground. The shooter fled the scene. Shukla was rushed to the trauma centre, where he is undergoing treatment. Following the incident, police teams launched a search for the attacker. Amit Shukla is a native of Prayagraj Constable Amit Shukla originally belongs to Varkarganj in Prayagraj. His father’s name is Surya Mani Shukla. He has a three-year-old daughter. Shukla has been posted at Lanka police station in Varanasi for the past three years. Before this, he also worked with the Varanasi Special Operations Group (SOG). He has received training from the Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS).

stories.title: 'You get nothing through shortcuts; money follows, bro...':Ravi Kishan in Lucknow says earn a name; money will follow
stories.summary: Nothing comes from shortcuts, money follows, bro... Build a name, and money will chase you on its own. This was said by Bollywood star and BJP MP from Gorakhpur Ravi Kishan. At the Content Creators Show organised by Dainik Bhaskar at The Centrum Hotel in Lucknow, he urged young people to move forward with hard work, patience and a positive mindset. Young content creators and influencers from different districts across the state took part in the programme. In an exclusive conversation with Bhaskar, he spoke openly about success, struggle, positive content and spirituality. What advice did he give young people? Read the full interview... Question: How do you view this initiative to help content creators progress? Answer: I wholeheartedly commend Dainik Bhaskar for this effort. People from Uttar Pradesh were invited today as content creators. Two hundred people were shortlisted from around 20,000. They were honoured. Some received tickets to Dubai, some to Goa, while others received a cash amount. This is a different kind of encouragement. Content creators are now the face of the country and society. An 'influencer' is someone who influences society and uses their content to showcase their state-One District, One Product; our culture and traditions; Bhojpuri music and folk music; how my road has improved and my village has improved; how this sportsperson is preparing well; how this girl is studying well and her ranking is improving. Whether it is a cinema story, comedy or one of the many other forms, children today are creating content. These people also promote shops in their cities and earn money. If I talk about Gorakhpur, four influencers from there have won. A major industry is being set up there, and countless projects are under way. These people get jobs and promote the city as well. Flyovers are being built, roads are being constructed and new aircraft are operating. The entire country sees what the city looks like at night, what new changes are taking place, and what changes are occurring in villages, localities, schools and hospitals. This is a very major initiative. Question: It took you 35 years to become Ravi Kishan. Young people want success quickly. What would you tell them? Answer: That's wrong! Look, it simply isn't possible. How long does it take us to learn to stand on our own feet from the time we are born? First, we are born, then we crawl on our knees, and gradually learn by falling and getting back up. It takes 25-26 years to complete our education. Everything takes time-whether it is a tree, a plant, a field or anything in nature. If a crop is growing, it takes time. The rains take time to arrive. You have to wait for summer and winter. This is nature's law. There is no instant shortcut, and whatever comes through a shortcut disappears just as quickly. That is why patience is very important. Once you have made up your mind, stay committed, remain steadfast and continue reading. Studying books is important. Educate yourself and read the newspaper every day. When making reels, think about what good things you can offer. What lessons can you give society, your juniors, your area and your villages and rural communities? Do not serve negativity. Likes come quickly with negativity, but do not spread false news. Check and recheck before commenting on anyone. 'Likes come quickly with negativity' Ravi Kishan said that in the pursuit of likes for perhaps just one of your reels, you could ruin someone's career or destroy someone's home. That is why it is also very important to ensure that, in the pursuit of increasing likes and followers, we are not unknowingly ruining someone's life. Negativity attracts likes quickly. If you abuse someone, people immediately like it. If you say something false about someone, people are interested in hearing it. Your followers and likes increase, but you gradually begin to destroy yourself without realising it. You become completely ostracised from society. The future ahead will be very bright because AI and the digital world have arrived. Prime Minister Modi has made India completely digital. If you travel abroad, you have to spend several dollars and pounds to get a SIM card and use the internet. If the cheapest internet in the world is anywhere, it is in India. We must use its benefits to move forward. Question: Your song 'Gucci-Gucci' was released recently. It went viral on the internet and became a sensation. What would you say about it? Answer: Look, I call Gen Z, as people refer to them, the soul of India. The younger generation saw themselves in me. I am fortunate. I thank them for embracing my carefree nature, my mistakes and my slips of the tongue. They liked my Parliament move. They also liked my films and projects such as 'Mirzapur', 'Dhamaal', 'Laapataa Ladies', 'Maamla Legal Hai' and 'Maa-Behan', which was released on Netflix. For the past two years, they have continued to give me blockbusters. The people of this country are giving them to me. Even after doing 760 films, I consider it Mahadev's blessing that people across the country still show us so much love today, and that we receive so much affection from the youth. They like me as I am and appreciate the things that are part of me. I do not make any extra effort for anything. I am the way I am, and I say whatever comes to my heart. I have won the Best Parliamentarian Award, the Best MP Award and the Best Actor Award. My film Laapataa Ladies even made it to the Oscars. Despite these achievements, I remain normal. I do not carry these achievements on my head and go around under any false impression. 'The youth should embrace spirituality; being spiritual is essential' I know that this is a moment, this is the present. Mahadev is giving this prasad, and his damru is beating. As long as the damru beats, everything, including the nagada, will continue to sound. When the damru stops, the nagada will stop too. I know this is the truth. That is why the youth should embrace spirituality. Being spiritual is very important. If you are spiritual, you will not go into depression, attempt suicide or turn to alcohol and drugs. You have to draw on the powers of spirituality. Falls, bad days, death, accidents, sorrow, hardship and illness will continue to come your way, but you will recover from them quickly and move on. If you have spiritual power and the strength of spirituality, even a major blow will hurt you a little less. This happens to everyone, whether they are important or ordinary, because it is a rule of life. Question: You have a dialogue that says recognition is important - "Money follows, bro." Where does this thinking come from? Answer: Name or money? Since childhood, we had thought that we would make a name for ourselves. We did not want to die unknown. I asked only for a name, and once you have a name, money follows. When someone has a name, money seeks them out. People think that this person has become well known, has some talent, and that the entire country is looking for them-so money seeks them out too. If you pursue money first, you will be ruined. Question: At the regional level, many content creators are doing good work to promote their languages and cultures. What should they keep in mind to make a name for themselves, and how should they maintain discipline? Answer: First, respect your parents, respect your teachers, and respect your neighbours and society. Study spirituality, love your country, love India, and love your soil. Remain completely honest towards India and your culture. Do not look for shortcuts; work hard and spread positivity. When you give something good to society, society and the country will themselves honour you greatly. Pursue recognition, and money will automatically follow you. Question: The MLC election results are being announced. What do you have to say about this? Answer: I have not yet been able to see the full result. Whatever happens, it will be for the best. Whatever Mahadev does will also be for the best. If something has gone wrong, it will be discussed, work will be done on it and the matter will be thoroughly deliberated upon. The Bharatiya Janata Party engages in introspection. It spends all 365 days looking for mistakes, then works hard and remains committed to correcting them. Even if something has gone wrong here or there, every effort will be made to rectify it. Heartfelt thanks to Dainik Bhaskar for this effort. You searched for influencers. There are many such departments. We have entered the world of AI and digital technology. You are taking it across the country. Today, your app is number one after Japan. We understand that you will reach great heights. Heartfelt congratulations to the entire Bhaskar team as well! I salute all those associated with the newspaper, app and media-the intelligent young men and women who are working. Keep it up! Continue showing the truth and reality. Continue showing your love for India as well. I request you to ensure that the spirit of love for India is awakened in everyone. Har Har Mahadev! Victory to Mother India!

stories.title: Lucknow's food culture blends tradition with new flavours:Pan-Asian restaurants and contemporary Indian menus attract diners
stories.summary: Lucknow’s food scene is expanding beyond its famous kebabs, biryanis and traditional Awadhi cuisine, with Pan-Asian restaurants, contemporary Indian menus and international cuisines gaining attention as the city marks one year since UNESCO designated it a Creative City of Gastronomy on October 31, 2025. The recognition made Lucknow the second Indian city after Hyderabad to receive the designation, highlighting its rich culinary heritage, while the growing popularity of diverse cuisines and modern dining concepts reflects how diners in the City of Nawabs are exploring new flavours and experiences beyond traditional food. For many, dining out is no longer just about the food. The ambience, the opportunity to discover new cuisines and the experience of spending time with others have also become important. This shift has attracted hospitality groups looking to expand into cities with established food cultures and growing demand for premium dining. One such group is Bellona Hospitality, the hospitality arm of The Phoenix Mills Ltd. It has introduced two dining concepts in Lucknow: Ishaara, which focuses on modern Indian cuisine and inclusive hospitality, and Eight, which offers pan-Asian food. Restaurants bring new flavours to Lucknow Prashant Issar, managing director of Bellona Hospitality and founder of Ishaara, said Lucknow’s growing interest in new cuisines builds on its longstanding appreciation of food. “Lucknow has never needed to prove itself as a food destination. Its culinary heritage speaks for itself. What makes the city particularly exciting today is the confidence with which its diners are exploring new experiences while remaining deeply connected to their traditions. A city that understands and appreciates good food is naturally curious about discovering more. That’s what makes Lucknow such an interesting market for contemporary hospitality,” Issar said. Located at Phoenix Palassio, Eight offers dishes inspired by Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Thai and other Asian cuisines. Its menu includes sushi, dim sum, aromatic curries and wok-prepared dishes, served in a contemporary setting. Ishaara, meanwhile, presents Indian cuisine through a modern approach. Its menu combines familiar regional flavours with dishes inspired by culinary traditions from across the country. The restaurant has also introduced diners to lesser-explored food histories through special showcases featuring cuisines from undivided Punjab and the Maratha kitchens. Ishaara focuses on inclusive hospitality Alongside its menu, Ishaara follows an inclusive hospitality model that creates career opportunities for people with speech and hearing impairments (SHI). The restaurant's team members play a central role in serving guests. Customers are encouraged to communicate with them through simple signs and gestures, making interaction an important part of the dining experience. Issar said the approach reflects the idea that hospitality depends on how guests feel, rather than only on the food served. “True hospitality is ultimately about how people feel, not simply what is served. At Ishaara, our SHI team members demonstrate every day that warmth, intuition and exceptional service transcend spoken words. Their abilities are recognised, their confidence grows, and guests discover a different, often more personal way of connecting. In a city where mehmaan-nawazi is part of its identity, this philosophy finds a natural home,” he said. Together, Ishaara and Eight represent two aspects of Lucknow’s changing dining scene: an appreciation of India's diverse culinary traditions and a growing interest in international flavours. Premium dining expands beyond metros The trend also reflects a broader change in India's hospitality sector, where premium dining is expanding beyond major metropolitan cities. Established cultural centres such as Lucknow are attracting restaurant brands that see opportunities among diners seeking quality food, authentic flavours and distinctive experiences. However, Issar said restaurant brands need to understand local traditions rather than simply replicate concepts that have succeeded elsewhere. “The future of Indian hospitality will not be shaped by metros alone. Cities like Lucknow bring something invaluable to the table: a deep-rooted appreciation of food, a strong sense of identity and an openness to new experiences. Successful restaurant brands must understand and respect that character rather than simply replicate what works elsewhere. The opportunity is to become part of the city’s evolving dining culture, not to change what makes it special,” he said. As Lucknow marks one year as a UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy, its culinary identity continues to draw strength from both tradition and innovation. Its kebabs, biryanis and age-old recipes remain popular, even as diners explore a wider range of cuisines and dining experiences. The city's evolving food culture shows how Lucknow is embracing new tastes while retaining the nazakat, tehzeeb and mehmaan-nawazi that define its identity.

stories.title: UP ATS arrests 3 suspects linked to Shahzad Bhatti:Planned to kill Army, police personnel and send videos to Pakistan
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (UP ATS) arrested three members of the banned Shahzad Bhatti network in Lucknow on Friday. A foreign-made pistol and 20 cartridges were recovered from them. The gang was operating on the direct instructions of Pakistan-based handler Rana Bhai. They planned to carry out the targeted killing of an Army or police personnel in Lucknow, record a video of it and send it to Pakistan. Accused reached Lucknow via Delhi from Punjab The ATS had received information that some youths from Punjab were planning to attack a major establishment or security personnel in Lucknow. Acting on the information, the ATS arrested four people in Lucknow on 30 October. The arrested accused include Gagandeep Singh, 26, and Rajat Kumar, 19, residents of Amritsar and Gurdaspur in Punjab, Krish, 21, and a juvenile accused. A foreign-made pistol and 20 live cartridges were recovered from their possession. Were lured with ₹3 lakh and the chance to flee to Nepal During questioning, the accused said they were in contact with Rana Bhai, who was in Pakistan, through Instagram, WhatsApp and virtual numbers. After reaching Lucknow on the night of 29 October, they made a video of Lucknow railway station at Rana Bhai's direction and sent it to Pakistan. Videos and locations related to the reconnaissance of several sensitive sites were also found on their phones. Rana Bhai had sent weapons from Pakistan and, through his local network in Lucknow, arranged for them to receive a pistol and 20 cartridges. Around ₹5,000 was sent to them online from Pakistan for travel and expenses. After carrying out the crime and sending its video, they were promised ₹3 lakh and given a plan to flee to Nepal to evade the police. One foreign-made pistol and 20 foreign-made cartridges recovered ADG (Law and Order) Amitabh Yash said that three people linked to the banned Shahzad Bhatti network had been arrested and a juvenile offender had been detained. All of them are residents of Punjab. They were plotting a targeted killing of a police or Army personnel in Lucknow. One foreign-made pistol and 20 foreign-made cartridges were recovered from their possession. They were all in contact with a Pakistani handler, Rana Bhai, through the social media platforms Instagram and WhatsApp. Interrogation of all the accused is under way. Case Registered at ATS Police Station, Preparation for Custody Remand A case has been registered against the accused at the ATS police station in Lucknow under serious sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Arms Act and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The ATS will now produce the accused in court and seek their police custody remand to identify the local facilitators who supplied weapons in Lucknow, the sources of funding, the financial trail and others linked to this network.

stories.title: BJP to contest 2027 Assembly polls with Yogi as face:State in-charge says Shah praised him repeatedly; the message is clear to those who understand
stories.summary: BJP national general secretary Vinod Tawde made it clear on Friday that the 2027 Assembly election would be fought with Yogi Adityanath as the party's face. Speaking at the BJP's state executive meeting in Lucknow, he said, "Today, Home Minister Amit Shah has repeatedly praised Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Those who are wise will understand the indication." On the issue of discontent among upper-caste voters over the UGC, Vinod Tawde said that the party would reach out to its voters, engage in direct dialogue with them and explain the matter to them. Tawde said: ‘If the BJP does not return to power, conditions will be like those before 2017’ Tawde said, "It is extremely important to tell the people that if the BJP does not form the government in the state, conditions will return to how they were before 2017." He said, "When you speak to a worker, he says that everything is fine, but... this 'but' is what is ruining everything. If half the glass is empty, we should not say that; instead, we must send the message that we will now fill the glass." Referring to the crackdown on crime, he said, "The Congress government had kept Mukhtar Ansari safe in a Punjab jail, but our government fought the matter all the way to the Supreme Court and brought him to a jail in Uttar Pradesh, where he had to live as a prisoner. Houses for the poor are now being built on land seized from mafias such as Atiq and Ansari." 'Flattery or money will not get you a ticket; only those who work will get an opportunity' On ticket distribution and the ambitions of party workers, Tawde said that there was nothing wrong with wanting to contest an election, but the state had only 403 seats. Some people would get tickets, and others would not, but those who did not get tickets would not work against the party. He issued a stern warning, saying that no one would get a ticket through flattering a leader or using money; tickets would be awarded solely on the basis of work. Tawde said, "I have not come only for the elections; I will remain in charge of Uttar Pradesh for the next three years. I will leave Uttar Pradesh only after fulfilling the promise made to any worker who does the work. You can ask workers in Bihar, Maharashtra and Haryana about me." We will not repeat a mistake like '400-plus' Speaking about the role of social media, Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde acknowledged that the BJP had become sluggish on this front. He said, "The Opposition now understands the power of social media. In 2014, we were ahead of everyone on social media, and at the time Lalu Yadav used to ask what difference it made. But today in Bihar, Tejashwi Yadav has more followers than Nitish Kumar. Our social media presence has weakened somewhat; we do not even like or repost the prime minister's and chief minister's posts. Everyone will have to become active on social media because our schemes are not just about development – they are changing people's lives." Speaking about the election target, Vinod Tawde made it clear that the mistake of the slogan 'Abki Baar 400 Paar' would not be repeated in this year's Uttar Pradesh election. He reminded party workers that they had to win 312 seats in the 2027 election, just as they did in 2017. He assured them that he would continue meeting party workers, engage in dialogue with them and find solutions to every problem.

stories.title: Trader writes killer’s name before dying:Reaches a dhaba in Sitapur covered in blood; was on his way to sister’s home for Karwa Chauth
stories.summary: A young trader was kidnapped and had his throat slit in Sitapur. The attackers fled the scene after assuming he was dead. After regaining consciousness, the young man somehow reached a dhaba on the Lakhimpur Kheri-Sitapur border. The blood-soaked young man could not speak because his throat had been cut. Before he died, he wrote the names of the accused on a slip of paper. He pleaded with people to help take him to hospital. The young man died before doctors could begin treating him at the hospital. A police investigation revealed that the young man had left to visit his sister's house on Karva Chauth. His family has filed a complaint against four people, alleging that he was murdered because of an old enmity. Police have detained some people in connection with the complaint. The incident took place in the Pisawan area, 37 km from the district headquarters. See three pictures... Read the full incident in detail... Nitesh Kumar Maurya (24), a resident of Saraiya Mahipat Singh village in Sitapur district, was the eldest of three brothers. One brother, Niket (20), works in Dubai, while the other, Sachin, is 19. Their father, Dinesh Kumar (45), is a farmer. Besides trading in paddy and wheat, Nitesh also ran an RO plant. Nitesh had two sisters, Neha and Khushboo. Khushboo (26) is married. Uncle said - He was going to his sister's house in Lucknow Nitesh's uncle, Harish Kumar Maurya (39), told the police that Nitesh had left home on Wednesday, saying he was going to Bakshi Ka Talab in Lucknow to get something done for his sister. He was also having a house built in Lucknow. For this reason, he left on his bike with a cylinder tied to it. Nitesh's bike found unattended in Barabanki According to Harish Kumar, Nitesh's motorcycle was found abandoned near the Daffarpur crossing in the Baddoopur police station area of Barabanki on Thursday morning. A cylinder was tied to the motorcycle, but Nitesh was not there. Fearing that something untoward had happened, some people said that Nitesh had been abducted by people travelling in a car. A search for Nitesh began after the motorcycle was found, but there was no trace of him. Nitesh wrote on a slip-Manoj is behind my death According to the police, the family suspects that the attackers abducted Nitesh from Baddoopur in Barabanki and took him to the Maigalganj area of Lakhimpur Kheri. They slit his throat near Lidhiyai's turn and dumped him, assuming he was dead. Badly injured, Nitesh somehow reached Pannu Dhaba in Pisawan on the Sitapur border. His throat had been slit, so he could not speak. Nitesh asked the people at the dhaba for paper and a pen. He wrote a plea asking them to take him to hospital. While he was being taken to hospital, Nitesh wrote the name of his acquaintance Manoj on a piece of paper. He also wrote Manoj's father Vidya Prasad's name, along with the village and post office address, Saraiya Mahipat Singh. Nitesh held Manoj responsible for his condition. Nitesh died at the district hospital After receiving information from the roadside eatery, Pisawan police reached the spot. The injured Nitesh was taken to CHC Maholi. His identity could not be established at the time. After first aid, he was referred to the district hospital, where he died at 3:10 p.m. He was later identified as Nitesh Maurya, a resident of Saraiya Mahipat Singh village. Uncle alleges murder over old enmity Nitesh's uncle Harish said he was murdered over an old enmity. According to him, Nitesh had been locked inside a shop and beaten around a year ago. A dispute had been continuing since the incident. Police are now investigating the links between the financial dispute, old enmity and the case ranging from abduction to murder. Manoj Sonkar, Station House Officer of Baddoopur Police Station in Barabanki – A case has been registered in connection with the murder of the businessman, and some suspects have been taken into custody. They are being questioned.

stories.title: Chandrashekhar says every household should have a lawyer:Accuses government of giving jobs to favourites; attends lawyers’ conference in Lucknow
stories.summary: Azad Samaj Party president and MP Chandrashekhar said at the third advocates’ conference organised by the party’s legal cell (Kanshiram) and the Bhim Army at the Gandhi Bhavan auditorium in Kaiserbagh, Lucknow, on Friday that every household needs a lawyer today, as advocates stand as a strong wall in the legal fight against injustice. He appealed to advocates to rise above caste and religion and support one another, while taking a dig at Amit Shah’s visit to Lucknow, saying, “The meeting will produce some result; otherwise, the public is in the mood to teach them a lesson this time.” He also alleged that the government was giving government jobs to its favourites. See three pictures... Emphasis on advocates' unity Chandrashekhar said that advocates' unity should be very strong. Anyone wearing a black coat, regardless of caste or religion, should be treated equally. He said that advocates facing financial hardship should receive as much support as other advocates. Advocates should stand against injustice while upholding the dignity of their profession. He said that in today's era, a person may face action simply for expressing their views. At such times, advocates come forward to protect that person's rights. 'The country's system is governed by the Constitution' The MP said the country's system is governed by the Constitution. The government, officials and independent constitutional institutions all function under the Constitution. But the question is whether ordinary citizens have adequate knowledge of the Constitution and its ethical values. He said the Constitution should be made part of school and college curricula so that people learn about their rights and duties from childhood. Takes a dig at Amit Shah's meeting and the BJP's preparations Home Minister Amit Shah is in Lucknow today. He is holding a meeting with party office bearers to discuss preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections. Commenting on the meeting, Chandrashekhar said the BJP should hold it because the party's position is not good. He said the meeting would yield some result; otherwise, the public appears determined to teach the BJP a lesson this time. 'Forget protests, people are not even being allowed to meet the victims' Chandrashekhar Azad said that when the Bharatiya Janata Party was in opposition, it used to hold frequent protests, but the situation in the state today is such that, far from being allowed to protest, people are detained even when they go to meet victims. He alleged that in several cases, victim families are not even being allowed to perform their children's last rites. 'The government is giving government jobs to its favourites' Chandrashekhar Azad said the government was giving government jobs to its favourites. He said that anyone could name a recruitment drive in the state in which allegations of a scam had not been made. He said the government wanted to intimidate protesters under the guise of such laws so that voices raised against it could be suppressed. The British had also enacted similar laws to stop movements against them and create fear among the people. The chairman said, 'The police harassed lawyers' Legal Cell national chairman Mohanshyam Maria said that incidents of harassment and attacks on advocates were continuing to come to light in Uttar Pradesh. In several places, advocates were harassed by the police, while in some cases miscreants entered their chambers and even opened fire. He also raised the issue of chairs and seats recently installed for advocates to sit in Lucknow being removed and demolished by the administration. Demand for security of chambers and independent legal representation Maria said advocates are an important link in the Constitution and the democratic system. They work to ensure justice for every person in society, but when those same advocates are concerned about their own safety, it is a serious matter. Through the conference, demands are being raised for better arrangements to ensure advocates' safety, protect their dignity and enable them to represent cases independently. Justice must reach those at the bottom of society Mohanshyam Maria said that a legal cell had been formed under the leadership of MP Chandrashekhar Azad and Bhim Army national president Vinay Ratna Singh to safeguard the rights and security of advocates. Its objective is to strengthen arrangements to ensure accessible and appropriate justice even for those at the bottom of society. The conference is discussing advocates' problems, their rights and various issues related to the judicial system. The event is being organised by Rajneesh Gautam, advocate and state president of the Azad Samaj Party Legal Cell, Uttar Pradesh. Safety and dignity of advocates are the main issues The main objective of the conference is to raise issues related to the dignity, self-respect and safety of advocates. The organisers say that advocates, who play an important role in the justice system, now feel unsafe themselves. They face challenges including the independence of their profession, their livelihoods, the security of their chambers and the ability to represent clients in cases without pressure.

stories.title: Dengue cases nearly double in a month:Varanasi count reaches 112, up from 60 on October 4
stories.summary: The dengue situation in Varanasi remained under control until September, but cases increased sharply in October. According to Health Department data, the district had reported 60 dengue cases by October 4. By October 30, the number had risen to 112. This means 52 new confirmed cases were reported during October so far. The rise comes after dengue cases in September 2026 were 35% lower than in the same month last year. Dengue cases rise in October Health Department data shows that Varanasi had recorded 60 dengue cases by October 4. The number increased to 112 by October 30. The rise in cases after a decline until September has raised concern. 60 patients reach district hospital, 7 cases confirmed In October, 60 patients with dengue symptoms visited Deendayal Upadhyay District Hospital. Tests confirmed dengue in seven of them, while the remaining 53 were listed as suspected cases. The patients underwent initial NS1 tests. A second test is also required to confirm dengue. The reports of these 53 patients are still awaited, so they have not yet been counted as confirmed cases. Cases in September were 35% lower than last year In September 2025, 57 dengue cases were reported in Varanasi, while 37 patients were recorded in September 2026. Thus, there were 20 fewer cases in September than in the same month last year. This represented a decline of around 35%. Most cases among people aged 15 to 59 Of the 60 dengue patients reported by 4 October, the highest number were people aged 15 to 59. There were 51 cases in this age group. Six cases were reported among children aged 0 to 14, while three cases were reported among people over 60. Total cases lower than last year In 2025, 229 dengue patients were reported in Varanasi between January and December. In 2026, a total of 112 cases had been reported by 30 October. So far this year, there have been 117 fewer cases than the total recorded throughout last year. According to the Health Department, 8,890 dengue tests were conducted between January and October, while 10,555 tests were conducted throughout 2025.

stories.title: Rat tied up and burnt alive in Jhansi:Hung from a gate, doused with petrol and set alight; FIR filed against four Muslim youths
stories.summary: An incident of animal cruelty has come to light in Jhansi, where four youths allegedly tied a rat to an iron gate, poured petrol on it and set it on fire. The youths first caught the rat and tied it with a rope. They then hung it from the gate, poured petrol over it and set it on fire. They also recorded the incident on video. After some time, the rope broke and the rat ran around trying to escape. However, it later died from its burns. The incident took place on October 29 in the Kotwali police station area. After the video surfaced, police registered a case against all four youths. DISTURBING VISUALS below : Rat caught using a cage The police said the accused caught a rat using a cage. They then tied it to a rope. Junaid Qureshi, son of Shafiq Qureshi, and Shafiq Qureshi, who live in Kasai Mandi near Orchha Gate under Kotwali police station, beat the rat with sticks. They then hung it from an iron gate. Junaid Qureshi, son of Safiq Qureshi, poured petrol from a bottle over the rat and then set it on fire with a matchstick, burning it alive. During this, Ashif Qureshi, son of Abad Qureshi, recorded a video on his mobile phone. He also spoke about burning the rat. Action taken after video goes viral The accused filmed the entire incident and posted it on social media. The video went viral and reached the police. After investigating, the police gathered the accused's details. The Kotwali police then registered a case on the complaint of Sub-Inspector Rohit Kumar. Kotwal Anjan Kumar said, "A case was registered on the basis of the video, and the accused, Junaid Qureshi, Ashif Qureshi and Shafique Qureshi, have been arrested. The three are being produced in court. One accused is absconding and is being searched for." Committee demands action People are angry after the video of the rat being burnt alive went viral. The accused are being criticised everywhere. Office-bearers and workers of Shri Mahakal Gau Seva Sansthan reached the Kotwali police station and demanded action. They said that such people should be given strict punishment.
