stories.title: Akhilesh retorted, ‘Swami Prasad is not part of our alliance’:Says ignore him; announces more tickets for women than BJP in 2027 elections
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said on Friday that Swami Prasad Maurya was not part of his alliance. During a press conference in Lucknow, Akhilesh lost his temper when asked whether Maurya would join the INDIA alliance. He angrily said that Maurya could not be included in the party's seat-sharing arrangement. "Avoid him. Ignore him. Keep quiet," he said. Making a major announcement on women's reservation for the 2027 elections, Akhilesh said his party would give tickets to more women than the BJP. Commenting on the MLC election results, he said the results had held up a mirror to the BJP. "Those who were making a big show have fallen flat on their faces," he said. He added that although the figures showed only 5 MLC seats, the BJP had lost in 50 districts. The SP chief said, "The message has reached the public that BJP leaders are dishonest. SP candidates have won on the strength of the people. They have won 6 seats through deceit. Had they not resorted to such tactics, they might not even have won this many seats." Asked about Amit Shah's visit to Lucknow, Akhilesh replied, "You have taken too long to arrive, my lord." Maurya joined the INDIA alliance after meeting Rahul Gandhi in Delhi Former minister and Apni Janta Party president Swami Prasad Maurya met Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on 3 October. Maurya announced that he was joining the INDIA alliance. He said discussions on the number of seats his party would contest would take place later. "We want Rahul Gandhi to become the country's next Prime Minister," he said. He had accused the SP of straying from socialist ideology Swami Prasad Maurya had accused the SP leadership of straying from socialist ideology and discriminating against him. His statements on the Ramcharitmanas and the consecration ceremony of the Ram temple in Ayodhya had triggered opposition within the party. Maurya alleged that the party leadership had failed to defend him when party leaders attacked him and opposition to him grew. He left the SP and formed his own party in 2024 After resigning as national general secretary on 13 February 2024, Maurya tried to speak to SP president Akhilesh Yadav, but his frustration grew when no meaningful initiative followed. On 20 February 2024, he resigned from the SP's primary membership, the post of national general secretary and his membership of the Legislative Council (MLC). Two days later, on 22 February 2024, he formed his own party, the Rashtriya Shoshit Samaj Party. Key points from Akhilesh's press conference 1. Women teachers voted unitedly against the BJP Akhilesh Yadav said, "Educated voters in Varanasi and the surrounding areas have handed the 'double-engine' government a 'double zero' this time." Referring to the passage of the Women's Reservation Bill in Parliament, he targeted the Union government and asked why the legislation had not yet been implemented despite being passed. He said women teachers and women voters had therefore united to vote against the BJP in this election. 2. MLC elections are not just a victory but a fight to save democracy Akhilesh referred to the famous statement by former US President Abraham Lincoln: "Government of the people, by the people, for the people." He said the MLC elections were not merely about winning but represented a major fight to save democracy. He added that the party's leaders and workers had proved that they would never allow the people's voice to be suppressed. 3. Biometric verification should be mandatory during elections Akhilesh alleged that around 26,000 primary schools had been shut down in the state, while thousands of new liquor shops had been opened. He claimed that question papers for more than 20 competitive examinations had been leaked under the current government and that recruitment irregularities had taken place. Questioning the impartiality of the Election Commission, Akhilesh demanded that biometric verification be made mandatory during elections to prevent bogus voting. 4. 'Even if we win all 80 seats, we still want ballot papers' Akhilesh once again advocated holding elections using ballot papers instead of EVMs. He said some of the world's most developed and prosperous countries, including the US and Germany, conduct elections using ballot papers. He also claimed that Germany's Constitution considered voting through EVMs unconstitutional. "I have said this on the floor of the House as well. Even if the Samajwadi Party wins all 80 out of 80 Lok Sabha seats, we will still demand that elections in the country be conducted using ballot papers," he said. 5. 'The courage of party workers is the real foundation of victory' Congratulating the candidates who won the MLC elections, Akhilesh said, "I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all our colleagues who have won. I also thank all the voters who placed their trust in the Samajwadi Party." He said the courage and determination shown by party workers in standing their ground during voting and counting had been the real foundation of the victory. 6. On the Varanasi victory, he said the people had stood by the truth Expressing happiness over the results in the Varanasi division, Akhilesh said the people had stood by the truth in an area where the government had made grand claims. He concluded by saying that the victory was only the beginning. As the truth reached more people, the Samajwadi Party's standing was steadily improving, he added. What did the newly elected MLC members say? Read here Dr Man Singh Yadav (Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates' constituency) said the SP workers' strategy had succeeded despite pressure from the government and administration. He promised that the Old Pension Scheme (OPS) would be restored if his party formed the government. Akash Agrawal (Agra Teachers' constituency) alleged that the SP would have won 8 seats instead of 5 if the administration had not indulged in electoral malpractice. Lal Bihari Yadav (Varanasi Teachers' constituency) alleged that the police had raided the homes of his party workers and office-bearers a day before the election and tried to intimidate them.

stories.title: 3 teams investigate crores buried underground:Police reach Pune to probe links; ₹5 crore cash found in a blue drum in Prayagraj
stories.summary: The mystery surrounding crores of cash buried underground in Prayagraj is deepening. Three teams have reached the spot to investigate more than ₹5 crore hidden in blue drums underground. The teams include officials from the Income Tax Department, the police and a bank. Bank employees will count the notes under the supervision of Income Tax officials. Meanwhile, a police team has also been sent to Pune to investigate the case. The investigation teams are trying to find out where such a large sum came from and how it reached Prayagraj. Cash worth crores was recovered from Rakesh Yadav's house in Baraipur village, 32 kilometres from the district headquarters, on Wednesday night. Bundles of ₹500 notes had been wrapped in cloth and buried underground. The recovered amount is estimated to be around ₹5 crore. See three pictures... Bundles of notes were repeatedly brought from Pune The investigation so far has revealed that Rajesh and Rakesh, residents of Nawabganj, used to bring cash worth crores of rupees from Pune to Prayagraj, fill it into drums and then bury them in the ground. A team has also been sent to Pune after questioning the two brothers. The two brothers worked for several years for a jeweller in Pune. They returned to Prayagraj during COVID-19. It is suspected that cash worth crores of rupees was brought here during this period. Investigating agencies suspect that, apart from the three drums, the family may also have hidden bundles of notes in the house, orchard, vacant plot or another property. Police cut off the village's electricity before conducting the raid Rakesh Yadav, also known as Mahakaal, has his ancestral house in Baraipur village in the Nawabganj area. The police had received information that Rakesh had hidden money stolen in a theft underground inside the house. This information reached Police Commissioner Piyush Mordia. After this, a police team, including DCP (Ganganagar) Sonam Kumar and ADCP Pushkar Verma, reached the spot at 6 p.m. on Wednesday. The electricity supply to the entire village was cut off before the operation. A search operation was then launched. ACP of Soraon, Shyamjeet Pramila Singh, was also present during the operation. Search operation continued for four and a half hours According to the police, three blue drums buried in the ground were found during a search of the house. Bundles of notes wrapped in cloth had been placed inside them. The police seized the cash, sealed the house and cordoned it off. After conducting the search operation for around four and a half hours, the police left the spot at 10:30 p.m. The police have also taken Rakesh's brother Bablu into custody. Police teams took the entire family with them. More than 40 police personnel have been deployed around the house. The police have also cordoned off and secured Rakesh's garden and vacant land adjoining the house. Villagers claim: 22 bighas of land bought within a few years Villagers said that several years ago, Rakesh Yadav had lived in Pune with his brother-in-law and his wife's brother and worked at a jeweller's house. During the Covid pandemic, he returned to his home in Bareipur. He then bought 22 bighas of land worth more than ₹10 crore. He built a house after investing around ₹1 crore. He bought two tractors, a DJ system and a pickup vehicle. He then started a cement and steel-rods business there. Rakesh lives in the village with two brothers Rakesh has six brothers. Of them, Rakesh, Rajesh and Lavkush live in the village, while the other three-Chhotu, Rajendra and Abhishek-live elsewhere. Their father, Ram Aadhar, has died. DCP Ganganagar Sonam Kumar said: Cash worth crores has been recovered from three drums buried beneath the ground at Rakesh's house. Police personnel have been deployed at the site. An investigation team from the Income Tax Department has arrived from Lucknow to investigate the case. A team has also been sent to Pune.

stories.title: Father, son die after falling from 23rd floor in Noida:Man fell while trying to save son, who slipped while plucking flowers on balcony
stories.summary: Father and 11-year-old son fall to their deaths from the 23rd floor in Noida: Father was helping his son pluck flowers using a ladder when the boy slipped; he fell while trying to save him The deceased have been identified as Randeep Patra (40) and his son Aarav (11). The incident took place at around 4.20 am on Friday at Mahagun Mywoods Society in the Bisrakh police station area. The father was helping his son pluck flowers using a ladder on the balcony when the boy lost his footing and began dangling from the balcony. In an attempt to save him, the father also fell from the 23rd floor. Both died on the spot. Family was preparing to visit Khatu Shyam Randeep Patra (40) worked as a section officer at the Central Secretariat in Delhi. He lived with his wife and 11-year-old son Aarav in Tower 23 of Mahagun Mywoods Society. During police questioning, his wife said, "We were supposed to visit Khatu Shyam with the family on Friday morning to register a plot of land. Randeep and Aarav went to the balcony to pluck flowers for the Puja(rituals). I was getting ready inside the house. Aarav slipped from the ladder on the balcony. Randeep rushed to save him, but both lost their footing and fell from the 23rd floor." Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central Noida) Praveen Ranjan Singh said: “At around 4.20 am on Friday, the control room received information through the 112 emergency helpline that two people had fallen from a height at Mywoods Society. The police sent the bodies for post-mortem examination. The matter is being thoroughly investigated from all angles.”

stories.title: Rickshaw driver's son detained by ATS in Kanpur:Mother breaks down, says he claimed to be playing games on his laptop when asked
stories.summary: There was a hole in my liver, and my son was paying for my treatment... How will I get treatment now? His father drove a rickshaw to educate him so that he would support us in our old age, but the police took him away. My son worked in digital marketing; he could not have been involved in terrorist activities. This was said by Savitri, the mother of 12th-pass Ankit Sanghwar, who was arrested by the ATS in Kanpur. The mother said, "When we asked my son, he would say that he was playing games. He worked on a laptop at night." His father, Prahlad, said, "My son cannot do this. He had bought a second-hand laptop on instalments from Govind Nagar only six months ago." On 24 October, the Uttar Pradesh ATS arrested from Kanpur the accused who carried out a bomb blast. He had sent emails threatening to blow up schools in Uttar Pradesh, Delhi and Gurugram, as well as actor Diljit Dosanjh, with bombs. The UP ATS said the accused created and sold fake email IDs to people based in countries such as Pakistan, Bangladesh, Turkey, Egypt and the USA. These IDs were used in anti-national activities. He had sold more than 5 lakh fake email IDs, and the investigation found that he received $20 to $50 for each email ID. Hole in mother's liver, cataracts in her eyes Ankit's mother, Savitri, said tearfully, "I also have cataracts in my eyes. My son was the one getting me treated at a private hospital in the city." She said, "Who will get me treated now?" The family could not believe that their son had become involved in such anti-national activities. Savitri said everything had been going smoothly. But on Saturday, two men in plain clothes arrived and said they were taking him for questioning. However, there has been no trace of him for six days. I have visited the police station and outpost repeatedly. My son is innocent; a friend from Barra has framed him. Received house under PM Awas Yojana in 2025 Prahlad Sankhwar, originally from Anoia village in the Sajeti police station area, moved to Kanpur four years ago. He initially lived in a rented accommodation in Barra's Damodar Nagar. On 20 July 2025, he bought a one-room unit in Block 5 under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana in the Sen Paschimpara police station area for ₹2 lakh. Prahlad, his wife Savitri and their younger son, accused Ankit, live in the house. Prahlad drives a rickshaw, while his wife Savitri works as a labourer. Their elder son Atit lives in Block Three in a rented colony with his wife Mamta and their two children. Their middle son Dharmendra works on a contractual basis for a municipal corporation in Arunachal Pradesh. His father, Prahlad, said that Ankit passed Class 12 in 2020. As the family's financial condition was not good, he did not continue his studies. He then started working as a labourer. After saving money, he bought a scooter in 2021. He often remained engrossed in his phone from 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. When asked, he said he was investing money in the share market. His sister-in-law, Mamta, said that he invested money in the share market several times, but never made a profit. After that, he became involved in all such activities. Now, read the full story... Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal said the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) received information that threatening emails were being sent from simenbriones9265@gmail.com to various schools in Gautam Buddh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi and Gurugram. The emails contained threats, purportedly from the Khalistan National Army and Babbar Khalsa, to bomb schools in various states, a proposed show by Punjabi singer and actor Diljit Dosanjh in the Delhi-NCR region, and his home. When the ATS began investigating the emails, it found that the mastermind with access to the email ID was Ankit Sankhwar, the son of Prahlad and a resident of Anoia village in the Ghatampur police station area of Kanpur. The police commissioner said Ankit used Wi-Fi and proxy networks to create fake email IDs, which he sold to anti-India elements based in Pakistan, Bangladesh and other countries, receiving payment in cryptocurrency in return. After receiving intelligence, the UP ATS conducted a raid on Wednesday and arrested Ankit Sanghwar. The ATS recovered a mobile phone and laptop from the accused. The police commissioner said several Excel files and crypto wallets were also found on the accused's mobile phone and laptop. When the Excel files found on the laptop were examined, they revealed shocking details. The investigation found that the accused had created 5 lakh fake email IDs using a proxy network. During questioning, Ankit said he had been creating fake email IDs since 2021. The police commissioner said the email ID from which threatening messages were sent to schools in Gurugram, Delhi and Noida was also found on the laptop. Another fake email ID, smithjohnson6889@gmail.com, was also found; it had been used to threaten to blow up the Mumbai mayor's office on 23 October. This is how the accused sold email IDs The arrested accused, Ankit, said he used to buy and sell these fake email accounts by joining Buy and Sell groups on Facebook. He had obtained these fake IDs through the groups from people connected to groups in Pakistan, Bangladesh, Turkey, Egypt and other countries. These people based abroad are involved in anti-India activities. Ankit said he sent the fake email IDs in an Excel sheet containing the email ID, its password, recovery email and two-factor code. Fake ID sold to Bangladeshi youth for 6000 USTD Ankit said he had connected with a Bangladeshi youth, Alamin Islam alias Alamin, through Facebook and WhatsApp, and had been asked to provide fake email IDs. Ankit subsequently provided the fake ID simenbriones9265@gmail.com, and 6,000 USDT (cryptocurrency) was paid in return through this fake email. The ATS found evidence of this on Ankit's mobile phone. Ankit said he had sent the simenbriones9265@gmail.com ID to Alamin, and that it was used to send threatening messages to various schools on 12 October. Threatening emails were also sent to the Mumbai Mayor's House on 23 October from the email ID smithjohnson6889@gmail.com. The passwords, recovery email addresses and two-factor codes for both email IDs were sent to Bangladeshi national Alamin via WhatsApp in an Excel sheet. The Police Commissioner said Ankit was connected via WhatsApp with people in Pakistan, Bangladesh, Egypt, Turkey and the USA. The ATS also found a large number of USDT transactions from foreign numbers. The ATS investigation revealed that Ankit was paid $20 to $50 in exchange for a fake email ID, and the ATS also found evidence of this.

stories.title: PET first shift exam concludes peacefully in Gorakhpur:Candidates rate paper moderate, say DI questions were tricky
stories.summary: The first shift of the Preliminary Eligibility Test (PET)-2026 was held peacefully under tight security in Gorakhpur on Friday. Candidates who came out after the exam described the paper as moderate, saying it was neither too difficult nor too easy. However, they said the questions on mathematics and Data Interpretation (DI) took more time to solve. Candidates found the questions on General Knowledge, current affairs and reasoning relatively easy. After the first shift ended, entry for the second shift also began. Strict security and monitoring arrangements were in place at the examination centres. Exam conducted peacefully under tight security Special security arrangements were made at examination centres across the district for PET-2026. Candidates were allowed to enter the examination halls only after proper checking. The entire exam was conducted under CCTV surveillance. After the first shift ended, candidates came out of the centres and shared their experiences. Most described the paper as moderate, while some said the mathematics and DI questions were time-consuming. The entry was closed at 1,372 exam centres across 60 districts in the state. Strict checking was carried out at several centres. In Prayagraj, Lucknow and Pratapgarh, male candidates were asked to remove their shoes and socks for checking. In Gorakhpur, candidates were even asked to remove their handkerchiefs. In Bareilly, female candidates were asked to open their hair for checking. Their hair clips, earrings and chains were also removed. In Sitapur, women candidates removed their jewellery and handed it over to their family members before entering the exam centres. Around 11.80 lakh candidates will appear for the exam in two shifts today. The first shift will be held from 10 am to 12 noon, while the second shift will take place from 3 pm to 5 pm. Entry for the second shift will begin at 1 pm, and the gates will close at 1:30 pm. Schools up to Class 12 have been closed in all 60 districts where the exam is being held. The first phase of the exam took place on October 25. Of the 11.80 lakh candidates scheduled to appear, 8.27 lakh took the exam that day. The final phase will be held on November 1. A total of around 35.41 lakh candidates have registered for PET 2026. Bangle removed during checking in Hardoi Subhashini, who travelled from Lucknow to Hardoi to take the PET, was also asked to remove her bangle and hair clip. She said the staff asked her to remove the bangle during checking. When she refused, she was told that she would not be allowed inside without removing it. She then had to take it off. Candidates reach exam centres in rain in Bhadohi In Bhadohi, candidates reached 13 exam centres despite the rain. Security staff put up tarpaulin sheets to protect themselves and the candidates from the rain while carrying out checks. After the checking, candidates were allowed to enter the centres.

stories.title: PET exam enters second day at 45 centres in Lucknow:Three-level security checks before entry, female candidates asked to remove shoes for frisking
stories.summary: The second day of the PET (Preliminary Eligibility Test) is being held in Lucknow today. Entry for candidates began at 8 a.m. at the capital's 45 examination centres. The examination will be conducted in two shifts. The first shift will begin at 10 a.m., while the second shift will run from 3 p.m. to 5 p.m. Tight security arrangements have been made at the examination centres. Candidates are being allowed inside only after three levels of checking. Female candidates are also undergoing thorough searches. During the checks, they are being asked to remove their shoes for inspection. Security tightened ahead of Amit Shah's visit Union Home Minister Amit Shah is also visiting Lucknow today. The venue for his programme is close to the examination centre. Security arrangements have therefore been tightened along the entire route. Police surveillance has been increased on the roads. A large police force has also been deployed at the examination centre. Security agencies are on alert in view of the examination and the Home Minister's visit. Candidates are being allowed to enter the examination centre only after completing the checking process.

stories.title: ‘BJP's foothold is like Angad’s foot, none can move it’:‘Focus on the target like Arjuna’; Shah attends state executive meeting
stories.summary: Amit Shah is in Lucknow on Friday, where he told BJP workers at the party's state executive committee meeting that the BJP is like Angad's foot in Uttar Pradesh and no one can move it. He urged workers to prepare for the 2027 Assembly elections, saying, "Keep your eyes fixed on the target like Arjuna. We have to form the government." Shah arrived in Lucknow after nearly nine months. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and both Deputy Chief Ministers welcomed him. Yogi and Shah were seated next to each other during the meeting. Uttar Pradesh BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary and state in-charge Vinod Tawde were also present. Addressing the meeting at the auditorium of Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University, Shah discussed the roadmap for the Assembly elections and gave more than 2,500 party workers a strategy to help the BJP secure a third consecutive term in Uttar Pradesh. Pankaj Chaudhary urged workers to remain alert and stay among voters. He said they need to prevent people from being misled, alleging that attempts are being made to create confusion and unrest through foreign funding. BJP MP Ravi Kishan described Shah as the "Chanakya of politics" and said his arrival was very auspicious. Referring to the Bengal elections, he said, "We saw it during the Bengal elections." Shah will remain at the meeting for around four hours before returning to Delhi. CM Yogi Adityanath will address the concluding session at 5 pm.

stories.title: Man jailed for 20-years for kidnapping and sexually assaulting minor:Varanasi court imposes ₹40,000 fine, 70% to go to victim
stories.summary: Varanasi's special POCSO court has convicted Cantt resident Tanveer Khan in a case involving the abduction and sexual exploitation of a teenage girl. On Thursday, the court of Special Judge Nitin Pandey sentenced him to 20 years' rigorous imprisonment and fined him ₹40,000. The court ordered that 70 per cent of the fine be paid to the victim as compensation. The case dates back to 8 March 2023, when the 15-year-old girl did not return home after going to the market. Cantt police registered a case and began an investigation following a complaint by the family. Case registered following family's complaint According to the prosecution, the girl's mother lodged an FIR at Cantt police station. She said her daughter had gone to the market to buy सामान, but did not return for a long time. The family searched for her, but found no information. The family then approached the police and informed them about the entire incident. Based on the complaint, police registered a case against Cantt resident Tanveer Khan. Investigation revealed sexual exploitation The police investigation found that the accused had lured the teenage girl away with him. After a search, the police recovered the girl and arrested the accused. During the investigation, it also emerged that the girl had been sexually abused. The police then completed the investigation and filed a charge sheet in court. Testimony of seven witnesses and medical report formed the basis During the trial, the prosecution presented a total of seven witnesses. The witnesses' statements, the medical report and other evidence were submitted before the court. On the basis of this evidence and the police investigation, the court found the accused guilty. He was then sentenced to 20 years' rigorous imprisonment and fined ₹40,000. Officials and employees of the Varanasi Commissionerate played a role in securing the conviction and sentence in this case.

stories.title: Special train to run between Gorakhpur and Mumbai:Festival travel home to become easier for passengers
stories.summary: Railways has decided to run a festival special train between Gorakhpur and Mumbai's Bandra Terminus to accommodate the additional rush of passengers during the festive season. Train numbers 05091/05092 Gorakhpur-Bandra Terminus-Gorakhpur Festival Special will make two trips in each direction. The train will depart from Gorakhpur on 9 and 16 November, while it will leave Bandra Terminus on 11 and 18 November. This will make travel more convenient for passengers travelling to Mumbai and other cities along the route. According to Railways, train number 05091 Gorakhpur-Bandra Terminus Festival Special will depart from Gorakhpur at 9:55 pm on the scheduled dates. The train will reach Kanpur Central via Basti, Gonda and Lucknow. It will then enter Gujarat via Tundla, Idgah Agra, Gangapur City, Kota, Bhawani Mandi and Ratlam. The train will reach Bandra Terminus at 12 noon the following day, stopping at Vadodara, Surat, Vapi and Borivali stations. Train will depart from Bandra at 1:45 am on its return journey Train will have 21 coaches According to the railway, the Festival Special will have a total of 21 coaches, including two LSLRD, 11 general and eight sleeper coaches. This will give passengers the option to travel according to their convenience.

stories.title: Rain alert in all 75 UP districts:Heavy rain warning in 21; strong winds in Lucknow, hail likely
stories.summary: Rain alerts have been issued for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh on Friday due to Cyclone 'Arnab'. A warning of heavy rain has been issued for 21 districts, including Gorakhpur, Ayodhya and Moradabad. Light rain and thunderstorms are expected in the other districts. Meanwhile, skies have been overcast in Lucknow and the surrounding districts since Friday morning. Strong winds are blowing. Earlier, light rain was recorded in 18 districts, including Ayodhya, Ghaziabad and Gorakhpur, on Thursday. Lightning struck the minaret of the Badi Masjid in Saharanpur. Clouds gathered over Lucknow in the afternoon, followed by rain. Meerut and Kashi received heavy rain in the evening. Unseasonal rain in the last week of October threatens to damage the paddy crop that is ready for harvesting in the fields. It could also affect preparations for sowing wheat, potatoes and mustard. In view of the cyclone's possible impact, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed state officials to remain on alert. The administration has been instructed to monitor the weather situation and take precautionary measures as required.

stories.title: Could Einstein’s equations explain the universe’s expansion?
stories.summary: Researchers from UC Davis have proposed that dark energy may not be necessary to explain the universe's acceleration. They found weak points in the Lambda-cold dark matter model using Einstein's equations. By examining instabilities in Friedmann spacetimes, they suggest alternative explanations for cosmic expansion. Their work raises questions about the Copernican principle in the context of current models. This research could lead to significant shifts in our understanding of cosmology.

stories.title: Scientists have developed a new technology that could make electric car batteries smaller, lighter and longer-lasting, potentially letting drivers travel farther on a single charge without carrying a heavier battery
stories.summary: Scientists from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology developed a new technology for anode-free batteries. This innovative approach focuses on enhancing lithium deposition to improve battery efficiency and longevity. By restructuring the copper surface for lithium storage, they have addressed issues with dendrite formation. Applying a thin layer of MXene further stabilizes the battery's performance.

Ranch Easement Preserves Habitat: Winn descendants shield 165 acres; Blanco River recharge gains
stories.summary: Four Winns Ranch in Texas, a treasured historical site, is preserved through dedicated efforts by the Winn family alongside conservation partners. Spanning 165 acres, this land is vital for protecting local wildlife habitats and water sources. Originally acquired by the noteworthy artist James Buchanan Buck Winn Jr., the ranch possesses rich cultural heritage while fostering agricultural and ecotourism activities, aiding the survival of rare birds and endangered aquatic species.

12th century Nepalese Manjushri statue sold for about Rs 166 crore in 2026
stories.summary: A 12th-century Manjushri sculpture from Nepal recently sold for around ₹166 crore, illuminating the exceptional artistry of Newar creators from the Kathmandu Valley. This sculpture's intriguing journey through different collections illustrates its cultural significance and uniqueness. Furthermore, the influence of Newar craftsmanship on Buddhist art permeated throughout Tibet and Asia, showcasing Nepal's profound artistic legacy and its vital role in international art history.

A Neanderthal who died 75,000 years ago may have been killed by a wooden spear deliberately aimed at his heart, scientists say, offering rare evidence of targeted violence among our closest ancient relatives
stories.summary: A recent archaeological find in Shanidar Cave revealed a Neanderthal skeleton showing signs of lethal violence, potentially from a wooden spear, suggesting that early human emotional responses might mirror those of today. The evidence hints at both a targeted attack and social care, as the skeleton bore previous injuries. This discovery serves as a window into the dualities of early human life, showcasing their capacity for both violence and compassion.

£5 ivory chess piece found in family drawer sells for £735,000 after 55 years
stories.summary: An extraordinary Lewis chessman carving has fetched an impressive £735,000 at auction. Hidden away in a drawer for more than 55 years by the family of the dealer, this remarkable figure was revealed as a warder, part of the legendary Lewis Chessmen collection. Originally found in 1831, this collection comprises 93 intricately carved pieces from 1150 to 1200 AD, though the auction leaves four original pieces still unaccounted for.

In 1913, an Ohio couple sent their eight-month-old son to his grandmother through the postal service
stories.summary: In the year 1913, the US Postal Service unveiled Parcel Post, permitting the mailing of bigger packages. Ingenious parents even started shipping their small children to reduce travel expenses, gaining notoriety when six-year-old May Pierstorff was dispatched 73 miles away. This phenomenon sparked national debate, leading to the ban of child parceling, although similar incidents lingered until 1915, prompting stricter postal regulations to curb such extraordinary practices.

stories.title: Idaho Supreme Court revives condo owners' challenge to property changes approved by 88% vote
stories.summary: The Idaho Supreme Court has revived a legal dispute involving condominium owners challenging changes to property ownership. The contentious amendments were made by the Crystal Beach Condominium Association, affecting owners' shares and rental rules. A previous dismissal by a lower court has been partly overturned, confirming owners' rights to challenge changes impacting their property. Plaintiffs now have their claims for declaratory relief and title slander allowed to proceed.

stories.title: Texas court reopens insurance dispute after landslide destroys two homeowners' backyards
stories.summary: A legal dispute involving home insurance coverage in Travis County has been returned to court for further hearings. The Texas Third Court of Appeal overturned a previous ruling that held the insurer liable for damages. Homeowners claimed that earth movement caused significant damage to their properties, leading to a denial of their insurance claims. The appeals court requires the insurer to demonstrate the cause of the landslide.

stories.title: Florida has allocated $3 million to acquire a 642-acre property along the Suwannee River; officials say ending its current land use could save 159,000 gallons of water daily and reduce nutrient inputs
stories.summary: Florida has allocated $3 million for the acquisition of property along the Suwannee River to reduce water consumption. The Suwannee Sandhill Tract-Drew Property will help conserve approximately 158,800 gallons of water daily. This initiative is part of a larger $100 million investment aimed at various water conservation projects. The acquisition will facilitate the restoration of the land for wildlife habitats and public recreation.

stories.title: Dorothy Dandridge Home Listed: Former Hollywood Hills residence hits $5.499 million; price up nearly 90% from 2014 sale
stories.summary: A stunning Mediterranean-style home in Hollywood Hills, once owned by the iconic actress Dorothy Dandridge, is now on the market for nearly $5.5 million. Covering 4,368 square feet, the residence boasts four luxurious bedrooms and five opulent bathrooms. Dandridge's impactful legacy as a pioneering Black actress echoes through this property, complemented by breathtaking views of Los Angeles. The current owners have thoughtfully renovated it while respecting its historic charm.

Bhutan dedicates Buddhist stupa to PM Modi; Rijiju calls it ‘huge honour’ for India
stories.summary: In a heartfelt gesture symbolizing the deep-rooted friendship between Bhutan and India, King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck dedicated a stupa to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This event took place in Gelephu Mindfulness City, where 108 stupas are being raised. Union minister Kiren Rijiju represented India, conveying PM Modi's gratitude. The stupa, numbered 76, represents the strong ties shared by the two nations.

Prosecutors said she used the money to buy five properties, two Tesla vehicles, including a Cybertruck, and expensive collectibles. She must also pay $32.9 million in restitution.

Beavers set to return to Loch Ness after 500 years, with 15 family groups approved for release.
stories.summary: In an exciting development, wild beavers are about to return to Loch Ness after centuries of absence. The Scottish nature agency NatureScot has sanctioned their release as part of a transformative rewilding project. Over the next three years, conservationists will introduce family groups of beavers to the area’s waterways, focusing on enhancing biodiversity and wildlife habitats, while also implementing strategies to resolve any conflicts with local farmers and landowners.

stories.title: Delaware couple wins disputed backyard land after 20 years, despite neighbours' $30,000 demand
stories.summary: After two decades of contention, a Delaware court officially awarded Joseph W.C. Murray, Jr. and Danielle F. Murray ownership of a long-disputed parcel of land. The case arose when the Preradovic family challenged property lines after purchasing an adjacent lot. Failed negotiations led to litigation, ultimately resulting in the court granting the Murrays the rear yard while their claims to the front areas were rejected.

The couple are reportedly considering downsizing as their children have gradually moved out of the family home.

He was homeless twice, now he is a billionaire
stories.summary: John Paul DeJoria overcame homelessness not once, but twice, before establishing thriving ventures in the hair-care and spirits sectors. A dedicated philanthropist, he signed the Giving Pledge to relinquish a minimum of half his fortune. Through the JP’s Peace, Love & Happiness Foundation, he champions diverse initiatives, especially food security. Notably, the Grow Appalachia program has empowered countless families to cultivate their own food.

stories.title: Ming royal descendant turned Buddhist monk painted 12 leaves of birds and flowers, sold for Rs 75 cr
stories.summary: Bada Shanren, originally named Zhu Da, was born into the Ming royal lineage in 1626. Following the Ming dynasty's collapse in 1644, he sought solace in a Buddhist monastery for many years. Later, he embraced secular life as a renowned painter, crafting works that emphasize bold simplicity. His masterpiece, 'Flowers and Birds,' comprised twelve ink-on-paper leaves and recently fetched HK$61.9 million at Christie's Hong Kong auction.

stories.title: Dhak beats on the Thames! British Bengalis take Durga Puja to London's iconic river
stories.summary: British Bengalis marked the fifth annual Durga Parade on the River Thames in London this Saturday. The event featured a decorated idol of Goddess Durga sailing past famous landmarks like Big Ben and the London Eye. Musical performances and dancing were part of the celebrations aboard the boat, showcasing local talent. Bihar Tourism Minister Kedar Prasad Gupta attended and invited Indians to visit Bihar.

Lexi Long launched her business, Slime & Squish, on October 1 and reached her fundraising goal within nine days. Her business has since gained more than 30,000 social media followers and attracted customers at local events and shops.

A Chester Zoo collection of Dracula orchids has been declared nationally important, drawing attention to rare flowers with bizarre, vampire-like appearances that are increasingly threatened in the wild.
stories.summary: Chester Zoo recently received National Plant Collection status for its impressive collection of Dracula orchids. These unique flowers, which mimic various shapes, face threats from habitat loss and illegal collection. Pollination occurs through specific fungi-attracting smells rather than traditional scents. Chester Zoo's horticulturists are dedicated to preserving these rare species amidst growing environmental challenges. Currently, the orchids are not on public display but contribute to plant biodiversity conservation efforts.

stories.title: Florida is planning 4,800 acres of wetlands at the mouth of the Kissimmee River to remove phosphorus before it reaches Lake Okeechobee, decades after engineers began undoing the river's earlier straightening
stories.summary: Florida is planning a 4,800-acre wetland project to filter phosphorus pollution before it reaches Lake Okeechobee. This initiative involves directing stormwater through treatment areas filled with aquatic vegetation. Wetlands help mitigate impacts of excess nutrients and support local ecosystems. The project has been under development since 2019 and will provide flood protection and recreational opportunities. A public meeting is scheduled for November 2026 to discuss construction details.

stories.title: A cupboard buried when Mount Vesuvius destroyed Pompeii in AD 79 has yielded 38 bronze coins and at least 24 tiny childhood charms; archaeologists say the objects reveal glimpses of a family's lost everyday life
stories.summary: Italian archaeologists recently uncovered a sealed wooden cupboard in Pompeii, revealing artifacts from 2,000 years ago. Among the findings were 38 bronze coins, personal care items, and a unique childhood necklace. The discovery adds to our understanding of daily life in ancient Rome, highlighting ordinary people's lives. It is speculated that the residents could not retrieve their belongings during the volcanic eruption.

stories.title: No paneer, no honey, no milky chai? The real challenge of going vegan in India
Trump says Bolsonaro can remain in US indefinitely, calls Brazil election a 'disgrace'
stories.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil after his electoral defeat, despite having led in several opinion polls. His departure came after a Brazilian Supreme Court justice ordered his passport revoked. He is also facing two federal money-laundering investigations, while police in Brazil had considered him a flight risk. The comments came as US secretary of state Marco Rubio held talks with Brazilian foreign minister Mauro Vieira.

stories.title: India trying to bring Russia, Ukraine & Europe to the table on 3 fronts: Jaishankar
stories.summary: India's External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has discussed the protection of civilian shipping with Russia, Ukraine, and European nations. Efforts are being made to restore grain exports through the Black Sea, which have significantly declined. Additionally, the safety of energy infrastructure and fuel shipments is a major concern amid the ongoing conflict. Different interpretations of energy infrastructure complicate discussions on protection measures.

US midterms: Trump ready with plan to outmaneuver Democrat-controlled Congress

These include policies on immigration, tariffs, housing costs and federal spending, according to a White House official and two people familiar with the plans.

stories.title: Veiled marble bust sells for record €1.925 million in Vienna
stories.summary: A marble sculpture of a veiled lady created by Antonio Corradini recently sold for €1.925 million. The auction took place in Vienna and set a new world record for the artist. The sculpture is 60 centimeters tall and showcases intricate craftsmanship that mimics the look of cloth. Bidders from the saleroom and via telephone competed for the artwork, but a telephone bidder ultimately won.

stories.title: Florida court overturns order against couple accused of disrupting weddings at a historic mansion
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, a Florida appeals court has reversed a previous order aimed at curbing a couple's disruptive activities that allegedly disrupted outdoor wedding ceremonies with loud machinery and gunfire. While the immediate limitations have been lifted, the legal battle persists with potential civil nuisance claims still on the table. The appeals court mandates that any new restrictions must strictly adhere to specific evidence criteria.

stories.title: Maya Jama donates £83,500 to charity after losing Celebrity Traitors, matching her potential prize money
stories.summary: Maya Jama, who participated in Celebrity Traitors, donated her potential prize of £83,500 to Action for Children. This charity supports children facing various hardships across the UK, including poverty and abuse. Following her exit in the show's finale, Jama shared her donation on social media platforms. Fellow contestants Sebastian Croft and Romesh Ranganathan each contributed their winnings to different charitable organizations.

stories.title: Rahul's Ramlila 'jalsa' to 'rub salt in wounds' of 1984 Sikh riot victims: Amit Shah
stories.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah said the "jalsa" would reopen painful memories for the victims and their families, accusing the Congress of showing little sensitivity towards the tragedy. Shah made the remarks in Chandigarh while addressing a gathering after inaugurating and laying the foundation stones for development projects worth Rs 258 crore.

stories.title: 'Stay quiet or I'll speak for an hour': Kharge's playful warning to supporters at Ramlila Maidan rally
'After Gyanesh, you are next': Rahul Gandhi says PM Modi, Amit Shah will face justice for 'vote chori'
'Gyanesh, when will you vanish?': Mamata mocks CEC; Akhilesh invokes Haldighati - who said what at INDIA bloc rally
stories.summary: During a rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, senior leaders from the INDIA coalition raised alarms about electoral roll manipulation. They accused the BJP of endangering democracy through the Chief Election Commissioner. Opposition leaders like Rahul Gandhi and Mamata Banerjee demanded Gyanesh Kumar's removal and vowed to continue their campaign against him.

stories.title: Inside UK PM’s Diwali party at his residence; Gita chanting to vegetarian snacks, woman shares
stories.summary: Shanu had the unique opportunity to celebrate Diwali at 10 Downing Street, the iconic residence of the UK Prime Minister. The event was beautifully adorned with traditional decorations, offering a range of vegetarian delicacies. During the gathering, the UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his wife participated in lighting a ceremonial diya, emphasizing the importance of community contributions and the strengthening of UK-India relations.

stories.title: US couple's fence extends nine feet into neighbour's land, court rules in their favour
stories.summary: A Delaware couple who maintained a fence and garden for more than 20 years won a property dispute after their new neighbours demanded $30,000 to let them keep the land. The neighbours claimed the fence crossed the legal boundary, but an October 30 court ruling recognised the couple's ownership of the entire disputed strip, including an unfenced garden planter, through adverse possession.

stories.title: Safari West's 400-acre wildlife preserve enters a new nonprofit era after decades of conservation
‘Will dig you out from ground, if needed’: Kharge warns CEC Gyanesh Kumar at INDIA bloc rally
‘Did they really have to choose this day?’ BJP targets Congress over INDIA bloc rally on anniversary of 1984 riots
stories.summary: BJP organized a protest march in West Delhi's Hari Nagar demanding an apology from Congress for the 1984 anti-Sikh violence. Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri described the killings as a well-planned genocide rather than a riot. Several leaders participated in the march, expressing concerns over Congress's perceived failure to acknowledge the tragedy. The protest coincided with the opposition's rally addressing electoral irregularities on the same day.

stories.title: ‘Deeply shameful’: Tharoor slams UK over colonialism omission in slavery apology
stories.summary: Responding to British Prime Minister Andy Burnham's remarks in a post on X on Saturday, Shashi Tharoor said he had long maintained that putting a monetary figure on the damage caused by British rule was difficult. He also said Britain had never formally apologised for the destruction and exploitation carried out during its colonial rule.

stories.title: DGCA mandates twin pilot operations from Monday, chopper operators threaten to suspend Char Dam flights
'Why do you challenge democracy?' BJP chief Nitin Nabin accuses Rahul Gandhi of acting on behest of foreign powers
stories.summary: BJP leader Nitin Nabin accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of furthering foreign agendas at a rally in Haryana. Nabin criticized Congress for claiming democracy is at risk only when it loses elections in multiple states. He challenged allegations regarding voter deletion and past election irregularities linked to the party’s leadership. Nabin emphasized the need for governance based on the Constitution rather than dynastic politics.

stories.title: 'Every single shop forcibly shut': Rahul Gandhi targets BJP over Connaught Place closures during mega rally
'Cutting 130m voters unacceptable': Shashi Tharoor targets EC amid INDIA bloc's Ramlila Maidan rally
'Gyanesh Kumar can no longer remain in his position': TMC's Sagarika Ghose demands CEC's removal
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress MP Sagarika Ghose has intensified calls for chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to step down. Uniting the opposition for a common cause, leaders stress the urgency to restore trust in the electoral process. At a rally in Delhi, they highlighted the importance of safeguarding voting rights against authoritarian measures.

stories.title: US river straightened 110 years ago to drain land, now set for restoration to reduce floods
stories.summary: Authorities in Tennessee, US, have acquired 985 acres along the South Fork of the Forked Deer River to reduce flooding and restore natural habitats. The river was straightened in 1916 to drain surrounding land, but the changes contributed to flash floods and erosion. The restoration project aims to reconnect the river with its floodplain and eventually open the area to the public.

stories.title: A new fossil from China may reveal the first amphibian known to have lived entirely at sea; the armoured, 2.4-foot creature lived about 237 million years ago, challenging what scientists know about amphibian evolution
stories.summary: A recent discovery of the fossil Gerrothorax maritimus reveals that some ancient amphibians lived completely in marine environments. Dated to approximately 237 million years ago, this species had a flattened body covered in bony armour. The fossils were found in deep-sea sediments, indicating they lived far from landmasses. Geochemical tests confirmed the strontium isotopes matched those in seawater during the Late Triassic period.

stories.title: 'PM Modi, Amit Shah suffering loss': Sanjay Raut on business concerns of traders ahead of INDIA bloc rally
stories.summary: Sanjay Raut asserted that the rally by the INDIA bloc in Delhi would not disrupt business activities. He emphasized that this event signifies the people's demand for a change in government. Supporters of various political parties began gathering for the rally, which aims to address alleged voter roll tampering. The demonstration is expected to attract significant participation amid security measures by the police.

stories.title: 'India not a banana republic': BJP attacks Rahul Gandhi ahead of INDIA bloc rally
stories.summary: Union minister JP Nadda accused Congress and Rahul Gandhi of attempting to destabilize the government and create unrest. Nadda labeled the opposition's rally at Ramlila Maidan as a calculated conspiracy against democracy and the economy. He outlined a model of politics involving misinformation and provoking protests. The INDIA bloc, however, claims to mobilize for democratic rights concerning alleged electoral roll irregularities.

stories.title: 'No military solutions': EAM Jaishankar reveals PM Modi-Putin talks on Ukraine conflict in Delhi, Bishkek
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar conveyed India's diplomatic commitment regarding the Ukraine conflict during discussions in Atlanta. His talks included priorities such as protecting civilian shipping and restoring crucial grain exports. Jaishankar also emphasized the need for energy security in light of ongoing disruptions. He met with counterparts from Russia, Poland, and South Korea to address bilateral and multilateral issues.

stories.title: Ohio couple splits before marriage, court awards woman $41,466 from house sale
stories.summary: An Ohio man who refused to share money from his house sale with his former partner has lost a court battle. The couple had signed an agreement in 2021 to divide the proceeds if the property was sold. After their breakup, the man argued that the woman had not spent enough on renovations. However, an appeals court upheld the agreement, awarding her $41,466.50.

stories.title: ‘A hurry to finish JD(U)’: RJD's Manoj Jha on MLCs who defeated Nitish's party joining BJP
'Remarkable valour': PM Modi pays tribute to Haryana's heritage on foundation day
stories.summary: Celebrating its 60th Foundation Day on November 1, Haryana showcased its rich heritage and remarkable achievements. Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted the state's vital role in agriculture, sports, and defense. Political leaders such as Amit Shah and Rahul Gandhi commended Haryana's vibrant culture. Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini spoke about the significant progress over the decades.

stories.title: Fat-dissolving claims land FatX Solution in regulatory trouble; CDSCO cancels registration
North Korea tests new cluster-bomb warhead under Kim Jong-un's military push
Texas Supreme Court Blocks Neighbours’ Broad Demand to Inspect Woman’s 14-Acre Homestead
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, the Texas Supreme Court has sided with Pamela Bosco, affirming her right to keep her 14-acre homestead intact. The court denied neighbors’ requests for property inspections due to insufficient evidence of alleged violations. This ruling underscores the importance of legal processes in property disputes and confirms that establishing wrongdoing necessitates proper evidence gathering.

stories.title: ‘It was Nehru Ji’s chair’: Cong reveals significance of seat used by Meira Kumar during CEC’s public impeachment

stories.summary: Discovered in the vast Sahara Desert, the meteorite Teghaza 001 is over four billion years old and is confirmed to be a Martian rock via isotopic studies. As researchers delve deeper into its origins, they are unraveling vital insights into the planet's early environmental conditions.

stories.summary: The Hope Diamond embarked on a remarkable journey in 1958 when it was sent as registered mail to the Smithsonian Institution for safekeeping. stories.summary: Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri spoke out about the lasting impact of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, firmly stating that no justification exists for the violence inflicted upon the Sikh community. He lamented the tragic toll and enduring pain endured by victims while commending HS Phoolka's tireless efforts for justice. Researchers found it capable of calculating astronomical cycles and predicting eclipses, intertwining science with the cultural tapestry of ancient Greece.

stories.summary: In a remarkable find in 2003, archaeologists unveiled a cosmetic cream container dating back almost 2,000 years in London. Around 18 minutes later, NVS-03 satellite was placed in a geosynchronous transfer orbit (GTO) of 37,023km apogee and 170km perigee.

Boasting 2,000 perennials alongside newly paved pathways and informative signage, this garden is distinctive in its grounded plantings. When finished, the High Line will welcome millions of annual visitors to enjoy its beauty and tranquility.

With a listing price of $34 million, this expansive estate includes an impressive limestone cave system, a vibrant wildlife park, and a private airport. As the sale process begins, state officials in Pennsylvania are looking into potential conservation strategies, with the family promising a smooth transition of current operations.

stories.title: Martha Washington’s 1760 Letter About Daughter’s Illness Sells for $47,500, Joins Library of Congress
stories.summary: A personal letter from Martha Washington, describing her daughter's recovery, has found a new home at the Library of Congress. This 1760 correspondence, directed to Margaret Green, sheds light on Martha's motherhood journey and is the first handwritten piece by her in the library's archives. Its acquisition underscores women's vital roles during colonial America, adding depth alongside Mary Todd Lincoln's letters.

His campaign has succeeded in keeping over 8 million utensils out of landfills, while restaurants collectively saved more than $200,000 by making cutlery optional for takeaway. This initiative showcases how small changes can lead to significant environmental impact and financial savings, presenting a scalable model for communities seeking to tackle single-use plastics.

The family unearthed these extraordinary pieces while seeking expert advice, discovering they were part of a significant series illustrating the tale of Cyrus the Great. This auction underscores the remarkable rarity and cultural value of these Italian Renaissance treasures.

stories.title: Quebec home built from 200,000 recycled bottles, assembled in just three days

This technique employs panels crafted from recycled plastic bottles, resulting in a building process that took merely three days. By minimizing construction waste and cutting costs by approximately 35 percent, this initiative contributes significantly to affordable housing and environmental sustainability in Canada.

Published in the journal Antiquity, the study suggests that ancient Shu people used silk to wrap or cover objects during rituals. Researchers also identified red pigments and different weaving patterns, offering clues about ancient textile practices.

The honey has shown effectiveness against various bacterial and fungal pathogens, including difficult-to-treat strains. Findings suggest that sugarbag honey is comparable in strength to well-known medical-grade honeys. While propolis displayed selective antimicrobial activity, the reason for honey's potency remains unclear. Further research is needed to identify the beneficial compounds within the honey.

stories.title: Arkansas couple pays $8,000 for access to landlocked property, loses court battle with neighbours

The Arkansas Court of Appeals upheld a route along the neighbours' property boundary, despite concerns about construction costs and difficult terrain. One judge disagreed, warning that the approved route could be unusable without expensive work.

stories.summary: A 62-year-old German educator faces fraud charges after reportedly taking a 16-year sick leave, during which she allegedly collected over €248,000 in salary. Investigators believe she fabricated medical documentation to support her prolonged absence from the classroom. Although she engaged in scuba diving, there’s no evidence of her undertaking any other professional work. The court is currently reviewing the case to determine if a full trial is warranted.

stories.title: Israel election results: Neither Netanyahu nor oppn wins majority; what happens next?
stories.summary: Israel faces a political deadlock after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc fell short of the 61 seats needed for a majority.
